URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E6%9C%AC%E8%8D%89%E7%B6%B1%E7%9B%AE_(%E5%9B%9B%E5%BA%AB%E5%85%A8%E6%9B%B8%E6%9C%AC)/%E5%8D%B712%E4%B8%8B. Shennong Bencao Jing verbatim: 「丹參 味苦，微寒。主心腹邪氣，腸鳴幽幽如走水，寒熱積聚；破症除瘕，止煩滿，益氣。一名卻蟬草。」 with the Wu Pu variant readings 「神農、桐君、黃帝、雷公、扁鵲：苦，無毒；李氏：小寒。岐伯：咸。」 — 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan recension, YEAR 1799, https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E7%A5%9E%E8%BE%B2%E6%9C%AC%E8%8D%89%E7%B6%93_(%E5%AD%AB%E6%98%9F%E8%A1%8D). Read in the original Chinese.
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 上品, UPPER grade — BCGM tags it 「丹參 本經上品」 and the Sun Xingyan 1799 text places it in 卷一·上經. The upper grade is defined in that same text as the class taken to nourish life, non-toxic, safe for long and heavy use. Of the four Chinese herbs in this batch, Dan Shen and Ji Li are the only two carrying upper-grade status. This is directly load-bearing for any 'daily herb' recommendation and the DB has no column for it.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), from two pre-1900 sources: Li Shizhen 1596 — 「入手少隂厥隂之經心與包絡血分藥也」, hand-Shaoyin and hand-Jueyin, a Heart-and-Pericardium BLOOD-LEVEL medicine; Wu Yiluo 1757 — 「入心與包絡」. The DB's tcm_pattern_match already says Heart/Pericardium/Liver; the pre-1900 record supports Heart and Pericardium and does NOT name the Liver.

CONTRAINDICATIONS / INCOMPATIBILITIES, stated and specific: 徐之才 in BCGM — 「畏鹽水反藜蘆」, fears salt water, COUNTERACTS Li Lu (Veratrum, one of the classical eighteen antagonisms). Wu Yiluo 1757 extends it — 「畏鹹水。忌醋。反藜蘆。」, adding vinegar to the avoid-list. Wu Yiluo also gives a use-limit the DB lacks: 「虽能補血。長於行血。無瘀。斟酌用之。」 — though it supplements blood it excels at MOVING blood; where there is no stasis, use it only after deliberation.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom (本經): 「主心腹邪氣，腸鳴幽幽如走水，寒熱積聚；破症除瘕，止煩滿，益氣」 — evil qi in the heart and abdomen, borborygmus like water running, cold-and-heat accumulations, breaking zheng and removing jia masses. 別錄 adds 「養血去心腹痼疾結氣腰脊强脚痺除風邪留熱乆服利人」. 大明 adds a striking obstetric pair the DB omits: 「安生胎落死胎」 — it settles a LIVING fetus and expels a DEAD one. Wu Yiluo 1757 repeats this and adds the famous claim 「功兼四物」 / 「一味丹參散、功同四物湯」 — single-herb Dan Shen powder equals the whole Four Substances Decoction.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE from the pre-1900 附方: it is overwhelmingly given as a simple powder taken in WARM WINE (溫酒調下 / 熱酒調下), or decocted in wine (酒五升煑取三升) for 落胎下血; externally it is rendered into pork lard or sheep fat as an ointment (丹參摩膏; 猪膏二兩同煎七上七下) for infant fevers and for burns. The wine vehicle is doctrine, not incidental.

DISSENT TO SURFACE, not resolve: 微寒 (本經, BCGM head) vs 大寒 (李當之) vs 平 (甄權, Li Shizhen's own 發明, Wu Yiluo 1757) vs 性熱 (陶弘景's argument from the red-eye side effect). Four readings across 1,400 years. The DB currently shows one.

results.pre1900_finding: The stored 'Cold' is the Mingyi Bielu reading, not the head-reading, and the pre-1900 record is split four ways. BOTH primary sources give 平 NEUTRAL as the canonical assignment: Shennong Bencao Jing 味苦，平; BCGM 1596 根氣味苦平無毒. The 大寒 (greatly cold) is printed in BCGM as an explicit DISSENT attributed to the 名醫別錄. Alongside it stand 李當之：小溫 (slightly WARM) and 張元素：氣涼 (cool). Later practice did settle toward cold — Wu Yiluo 1757 writes 苦入心。寒勝熱 — but the DB is currently recording one voice out of four as if it were the record.
results.evidence: BCGM verbatim: 「根氣味苦平無毒」 with the attached note 「别録曰大寒普曰神農桐君雷公苦無毒李當之小温杲曰可升可降隂也好古曰氣寒味㣲苦而甘隂中㣲陽入手太隂血分元素曰氣凉味苦甘氣厚味薄浮而升陽中隂也入手少陽陽明經酒炒則上行之才曰山茱萸龍骨為之使惡葱實」 — 李時珍, 本草綱目, 卷十三 草之二 山草類下, entry 黄芩, marked 本經中品, YEAR 1596. URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E6%9C%AC%E8%8D%89%E7%B6%B1%E7%9B%AE_(%E5%9B%9B%E5%BA%AB%E5%85%A8%E6%9B%B8%E6%9C%AC)/%E5%8D%B713. Shennong Bencao Jing verbatim: 「黃芩 味苦，平。主諸熱黃膽，腸澼泄利，逐水，下血閉，惡創，恆蝕火瘍。一名腐腸。」 with the Wu Pu variants 「神農、桐君、黃帝、雷公、扁鵲：苦，無毒；李氏：小溫。」 — 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan recension, YEAR 1799, https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E7%A5%9E%E8%BE%B2%E6%9C%AC%E8%8D%89%E7%B6%93_(%E5%AD%AB%E6%98%9F%E8%A1%8D). Ben Cao Cong Xin 1757 verbatim: 「苦入心。寒勝熱。瀉中焦實火。除脾家溼熱。」 — 吳儀洛, 本草從新, https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E6%9C%AC%E8%8D%89%E5%BE%9E%E6%96%B0. Species is correct: 黃芩 is Scutellaria baicalensis, not S. lateriflora, which has no classical Chinese entry at all. Read in the original Chinese.
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 中品, MIDDLE grade — BCGM tags 「黄芩 本經中品」 and Sun Xingyan 1799 lists it under 上草，中品四十九種. Middle-grade herbs are the 'ministers', to be weighed for suitability and used to check disease, NOT the upper-grade daily-nourishing class. Material for a duration-of-use flag.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), and the sources disagree usefully: 王好古 — 「入手太隂血分」, hand-Taiyin (Lung), blood aspect; 張元素 — 「入手少陽陽明經」, hand-Shaoyang and Yangming; Li Shizhen's own synthesis, verbatim — 「黄芩能入手少隂陽明手足太隂少陽六經矣」, six channels. Wu Yiluo 1757: 「黃芩亦少陽藥也」.

PART DISCIPLINE — two drugs inside one entry, both pre-1900 and absent from the DB. Li Gao and Wu Yiluo distinguish 枯芩 / 片芩 (the old, hollow, floating root) from 子芩 / 條芩 (the new, solid, heavy root). Verbatim from BCGM: 「黄芩之中枯而飄者瀉肺火利氣消痰除風熱清肌表之熱細實而堅者瀉大腸火飬隂退陽補膀胱寒水」. Wu Yiluo 1757: 「中虚者名枯芩。即片芩。瀉肺火。清肌表之熱。內實者名条芩。即子芩。瀉大腸火。」 Hollow root drains LUNG fire and goes up; solid root drains LARGE INTESTINE fire and goes down. Also 「子主治腸澼膿血」 — the SEED is a separate drug for dysentery with pus and blood.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, and it is directional: 「酒炒則上行」 wine-frying makes it ascend; 「得酒上行得豬膽汁除肝膽火」 with pig-bile it drains Liver-Gallbladder fire; Wu Yiluo 1757 spells it out: 「上行酒炒。瀉肝胆火猪胆汁炒。」 Also 朱震亨 in BCGM: 「凡去上焦濕熱湏以酒洗過用」 — wash with wine before use for upper-burner damp-heat.

CONTRAINDICATIONS as stated classically, several, and sharp. Li Shizhen — 「若因飲寒受寒腹中痛及飲水心下悸小便不利而脉不數者是裏無熱證則黄芩不可用也」 — if the abdominal pain comes from drinking cold or contracting cold, and the pulse is not rapid, there is no interior heat pattern and Huang Qin MUST NOT be used. 朱震亨 — 「若肺虛者多用則傷肺必先以天門冬保定肺氣而後用之」. Wu Yiluo 1757 — 「苦寒傷胃。虚寒者。均宜戒。胎前若非實熱而服之。陰損胎元矣。」 — bitter cold injures the stomach, the deficient-cold must abstain, and in pregnancy, if the pattern is not excess heat, it covertly damages the fetal foundation. That last line directly qualifies the DB's 'settles a restless fetus (an tai)': the classical caveat is that it settles the fetus ONLY in heat patterns and harms it otherwise.

INCOMPATIBILITIES / SYNERGIES from 徐之才 and Li Shizhen: 「山茱萸龍骨為之使惡葱實…得厚朴黄連止腹痛得五味子牡蠣令人有子得黄茋白歛赤小豆療鼠瘻…得柴胡退寒熱得芍藥治下痢得桑白皮瀉肺火得白术安胎」. Wu Yiluo adds 「畏丹皮、丹砂」. These paired-herb rules are a whole class of classical information the DB has no field for.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom (本經): 「主諸熱黃疸腸澼洩痢逐水下血閉惡瘡疽蝕火瘍」. The alias 腐腸 ('rotted intestine') is explained by Tao Hongjing as descriptive of the hollow old root, not of its action — worth knowing before it gets mistranslated onto a label.

results.stored_temperature: Cool (Ayurvedic sheeta virya used as anchor; Chinese tradition noted as slightly Warm)
results.pre1900_finding: The Ayurvedic anchor is confirmed by two pre-1900 sources that both use the word COOLING. But the DB understates the Chinese side: it says 'slightly Warm', whereas THREE pre-1900 Chinese sources give plain 溫 warm, and the Shennong Bencao Jing puts it in the UPPER grade with 味苦，溫. Ma Zhi's note in BCGM is an explicit argument FOR the warm reading against the alternatives. So the cross-tradition split is wider than the DB records: sita/cooling in India, 溫 warm in China, on the same fruit.
results.evidence: INDIAN, verbatim: "The entire plant but more particularly the fruits are used in medicine. They are regarded as cooling, diuretic, tonic and aphrodisiac and are used in painful micturition, calculous affections, urinary disorders and impotence." — Udoy Chand Dutt, The Materia Medica of the Hindus, p. 125, YEAR 1877, https://archive.org/details/materiamedicaofh00duttuoft. Corroborated verbatim: "The Hindus use the fruit and root; they regard them as having Cooling, diuretic, tonic and aphrodisiac properties, and use them in gonorrhoea and dysuria." — Dymock, Warden & Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica, Vol. I, p. 243, YEAR 1890, https://archive.org/details/b21960343_0001. CHINESE, verbatim: 「氣味苦温無毒」 with the note 「别錄曰辛微温權曰甘有小毒志曰其性宣通久服不冷而無壅熱當以性温為是之才曰烏頭為之使」 — 李時珍, 本草綱目, 卷十六 草之五 隰草類下, entry 蒺蔾, marked 本經上品, YEAR 1596, https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E6%9C%AC%E8%8D%89%E7%B6%B1%E7%9B%AE_(%E5%9B%9B%E5%BA%AB%E5%85%A8%E6%9B%B8%E6%9C%AC)/%E5%8D%B716. And 「蒺藜子 味苦，溫。主惡血，破症結積聚，喉痹，乳難。久服，長肌肉，明目、輕身。」 — 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan recension, YEAR 1799. And 「刺蒺藜…辛苦而溫。散肝風而瀉肺氣。勝溼破血。催生堕胎。」 — 吳儀洛, 本草從新, YEAR 1757.
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 上品, UPPER grade — BCGM tags 「蒺蔾 本經上品」 and Sun Xingyan 1799 places 蒺藜子 in 卷一·上經. The Chinese tradition explicitly licenses long-term daily use, and prints a regimen to prove it: 「服食法…每服二錢新汲水調下日三服…服之一年以後冬不寒夏不熱二年老者復少髮白復黒齒落更生服之三年身輕長生 神仙秘㫖」.

THE WARM READING IS ARGUED, NOT ASSUMED. Ma Zhi's note in BCGM, verbatim: 「其性宣通久服不冷而無壅熱當以性温為是」 — its nature disperses and frees; long use is neither cold-producing nor heat-obstructing, therefore the WARM reading is the correct one. That is a pre-1900 author explicitly adjudicating this herb's temperature, and it lands opposite to the DB's anchor. Surface it; do not let the Ayurvedic anchor silently overwrite it.

PART / SPECIES DISCIPLINE — a hard trap the DB does not carry. BCGM 1596 separates 刺蒺藜 / 杜蒺藜 (the true spiny Tribulus terrestris) from 白蒺藜 / 沙苑蒺藜, which Li Shizhen describes as a kidney-day-lily-seed-shaped legume from Tongzhou (今人謂之沙苑蒺藜) — that is ASTRAGALUS COMPLANATUS, a different plant with its own reading 「白蒺䔧氣味甘温無毒主治補腎治腰痛泄精虚損勞乏」. Wu Yiluo 1757 keeps them as two separate entries (刺蒺藜 vs 沙苑蒺藜 苦溫). Kou Zongshi's warning, verbatim: 「補腎藥今人多用風家惟用刺蒺䔧也」. Almost all of the DB's kidney/reproductive-tonic language belongs to the ASTRAGALUS drug, not to Tribulus. This needs founder review.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, mandatory: 雷斆 — 「凡使揀浮蒸之從午至酉日乾木臼舂令刺盡用酒拌…蒸從午至酉日乾用」 (steam from the wu to the you double-hour, sun-dry, pound in a WOODEN mortar until every spine is gone, mix with wine and steam again); 大明 — 「入藥不計丸散並炒去刺用」 (whether pill or powder, dry-fry and remove the spines). The spines must be removed; this is not optional in 1596.

CONTRAINDICATION, unambiguous and absent from the DB: 大明 in BCGM lists 「催生墮胎」 among its actions, and Wu Yiluo 1757 repeats 「催生堕胎」 — it hastens delivery and CAUSES MISCARRIAGE. Dutt 1877's own formulary uses it that way: 「Take of the entire plant of Tribulus terrestris… [given] in painful micturition, suppression of urine, bloody urine]」 alongside a Sanskrit prescription pairing gokshura with vacha for '催生下衣' equivalents in the Chinese附方 (蒺䔧子貝母各四兩為末米湯服三錢, for difficult labour, retained placenta and dead fetus). Contraindicated in pregnancy on pre-1900 authority.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经): NOT stated in the BCGM entry. Wu Yiluo 1757 gives an organ target rather than a channel — 「散肝風而瀉肺氣」, disperses Liver wind and drains Lung qi. Record what is there; do not invent a 归经 for this one.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom (本經): 「主惡血，破症結積聚，喉痹，乳難。久服，長肌肉，明目、輕身」 — malign blood, breaking masses, throat closure, difficult lactation; with long use, builds flesh, brightens the eyes, lightens the body. 別錄 adds 「身體風癢頭痛欬逆傷肺肺痿止煩下氣小兒頭瘡癰腫」. Note that EYE indications and WIND-ITCH dominate the Chinese record, and lactation difficulty appears in the very first line of the 200 CE text — none of which is in the DB's Ayurvedic-led framing.

VIPAKA and GUNA: not stated in Dutt 1877, Ainslie 1826, Dymock 1890 or Watt. The DB's 'sweet post-digestive effect' and 'unctuous quality' have no pre-1900 warrant I could find. Ainslie 1826 records only 'pleasant-smelling and sweetish-tasted leaves… said by the native practitioners to possess diuretic qualities' (Materia Indica Vol. II, p. 247).

results.pre1900_finding: Confirmed by two independent pre-1900 sources that use the explicit thermal word COOLING, both compiling directly from Sanskrit medical works, and the second naming its classical authority (Chakradatta, 11th c.). Species is correct and unambiguous — both sources head the entry TERMINALIA ARJUNA, Bedd., Sanskrit अर्जुन Arjuna / ककुभ Kukubha, and both name the STEM BARK, matching the DB's part_used.
results.evidence: Verbatim: "THE bark of this timber tree is considered tonic, astringent and cooling, and is used in heart diseases, contusions, fractures, ulcers, etc." — Udoy Chand Dutt, The Materia Medica of the Hindus, Compiled from Sanskrit Medical Works, entry TERMINALIA ARJUNA, Bedd. (Sans. Arjuna, Kakubha), p. 163, YEAR 1877. URL: https://archive.org/details/materiamedicaofh00duttuoft. Independently, verbatim: "This tree is the Arjuna and Kukubha of Chakradatta, who describes it as tonic, astringent, and cooling, and prescribes it in heart disease and for those purposes for which astringents are generally applied." — Dymock, Warden & Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica, Vol. II, Combretaceae, p. 11, YEAR 1891. URL: https://archive.org/details/b21960343_0002.
additions: PREPARATION AND VEHICLE DOCTRINE, explicit in both sources and absent from the DB. Dymock 1891, verbatim: "He recommends it to be given in milk, treacle or water when used internally, or as a ghrita (medicinal butter), made with the decoction and powder of the bark." Dutt 1877, verbatim: "a decoction of the bark with milk is given as a nourishment. The powdered bark is given with milk, treacle or water. A ghrita is prepared with the decoction and paste of the bark for internal use." MILK is the classical vehicle for the cardiac indication — this is doctrine, not garnish, and it is the single most quotable practical detail for a monograph.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the sources' own idiom, in the classical order: heart disease FIRST, then contusions, fractures, ulcers and chancres. Dutt 1877, verbatim: "In fractures and contusions with extensive ecchymosis, powdered arjuna bark is recommended to be taken internally with milk. A decoction of the bark is used as a wash in ulcers and chancres." So there are two routes, internal in milk and external as a wash, and the DB records neither.

A CLASSICAL PROPERTY-TERM the DB has no field for, with its rationale: Dymock 1891, verbatim — "It is considered to be Asmari-hara, or lithontriptic, and a reference to the chemical composition will show that the ash of the bark contains an extraordinarily large proportion of calcium carbonate." अश्मरीहर asmari-hara = stone-destroying. Dymock's own analysis puts the ash at 34% near-pure calcium carbonate. A pre-1900 property term, a pre-1900 chemical rationale, and a fourth indication class (urinary calculi).

CLASSICAL BONE-KNITTING CLAIM, stated as a distinct doctrine: Dymock 1891, verbatim — "Hindu physicians think that the bark has some special virtue in promoting the union of fractures, and the dispersion of ecchymosis when given internally." This is not the same as 'astringent'; it is a named specific virtue.

A CLASSICAL PAIRING the DB does not record: arjuna bark is a constituent of Dutt's Gokshuradya avaleha, an electuary built on Tribulus terrestris — 'bark of Terminalia Arjuna… sixteen tolas' — given for painful micturition, suppression of urine, bloody urine and calculous affections (Dutt 1877, p. 126). Arjuna and Gokshura, both in this batch, are formulary partners in the pre-1900 record.

VIPAKA and GUNA: not stated in Dutt 1877, Dymock 1885, Dymock 1891 or Watt. Do not fill in. The DB's ayurvedic_dosha_match 'Kapha, Pitta' has no pre-1900 textual warrant that I located; the pre-1900 sources give only rasa (astringent, kashaya) and virya (cooling).

CHINESE CORRESPONDENCE: correctly flagged in the DB as non-classical. There is no Terminalia arjuna entry in the Bencao Gangmu or the Shennong Bencao Jing, and therefore no 归经 and no Shennong grade. The tcm_pattern_match must stay labelled as a functional analogy, which it currently is — that labelling is right and should be preserved.

results.herb: Musta / Nut Grass / Xiang Fu (Cyperus rotundus)
results.stored_temperature: Cool (Ayurvedic virya: sheeta/cold; the row's note claims "the Chinese tradition instead classes it as neutral")
results.pre1900_finding: The Ayurvedic half of the stored value is CONFIRMED verbatim: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu reads मुस्तं कटु हिमं — Musta is pungent and COLD (hima = sita virya). The Chinese half is WRONG AS STATED: the Bencao Gangmu head line is 氣味甘微寒無毒 (sweet, SLIGHTLY COLD, non-toxic), not neutral. "Neutral" is Li Shizhen's own dissenting gloss (辛微苦甘平) and Wang Ang's 1694 head reading (性平), not the tradition's assignment. Both readings are pre-1900; the row presents one as if it were the whole Chinese position.
results.source_year: 16th c. (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, c. 1550–1590); 1596 (Bencao Gangmu)
results.evidence:
Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Bhava Mishra, 16th c.), Haritakyadi Varga vv.92–94, Sanskrit original: 「मुस्तकं न स्त्रियां मुस्तं त्रिषु वारिदनामकम् ... भद्र मुस्तञ्च गुन्द्रा च तथा नागरमुस्तकः / मुस्तं कटु हिमं ग्राहि तिक्तं दीपनपाचनम् ९३ / कषायं कफपित्तास्रतृड्ज्वरारुचिजन्तुहृत् / अनूपदेशे यज्जातं मुस्तकं तत्प्रशस्यते / तत्रापि मुनिभिः प्रोक्तं वरं नागरमुस्तकम् ९४」 — https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/भावप्रकाशः/पूर्वखण्डे_भावप्रकाशनिघण्टुः (Sanskrit original-language transcription; the digital text follows the Brahmashankar Mishra printed edition — no translation layer, but flagging the edition honestly).

Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (1596), 卷十四 草部芳草類, entry 「莎草香附子」 {{别錄中品}}: 「氣味甘微寒無毒」 with the attached notes: 「宗奭曰苦　頌曰天寳單方云辛微寒無毒性濇　元素曰甘苦微寒氣厚於味陽中之隂血中之氣藥也　時珍曰辛微苦甘平足厥隂手少陽藥也能兼行十二經八脈氣分得童子小便醋芎藭蒼术良」 — Siku Quanshu recension, https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷14 (traditional characters, unabridged).

Corroboration on the neutral line, Wu Yiluo, 本草從新 (1757), 香附: 「氣香。味辛能散，微苦能降，微甘能和。乃血中氣藥。通行十二經八脉氣分。」 (no explicit thermal quality given) — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新 . Wang Ang, 本草備要 (1694), 香附: 「性平氣香」 (LOCATE-ONLY: that Wikisource transcription is simplified with dropped glyphs and must not be quoted as the 1694 text).

NEGATIVE RESULT worth recording: neither pre-1900 Indian English-language authority supplies a virya. U. C. Dutt, Materia Medica of the Hindus (1877), p.264, Cyperus rotundus / Mustaka: "They are considered diaphoretic, astringent, stomachic and useful in fever, diarrhoea and dyspepsia" — https://archive.org/details/materiamedicaofh00duttuoft . Dymock, Warden & Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica vol. III (1893), pp.552–553: "This is the Mustaka of Sanskrit writers; it is considered to be diuretic, diaphoretic, astringent, and stomachic" — https://archive.org/details/pharmacographia03dymogoog . Ainslie, Materia Indica (1826), art. CXLIX, is likewise action-words only. All action words, no temperature. The cold reading rests on the Sanskrit verse alone.
additions: SHENNONG GRADE — absent, and that matters. Xiang Fu is NOT in the Shennong Bencao Jing at all. Li Shizhen tags the entry 「别錄中品」 — Mingyi Bielu, MIDDLE grade. The Shennong middle-grade rubric (Sun Xingyan recension 1799, 卷二·中經) reads: 「中藥一百二十種為臣，主養性以應人。無毒、有毒，斟酌其宜。」 — ministers, for nourishing the nature, some toxic and some not, to be weighed for fitness. That is not the unrestricted daily-use class. For a product recommending daily herbs, Xiang Fu should not sit in the same duration tier as an 上品 herb.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经) — 足厥陰 (Liver) and 手少陽 (Sanjiao/Triple Burner), plus an unusually broad reach: 「時珍曰辛微苦甘平足厥隂手少陽藥也能兼行十二經八脈氣分」 (BCGM 1596). Wu Yiluo repeats it in 1757: 「通行十二經八脉氣分」 — it moves the QI DIVISION of all twelve channels and the eight extraordinary vessels. The DB's tcm_pattern_match names Liver qi stagnation correctly but carries no channel column; this is the classical warrant for the 'commander of qi' language.

AYURVEDIC RASA — confirmed exactly as stored: कटु (pungent), तिक्त (bitter), कषाय (astringent). HONEST GAP: the Bhavaprakasha verse gives NO vipaka and NO guna for Musta. It gives ग्राही (grahi, absorbent/binding) and दीपनपाचन (kindles and cooks), which are actions, not guna. Do not let anyone backfill a vipaka here.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, Indian idiom (BPN 16th c.): 「कफपित्तास्रतृड्ज्वरारुचिजन्तुहृत्」 — removes kapha, PITTA, asra (blood/rakta disorders), thirst, fever, anorexia and worms. Note it removes pitta, which is internally consistent with the cold virya and supports the row's Kapha+Pitta dosha match.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, Chinese idiom (別錄, quoted in BCGM 1596): 「除胸中熱充皮毛久服令人益氣長鬚眉」 — clears heat in the chest, fills out skin and hair, and with prolonged use boosts qi and grows the beard and eyebrows. Also 蘇頌: 「治心腹中客熱膀胱間連脇下氣妨常日憂愁不樂心忪少氣」 — habitual sorrow and joylessness, palpitation and shortness of breath. That emotional framing is older and richer than the DB's summary.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, and it is strict. Lei Xiao (via BCGM 1596): 「凡采得隂乾於石臼中搗之切忌鐵器」 — shade-dry and pound in a STONE mortar; IRON IMPLEMENTS ARE STRICTLY FORBIDDEN. Li Shizhen: 「凡采得連苗暴乾以火燎去苗及毛用時以水洗淨石上磨去皮用童子小便浸透洗晒搗用或生或炒或以酒醋鹽水浸諸法各從本方」 — singe off the sprout and hairs, grind off the skin on stone, steep through with boys' urine; then raw, or dry-fried, or steeped in wine, vinegar or salt water, each according to the formula. And 「又稻草煑之味不苦」 — boiled with rice straw it loses its bitterness. Synergists: 「得童子小便醋芎藭蒼术良」.

SOURCING DOCTRINE — BPN v.94: 「अनूपदेशे यज्जातं मुस्तकं तत्प्रशस्यते / तत्रापि मुनिभिः प्रोक्तं वरं नागरमुस्तकम्」 — that grown in marshy (anupa) ground is the praised material, and among these the sages declared Nagara-musta best. Dutt 1877 says the same in English: "Those growing in moist soil are preferred for use."

SPECIES / ADULTERATION — Dutt 1877 records a second drug, Nagaramustaka, which he assigns to Cyperus pertenuis Roxb.; his editor George King notes it "can hardly be maintained as a species; it is a variety of the C. rotundus of Linnaeus." Dymock 1893 instead assigns Nagar-motha to Cyperus scariosus R.Br. and says Arabian and Persian writers rate it INFERIOR to C. rotundus — the exact opposite of the Bhavaprakasha's ranking. Two pre-1900 traditions disagree about which Cyperus is better; the DB should not silently pick one. Separately, BCGM 1596 warns of trade substitution in the other direction: 「今人乃妄以鳬茈香附子為之」 — Xiang Fu being passed off as San Leng.

CONTRAINDICATIONS — HONEST GAP. Neither the BCGM 1596 entry nor the Bhavaprakasha verse states a contraindication for Musta/Xiang Fu. Do not manufacture one. The only adjacent classical caution is Zhang Yuansu's on the neighbouring 三稜 entry (「能瀉真氣真氣虚者勿用」), which belongs to San Leng, not Xiang Fu, and must not be carried across.

The stored 'cool bordering cold' is an accurate rendering of 微寒. This also REPLACES the row's current primary citation, Grieve's A Modern Herbal (1931), which is forbidden under the pre-1900 rule.
results.evidence:
Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (1596), 卷三十二 果部之四 味類, entry 「茗」{{唐本草}}: 「葉氣味苦甘㣲寒無毒」 with notes: 「藏器曰苦寒久食令人痩去人脂使人不睡飲之宜熱冷則聚痰　胡洽曰與榧同食令人身重　李廷飛曰大渴及酒後飲茶水入腎經令人腰脚膀胱冷痛兼患水腫攣痺諸疾大抵飲茶宜熱宜少不飲尤佳空腹最忌　時珍曰服威靈仙土茯苓者忌飲茶」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷32 (Siku Quanshu recension, traditional characters).

Wu Yiluo, 本草從新 (1757), 茶: 「苦甘微寒。下氣消食。去痰熱，除煩渴，清頭目。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新 (note: this Wikisource transcription carries mixed simplified glyphs, so it is corroborating, not the citation of record).
additions: SHENNONG GRADE — NONE, and this is a substantive finding. Tea has no Shennong grade because it is not in the Shennong Bencao Jing. Li Shizhen tags the 茗 entry 「唐本草」 (Tang Ben Cao, 659 CE) with 「校正…自木部移入此」. The Sun Xingyan 1799 recension of the Shennong Bencao Jing mentions 茗 only inside the 苦菜 entry's philological note, where Tao Hongjing identified 苦菜 with tea and the Tang commentators rejected the identification: 「《唐本》注駁之，非矣」. So there is NO Han-dynasty duration ruling for tea. Any 'safe for daily use because it is an upper-grade herb' claim would be false here.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经) — 手足厥陰, hand and foot JUEYIN (Pericardium and Liver): 「好古曰茗茶氣寒味苦入手足厥隂經」 (Wang Haogu, quoted BCGM 1596). This is materially different from what a modern monograph would say (Heart/Lung/Stomach/Bladder). Direction of action: 「其體下行」 and 「沉也降也最能降火」 — its body descends; it sinks and descends and is supremely able to bring fire down.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — a temperature-management rule, not a processing rule: 「飲之宜熱冷則聚痰」 (Chen Cangqi) — it should be drunk HOT; drunk cold it gathers phlegm. And Li Tingfei: 「大抵飲茶宜熱宜少不飲尤佳空腹最忌」 — in general drink it hot, drink it little, better still not at all, and on an empty stomach it is most forbidden. Li Shizhen restates the mechanism: 「温飲則火因寒氣而下降熱飲則茶借火氣而升散」.

CONTRAINDICATIONS, classically stated, and there are five distinct ones the DB has no field for. (1) Long use: 「苦寒久食令人痩去人脂使人不睡」 — prolonged use emaciates, strips the body's fat, prevents sleep. (2) FOOD INCOMPATIBILITY: 「與榧同食令人身重」 — with torreya nuts it makes the body heavy. (3) After thirst or wine: 「大渴及酒後飲茶水入腎經令人腰脚膀胱冷痛兼患水腫攣痺諸疾」 — the water enters the Kidney channel and causes cold pain in loin, legs and bladder, plus edema and cramping. (4) HERB–HERB INTERACTION: 「時珍曰服威靈仙土茯苓者忌飲茶」 — those taking Wei Ling Xian (Clematis) or Tu Fu Ling (Smilax) must not drink tea. (5) Constitution: 「若虚寒及血弱之人飲之既久則脾胃惡寒元氣暗損土不制水精血潛虚成痰飲成痞脹成痿痺成黄痩成嘔逆成洞瀉成腹痛成疝瘕種種内傷」 — in deficient-cold or blood-weak people, sustained drinking silently damages the yuan qi. Li Shizhen gives his own case history: 「時珍早年盛氣毎飲新茗必至數椀輕汗發而肌骨清頗覺痛快中年胃氣稍損飲之即覺為害不痞悶嘔惡即腹冷洞泄」 — a first-person report of the same herb turning harmful as constitution changed. That is exactly the nuance a personalized recommender needs and it is entirely absent from the row.

TERROIR EXCEPTION TO THE TEMPERATURE — 「真茶性冷惟雅州䝉山出者温而主疾」 (Su Song, quoted BCGM 1596): true tea is COLD in nature; only that from Mengshan in Yazhou is WARM and treats disease. A pre-1900 source explicitly states that one origin inverts the thermal assignment. Worth flagging next to any single stored value.

CLASSICAL SYNERGY — the ginger–tea pairing, given as an explicit thermal-balancing device: 「薑茶治痢薑助陽茶助隂並能消暑解酒食毒且一寒一熱調平隂陽不問赤白冷熱用之皆良生薑細切與真茶等分新水濃煎服之」 (Yang Shiying, quoted BCGM 1596; repeated in BCCX 1757 as 薑茶飲). A ready-made classical formula for pairing a cold herb the DB already stocks.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, source idiom: 「主治瘻瘡利小便去痰熱止渴令人少睡有力悅志」 (神農食經, quoted BCGM) — fistulous sores, promotes urination, removes phlegm-heat, stops thirst, reduces sleep, gives strength and GLADDENS THE WILL. Plus 「清頭目治中風昬憒多睡不醒」 (Wang Haogu) and 「濃煎吐風熱痰涎」 (Li Shizhen — strongly decocted it induces vomiting of wind-heat phlegm; note this emetic use is a dose-dependent effect the DB does not carry).

results.herb: Moringa / Shigru / Drumstick (Moringa oleifera Lam., = M. pterygosperma Gaertn. in pre-1900 sources)
results.pre1900_finding: उष्ण — HOT, and sharp with it. Bhavaprakasha Nighantu: शिग्रुः कटुः कटुः पाके तीक्ष्णोष्णो मधुरो लघुः — Shigru is pungent, PUNGENT IN VIPAKA, sharp-and-HOT, sweet, light. Independently corroborated on the Unani side by Dymock 1890 for the flowers: 'hot and dry'. The stored 'Warm' is confirmed and, if anything, understated — the Sanskrit says ushna (hot), not merely warm. This replaces the row's current primary citation, Grieve 1931, and its secondary, the modern Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia — both forbidden.
results.source_year: 16th c. (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, c. 1550–1590); corroborated 1890 (Dymock)
results.evidence:
Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Bhava Mishra, 16th c.), Guduchyadi Varga vv.105–110, Sanskrit original: 「शोभाञ्जनः शिग्रुतीक्ष्णगन्धकाक्षीवमोचकाः / तद्बीजं श्वेतमरिचंमधुशिग्रुः सलोहितः / शिग्रुः कटुः कटुः पाके तीक्ष्णोष्णो मधुरो लघुः १०५ / दीपनो रोचनो रूक्षः क्षारस्तिक्तो विदाहकृत् / संग्राही शुक्रलो हृद्यः पित्तरक्तप्रकोपणः १०६ / चक्षुष्यः कफवातघ्नो विद्र धिश्वयथुक्रिमीन् / मेदोऽपचीविषप्लीहगुल्मगण्डव्रणान्हरेत् १०७ / श्वेतः प्रोक्तगुणो ज्ञेयो विशेषाद्दाहकृद्भवेत् ... मधुशिग्रुः प्रोक्तगुणो विशेषाद्दीपनः सरः १०८ / शिग्रुवल्कलपत्राणां स्वरसः परमार्त्तिहृत् १०९ / चक्षुष्यं शिग्रुजं बीजं तीक्ष्णोष्णं विषनाशनम् / अवृष्यं कफवातघ्नं तन्नस्येन शिरोऽत्तिनुत् ४.११०」 — https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/भावप्रकाशः/पूर्वखण्डे_भावप्रकाशनिघण्टुः (Sanskrit original-language transcription).

Dymock, Warden & Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica, vol. I (1890), p.897, Moringa pterygosperma: "Mahometan writers describe Sahjna flowers as hot and dry, and consider that they expel cold humours, disperse swellings, act as a tonic and diuretic, and increase the flow of bile." (Verified identical in two independent scans, pharmacographia00dymogoog and pharmacographia00hoopgoog.) — https://archive.org/details/pharmacographia00dymogoog

U. C. Dutt, Materia Medica of the Hindus (1877), pp.117–118: "The root is described as acrid, pungent, stimulant and diuretic. Applied externally it acts as a rubefacient. The seeds are described as acrid and pungent... The Bhavaprakasa describes two varieties of sobhanjana, namely, white and red. The root of the white variety is said to be a stronger rubefacient, while that of the red, is preferred for internal use" — https://archive.org/details/materiamedicaofh00duttuoft (action words only; carries no virya, so it corroborates the character but not the temperature).
additions: VIPAKA — कटुः पाके, KATU VIPAKA (pungent post-digestive effect). This is the founder's named target and the Bhavaprakasha states it explicitly, in the same half-line as the virya. The DB has no vipaka column at all.

GUNA — three of them, explicitly: लघुः (laghu, LIGHT), रूक्षः (ruksha, DRY), तीक्ष्ण (tikshna, SHARP/penetrating). The row's stored moisture 'Dry' is therefore CONFIRMED by the Sanskrit rather than inferred. Add laghu and tikshna, which the row lacks.

DOSHA — कफवातघ्नो, destroys kapha and vata: the row's 'Kapha primarily, also settles Vata' is confirmed word for word. BUT the same verse says पित्तरक्तप्रकोपणः — it AGGRAVATES PITTA AND RAKTA (blood) — and विदाहकृत् — it causes burning. The row carries NO pitta caution. For a hot, sharp, pitta-provoking herb being fed to a recommender, that omission is a safety gap, not a nuance. The white variety is singled out as worse: 「श्वेतः प्रोक्तगुणो ज्ञेयो विशेषाद्दाहकृद्भवेत्」 — the white one is ESPECIALLY burning-producing.

RASA — the Bhavaprakasha gives a wider set than the row: कटु (pungent), मधुर (SWEET), तिक्त (bitter), क्षार (ALKALINE/kshara), plus संग्राही (binding). The row stores 'Pungent, Bitter; mildly Astringent'. Sweet and alkaline are missing; and the classical term is संग्राही (grahi, absorbent), which is not the same as कषाय (kashaya, astringent rasa).

PART DISCIPLINE — the row stores LEAF, but the classical record is mostly about the root, bark and seed, and the parts diverge sharply. The virya in v.105 attaches to शिग्रु as a drug. The only verse naming leaves is v.109: 「शिग्रुवल्कलपत्राणां स्वरसः परमार्त्तिहृत्」 — the fresh juice of the BARK AND LEAVES is supremely pain-relieving. The SEED gets its own separate reading in v.110: 「चक्षुष्यं शिग्रुजं बीजं तीक्ष्णोष्णं विषनाशनम् / अवृष्यं कफवातघ्नं」 — also sharp-hot, but अवृष्य (NOT aphrodisiac), which directly contradicts the whole-drug शुक्रल (semen-promoting) two verses earlier. So a leaf monograph cannot silently inherit every property of the head reading. This is the same structural trap the project already hit on Gou Qi Zi.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, Indian idiom: 「दीपनो रोचनो」 (kindles the digestive fire, restores relish for food), 「हृद्यः」 (good for the heart), 「चक्षुष्यः」 (good for the eyes), and it removes 「विद्रधि श्वयथु क्रिमीन् मेदः अपची विष प्लीहा गुल्म गण्ड व्रणान्」 — deep abscess, swelling, worms, MEDAS (fat/adipose tissue), scrofula, poison, enlarged spleen, gulma, goitre and ulcers. The medas indication is the classical warrant for any weight/metabolic framing and it is right there in the 16th-century verse.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — nasya: 「तन्नस्येन शिरोऽत्तिनुत्」, the seed given as nasal instillation cures headache (BPN v.110). Dutt 1877 p.118 records the compound: seeds + rock salt + mustard + putchuk, ground with goat's urine and dried, 'used as a snuff for rousing comatose or drowsy persons'; and the fresh root-bark juice poured into the ear for otalgia, or the gum with sesamum oil for the same. Dymock 1890 p.897 adds the gum 'rubbed with milk and applied in headache to the temples'.

CONTRAINDICATION IN PREGNANCY — now has a pre-1900 basis, which the row previously supported only with modern reviews. Dymock, Pharmacographia Indica I (1890), p.897: "Rumphius and Loureiro state that the bark is emmenagogue and even abortifacient. In Bengal half-ounce doses of the bark are said to be used to procure abortion." That is bark-specific and confirms the row's existing bark/root/flower pregnancy caution.

VARIETY DOCTRINE — the row treats Moringa as one drug; the Bhavaprakasha names three: श्वेत (white), लोहित/रक्त (red), and मधुशिग्रु. Same base properties, but 'the white is especially burning', and 「मधुशिग्रुः प्रोक्तगुणो विशेषाद्दीपनः सरः」 — Madhushigru is especially digestive-kindling and मोबाइल/laxative (sara). Dutt 1877 adds the clinical split: white root the stronger rubefacient, red root preferred for internal use. Dymock 1890 speculates the red is Moringa concanensis Nimmo — a DIFFERENT SPECIES, so the red-variety statements may not belong to M. oleifera at all.
SHENNONG GRADE — not applicable. Moringa has no Chinese materia medica entry in the sources consulted; there is nothing to import.

results.pre1900_finding: 寒 — cold, in the oldest layer, and 大寒 (greatly cold) in the Mingyi Bielu. Shennong Bencao Jing: 大黃 味苦，寒。 Bencao Gangmu 1596: 氣味苦寒無毒, with 别錄曰大寒. Ben Cao Cong Xin 1757 intensifies it to 大苦大寒. Every pre-1900 source agrees; the only dissent is Li Dangzhi's 小寒 (slightly cold), which is still cold. Stored value stands unchanged.
results.source_year: 1799 (Sun Xingyan recension of the c. 200 CE Shennong Bencao Jing); 1596 (Bencao Gangmu)
results.evidence:
Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan & Sun Fengyi recension (1799), 卷三·下經: 「==大黃== 味苦，寒。主下瘀血、血閉、寒熱，破症瘕積聚，留飲宿食，蕩滌腸胃，推陳致新，通利水殺（《御覽》，此下有道字），調中化食，安和五臟，生山谷。《吳普》曰：大黃，一名黃良，一名火參，一名膚如，神農、雷公：苦，有毒；扁鵲：苦，無毒；李氏：小寒，為中將軍。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) (traditional characters, attributable 1799 recension, preserving the Wu Pu variant readings).

Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (1596), 卷十七上 草部毒草類, 「大黄」{{本經下品}}: 「氣味苦寒無毒」 with notes: 「别錄曰大寒　普曰神農雷公苦有毒扁鵲苦無毒李當之大寒　元素曰味苦氣寒氣味俱厚沈而降隂也用之須酒浸煨熟者寒因熟用…時珍曰凡病在氣分及胃寒血虚并姙娠産後並勿輕用其性苦寒能傷元氣耗隂血故也　之才曰黄芩為之使無所畏　權曰忌冷水惡乾漆」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷17上

Wu Yiluo, 本草從新 (1757), 大黃: 「大苦大寒。入足太陰（脾）、手足陽明、厥陰（大腸、胃、心包、肝。）血分。其性沉而不浮。其用走而不守。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: SHENNONG GRADE — 下品, LOWER GRADE, and this is the single most product-relevant fact in the whole batch. The Sun Xingyan 1799 recension heads 卷三·下經 with: 「下藥，一百二十五種，為左使。主治病以應地。多毒，不可久服。欲除寒熱邪氣，破積聚，愈疾者，本下經。」 — lower drugs are the assistants; they TREAT DISEASE; many are toxic; THEY MUST NOT BE TAKEN FOR LONG. Li Shizhen tags the entry 「本經下品」 and files it under 毒草類 (the TOXIC herbs section). Da Huang is explicitly excluded by the founding classic from the daily/long-term tier. Anything in the product that could route a user toward habitual use needs to hard-stop on this.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经) — five channels, blood division: 「時珍曰大黄乃足太隂手足陽明手足厥隂五經血分之藥凡病在五經血分者宜用之若在氣分用之是謂誅伐無過」 (BCGM 1596) — foot taiyin, hand-and-foot yangming, hand-and-foot jueyin. Wu Yiluo 1757 names the organs: 「入足太陰（脾）、手足陽明、厥陰（大腸、胃、心包、肝。）血分」 — Spleen, Large Intestine, Stomach, Pericardium, Liver. The row's tcm_pattern_match already lists exactly these organs; it now has a pre-1900 anchor. Li Shizhen adds a decision rule the row lacks: if the disease is in the QI division rather than the blood division, using Da Huang is 「誅伐無過」 — punishing the innocent.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — the most elaborate in the batch, and it changes where the herb acts. Zhang Yuansu: 「用之須酒浸煨熟者寒因熟用酒浸入太陽經酒洗入陽明經餘經不用酒」 — wine-SOAKED it enters the taiyang channel, wine-WASHED it enters the yangming; for other channels use no wine. Li Gao: 「大黄苦峻下走用之于下必生用若邪氣在上非酒不至必用酒浸引上至高之分驅熱而下如物在高巔必射以取之也若用生者則遺至高之邪熱是以愈後或目赤或㗋痺或頭腫或膈上熱疾生也」 — to purge downward use it RAW; to reach heat in the upper body it MUST be wine-steeped, or the upper heat is left behind and the patient develops red eyes, throat closure, head swelling or diaphragmatic heat after apparent recovery. Wu Yiluo 1757 shows Zhang Zhongjing grading this across three formulas: 調胃承氣湯 wine-soaked, 大承氣湯 wine-washed, 小承氣湯 no wine at all. The row's part_used says nothing about processing; this is a whole doctrine.

CONTRAINDICATIONS, classically stated: 「時珍曰凡病在氣分及胃寒血虚并姙娠産後並勿輕用其性苦寒能傷元氣耗隂血故也」 (BCGM 1596) — qi-division disease, COLD STOMACH, BLOOD DEFICIENCY, PREGNANCY and POSTPARTUM: do not use lightly, because bitter-cold injures the yuan qi and drains the yin blood. Also 「權曰忌冷水惡乾漆」 (Zhen Quan: avoid cold water; antagonises dried lacquer) and 「之才曰黄芩為之使無所畏」 (Xu Zhicai: Huang Qin is its envoy; it fears nothing). Note the pregnancy caution is 1596, not modern.

TOXICITY — recorded and CONTESTED in antiquity, which the row does not show. Wu Pu (via Sun Xingyan 1799): 「神農、雷公：苦，有毒；扁鵲：苦，無毒」 — Shennong and Lei Gong called it TOXIC, Bian Que called it non-toxic. The BCGM head line settles on 無毒 but files the herb in 毒草類. Report the split, do not resolve it.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, source idiom (本經, via Sun Xingyan 1799): 「主下瘀血、血閉、寒熱，破症瘕積聚，留飲宿食，蕩滌腸胃，推陳致新，調中化食，安和五臟」 — 蕩滌腸胃 (sluices out the intestines and stomach) and 推陳致新 (pushes out the old and brings on the new) are the two idioms every later text repeats. Li Gao's gloss on the latter, via BCCX 1757: 「如定禍亂以致太平、所以有將軍之名」 — like quelling a rebellion to bring about peace, whence its name 'the General'. Wu Pu already calls it 中將軍 in the Han-layer variant readings.

SYNERGIES (Xu Zhicai, quoted BCGM 1596): 「得芍藥黄芩牡蠣細辛茯苓療驚恚怒心下悸氣得消石紫石英桃仁療女子血閉」 — with Shao Yao (WHITE PEONY, H173 in this same batch), Huang Qin, oyster shell, Xi Xin and Fu Ling it treats fright, rage and palpitation below the heart. A documented classical pairing between two herbs the DB already holds.

results.pre1900_finding: The two oldest and most authoritative sources say NEUTRAL, not cool. Shennong Bencao Jing: 鞠華 味苦，平。 Bencao Gangmu 1596 head line: 氣味苦平無毒, and Li Shizhen's own summation is emphatic — 味兼甘苦性禀平和 ('its flavour joins sweet and bitter; its nature is endowed level and harmonious'). The 'cool' reading is genuine but LATER and narrower: Li Gao (Jin–Yuan) 苦甘寒, Wang Ang 1694 and Wu Yiluo 1757 both 甘苦微寒. So the stored 'Cool' tracks the Qing-era line while the Han and Ming head readings say 平. Both are pre-1900. The value should be represented as a contested range (neutral to slightly cold), not as a single 'Cool'. Reporting both; not adjudicating.
results.source_year: 1799 (Sun Xingyan recension of the c. 200 CE Shennong Bencao Jing); 1596 (Bencao Gangmu); 1757 (Ben Cao Cong Xin, for the 微寒 line)
results.evidence:
Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan recension (1799), 卷一·上經 草部上品: 「==鞠華== 味苦，平。主風，頭眩腫痛，目欲脫，淚出，皮膚死肌，惡風濕痹。久服，利血氣，輕身、耐老、延年。一名節華，生川澤及田野。《吳普》曰：菊華，一名白華（《初學記》），一名女華，一名女莖。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍)

Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (1596), 卷十五 草部隰草類上, 「菊」{{本經上品}}: 「氣味苦平無毒」 with notes: 「别録曰甘　損之曰甘者入藥苦者不入藥　杲曰苦甘寒可升可降隂中微陽也　時珍曰本經言菊花味苦别録言菊花味甘…之才曰术及枸杞根桑根白皮為之使」. And in 發明: 「時珍曰菊春生夏茂秋花冬實偹受四氣飽經露霜葉枯不落花稿不零味兼甘苦性禀平和昔人謂其能除風熱益肝補隂葢不知其得金水之精英尤多能益金水二臟也補水所以制火益金所以平木木平則風息火降則熱除…黄者入金水隂分白者入金水陽分紅者行婦人血分」. Also 「白菊氣味苦辛平無毒」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷15

The later, colder line — Wu Yiluo, 本草從新 (1757), 甘菊花: 「甘苦微寒。備受四氣。（冬苗、春葉、夏蕊、秋花。）飽經霜露。得金水之精。能益肺腎二臟。以制心火而平肝木。木平則風息。火降則熱除。故能養目血。去翳膜。（與枸杞相對、蜜丸久服、永無目疾。）」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新 (transcription has mixed simplified glyphs; corroborating only).
additions: SHENNONG GRADE — 上品, UPPER GRADE, and the rubric is quotable: 「上藥一百二十種，為君，主養命以應天，無毒。多服、久服不傷人。欲輕身益氣，不老延年者，本上經。」 (Sun Xingyan 1799, 卷一·上經) — sovereign drugs, non-toxic, ABUNDANT AND PROLONGED USE DOES NOT HARM. 鞠華 appears in that volume's 草部上品 roster. Li Shizhen underlines it: 「宜乎前賢比之君子…神農列之上品」. For a product recommending daily herbs this is the strongest possible classical warrant, and it is a fact the row does not carry.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经) — and the classical answer differs materially from the modern one the row stores. The row says 'entering the Lung and Liver channels'. Li Shizhen 1596 says the metal and water organs, i.e. LUNG AND KIDNEY: 「其得金水之精英尤多能益金水二臟也補水所以制火益金所以平木木平則風息火降則熱除」 — it enriches Lung and Kidney; enriching water restrains fire, supplementing metal levels wood; wood levelled, wind ceases; fire descending, heat is removed. Wu Yiluo 1757 says the same: 「能益肺腎二臟。以制心火而平肝木」. The Liver action is INDIRECT (via levelling wood), not a direct channel entry. Wang Haogu's contribution is narrower: 「主肝氣不足」 (governs insufficiency of Liver qi). Li Shizhen also splits by flower colour: 「黄者入金水隂分白者入金水陽分紅者行婦人血分」 — yellow enters the yin division of metal-and-water, white the yang division, red moves women's blood division.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, source idiom (本經, via Sun Xingyan 1799): 「主風，頭眩腫痛，目欲脫，淚出，皮膚死肌，惡風濕痹。久服，利血氣，輕身、耐老、延年。」 — wind; head spinning with swelling and pain; THE EYES AS IF ABOUT TO FALL OUT; tears streaming; dead flesh of the skin; aversion to wind and damp painful obstruction. With prolonged use it benefits blood and qi, lightens the body, withstands ageing, extends the years. The Bielu adds 「療腰痛去來陶陶除胸中煩熱安腸胃利五脉調四肢」.

ENVOY HERBS AND A FORMULA PAIRING INSIDE THIS BATCH — Xu Zhicai (via BCGM 1596): 「之才曰术及枸杞根桑根白皮為之使」 — Atractylodes, LYCIUM ROOT-BARK and mulberry root-bark act as its envoys. Wu Yiluo 1757 updates the list to 「點朮、枸杞子、地骨皮爲使」 and gives the clinical pairing outright: 「與枸杞相對、蜜丸久服、永無目疾」 — matched with GOU QI ZI (H170 in this batch), made into honey pills, taken long, and one will never have eye disease. That is a documented pre-1900 pairing between two herbs the DB already holds and it has no place to live in the current schema.

SPECIES DISCIPLINE AND CONTRAINDICATION, in the same breath — 「但不得用野菊名苦薏者爾故景煥牧竪閑談云真菊延齡野菊泄人正如黄精益夀鉤吻殺人之意」 (BCGM 1596): one must NOT use the wild chrysanthemum called 苦薏 (Chrysanthemum indicum); 'true chrysanthemum extends the years, wild chrysanthemum drains a person' — exactly as Huang Jing benefits longevity while Gou Wen kills. The identification test is given earlier in the same entry: 「氣味苦不堪食者名苦薏非真菊也葉正相似」 — bitter and inedible, and the LEAVES LOOK IDENTICAL. Wu Yiluo 1757 repeats it and adds the selection rule: 「家園所種。杭產者良…有黃白二種。單瓣味甘者入藥」 — garden-grown, Hangzhou produce is good; of the yellow and white kinds, only the SINGLE-PETALLED SWEET-TASTING one goes into medicine. This is directly actionable sourcing guidance for a product and it is absent from the row.

A SEPARATE ENTRY FOR THE WHITE FLOWER — 「白菊氣味苦辛平無毒」 (BCGM 1596): white chrysanthemum is bitter, ACRID, neutral, non-toxic; 主治風眩能令頭不白 (wind-dizziness; keeps the head from greying). Different rasa from the head reading. The row treats Ju Hua as one drug.

PREPARATION — 「自本至末罔不有功宜乎前賢比之君子其苗可蔬葉可啜花可餌根實可藥嚢之可枕醸之可飲」 (BCGM 1596): sprout as a vegetable, leaf sipped, flower eaten as a supplement, root and fruit as medicine, bagged into a PILLOW, brewed into a drink. 大明 adds 「作枕明目葉亦明目生熟並可食」 — made into a pillow it brightens the eyes. The chrysanthemum-flower pillow is a classical preparation the row has no way to express.
MOISTURE — HONEST GAP. The row stores moisture 'Neutral'. There is no moisture axis in any of these sources; do not claim classical support for that field either way.

results.herb: Goji / Wolfberry / Gou Qi Zi (Lycium barbarum)
results.pre1900_finding: 'Neutral' is CORRECT FOR THE BERRY and is Li Shizhen's own part-specific verdict — 至于子則甘平而潤性滋而補…此乃平補之藥 ('as for the fruit, it is sweet and NEUTRAL and moistening; enriching and tonifying in nature; this is a level-tonifying drug'). But the same herb carries FOUR conflicting pre-1900 readings and the head line of the entry is COLD: 氣味枸杞苦寒無毒 (本經), 根大寒子微寒 (別錄), 甘平 (甄權, endorsed by Li Shizhen), 甘微溫 (Wu Yiluo 1757). Li Shizhen states outright that the Benjing reading was never part-specific: 今考本經止云枸杞不指是根莖葉子. So the stored value is defensible but must be recorded as the BERRY reading within a contested set, not as the herb's undisputed temperature.
results.source_year: 1596 (Bencao Gangmu); 1799 (Sun Xingyan recension of the c. 200 CE Shennong Bencao Jing); 1757 (Ben Cao Cong Xin)
results.evidence:
Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (1596), 卷三十六 木部灌木類, 「枸杞地骨皮」{{本經上品}} head: 「氣味枸杞苦寒無毒」 with notes: 「别錄曰根大寒子微寒無毒冬采根春夏采葉秋采莖實　權曰枸杞甘平子葉同　宗奭曰枸杞當用梗皮地骨當用根皮子當用紅實其皮寒根大寒子微寒今人多用其子為補腎藥是末曽考竟經意當量其虚實冷熱用之　時珍曰今考本經止云枸杞不指是根莖葉子别錄乃增根大寒子微寒字…竊謂枸杞苖葉味苦甘而氣凉根味甘淡氣寒子味甘氣平氣味既殊則功用當别」. The 枸杞子 sub-entry head: 「氣味苦寒」{{權曰甘平}}. And in 發明: 「蓋其苖乃天精苦甘而凉上焦心肺客熱者宜之根乃地骨甘淡而寒下焦肝腎虚熱者宜之此皆三焦氣分之藥所謂熱淫于内瀉以甘寒也至于子則甘平而潤性滋而補不能退熱止能補腎潤肺生精益氣此乃平補之藥所謂精不足者補之以味也」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷36

Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan recension (1799), 木部上品 (entry has no heading; located by its alias string 一名杞根，一名地骨): 「味苦，寒。主五內邪氣，熱中消渴，周痹。久服，堅筋骨、輕身、不老（《御覽》作耐老）。一名杞根，一名地骨，一名枸杞，一名地輔。生平澤。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍)

The warm reading — Wu Yiluo, 本草從新 (1757), 枸杞子: 「甘微溫。滋肝益腎…便滑者勿用…以甘州所產。紅潤少核者佳。酒潤搗。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新 . Wang Ang, 本草備要 (1694), 枸杞子, prints the disagreement openly: 「甘平（《本草》苦寒）」 (LOCATE-ONLY; that transcription is simplified and must not be quoted as the 1694 text).
additions: SHENNONG GRADE — 上品, UPPER GRADE (Sun Xingyan 1799, 木部上品; BCGM tags the entry 「本經上品」). Rubric: 「上藥一百二十種，為君，主養命以應天，無毒。多服、久服不傷人。」 Prolonged and abundant use does not harm. Li Shizhen reinforces it by quoting Liu Yuxi's well poem: 「上品功能甘露味還知一勺可延齡」. Strong classical warrant for daily use — but see the four-readings problem below before letting that stand unqualified.

PART DISCIPLINE — this is the herb's defining problem and the row shows none of it. One plant, FOUR drugs with FOUR different temperatures, stated in one sentence by Li Shizhen (BCGM 1596): 「苖乃天精苦甘而凉」 (sprout/leaf = Tian Jing, bitter-sweet and COOL, for upper-burner Heart and Lung visiting heat), 「根乃地骨甘淡而寒」 (root-bark = Di Gu Pi, sweet-bland and COLD, for lower-burner Liver and Kidney deficient heat), 「至于子則甘平而潤」 (fruit = sweet, NEUTRAL, moistening). Plus Kou Zongshi's fourth: 「枸杞當用梗皮」 — the stem bark. Kou Zongshi's warning is aimed precisely at the modern error: 「今人多用其子為補腎藥是末曽考竟經意當量其虚實冷熱用之」 — people use the fruit as a Kidney tonic without having thought through the classic's intent; weigh deficiency, excess, cold and heat before using.

FOUR-SEASON HARVEST DOCTRINE — one plant, four drugs, four seasons (BCGM 1596, 地仙丹 from 保壽堂方): 「春采枸杞葉名天精草夏采花名長生草秋采子名枸杞子冬采根名地骨皮並隂乾用」 — spring leaf = Tian Jing Cao, summer flower = Chang Sheng Cao, autumn fruit = Gou Qi Zi, winter root = Di Gu Pi, all shade-dried. The Bielu gives its own calendar: 「冬采根春夏采葉秋采莖實」. Nothing in the DB captures seasonal identity of a part.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经) — for the BERRY specifically: 「時珍曰滋腎潤肺」 (enriches Kidney, moistens Lung) and 「好古曰主心病嗌乾心痛渴而引飲腎病消中」 (Heart disease with dry throat and heart pain; thirst that drives drinking; Kidney disease with middle-wasting). Wu Yiluo 1757: 「滋肝益腎」 — Liver and Kidney, which matches the row. IMPORTANT TRAP: the widely quoted 「好古曰入足少隂手少陽經」 (foot shaoyin Kidney, hand shaoyang Sanjiao) belongs to the 地骨皮 (ROOT-BARK) sub-entry, not the berry. Do not carry it across. Li Shizhen classes leaf and root together as 「三焦氣分之藥」 and the berry separately as 「平補之藥」.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, source idiom (本經, via Sun Xingyan 1799): 「主五內邪氣，熱中消渴，周痹。久服，堅筋骨、輕身、不老。」 — evil qi of the five viscera, heat in the centre with wasting-thirst, generalized painful obstruction; prolonged use hardens sinew and bone, lightens the body, prevents ageing. 甄權 adds 「補精氣諸不足易顔色變白明目安神令人長壽」.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — wine, and it is unanimous across three centuries. Li Shizhen 1596, 枸杞子修治: 「凡用揀淨枝梗取鮮明者洗淨酒潤一夜搗爛入藥」 — pick out twigs and stems, take the bright clear berries, wash clean, MOISTEN WITH WINE OVERNIGHT, pound to a mash, then add to the formula. Wu Yiluo 1757: 「酒潤搗」. Wang Ang 1694: 「酒浸捣用」. The row's part_used says only 'ripe fruit, dried'.

SOURCING DOCTRINE, and the only species-discriminating evidence found — Wu Yiluo, 本草從新 (1757): 「以甘州所產。紅潤少核者佳」 — the Ganzhou (Gansu) produce, red, plump, few-seeded, is the good grade. Ganzhou is Lycium barbarum country, which is the nearest a pre-1900 Chinese source comes to endorsing the row's stored binomial. Li Shizhen adds a field test: 「此藥采無刺味甜者其有刺者服之無益也」 — harvest the THORNLESS, SWEET-TASTING kind; the thorny kind taken internally is of no benefit.

CONTRAINDICATION — 「便滑者勿用」 (Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757): do not use in those with slippery/loose stool. That is the only contraindication any of these sources states for the berry, and the row has none. Note also that the 本經 head reading being 苦寒 while the berry is 甘平 means the herb's reputation for 'clearing heat' belongs to the ROOT-BARK; Li Shizhen is explicit that the berry 「不能退熱止能補腎潤肺生精益氣」 — it CANNOT reduce heat, it can only tonify.

FORMULA PAIRING INSIDE THIS BATCH — Wu Yiluo 1757, under 甘菊花: 「與枸杞相對、蜜丸久服、永無目疾」 — chrysanthemum matched with Gou Qi Zi in honey pills, taken long, and one will never have eye disease. Xu Zhicai (BCGM 1596) makes Lycium root-bark an envoy for chrysanthemum. Both herbs are in this batch (H169) and the pairing is the classical basis for every 'brighten the eyes' claim.

SPECIES CAVEAT — no pre-1900 Chinese source distinguishes Lycium barbarum from L. chinense; both are 枸杞, and BCGM records only geographic and habit variation (「生北方沙地者皆木類南方堅地者如草類也」). The row's binomial is a modern determination and should be marked as such. SEPARATELY: F. Porter Smith 1871 identifies the 枸杞/地骨皮 drug as Berberis Lycium and Berberis chinensis — a BARBERRY. That determination is wrong for this herb and must not be imported.

results.pre1900_finding: Contested across the whole pre-1900 span, and the oldest layer says NEUTRAL. Shennong Bencao Jing: 芍藥 味苦，平。 Bencao Gangmu 1596 head: 氣味苦平無毒. And the reading that is specifically about WHITE peony is also neutral — 杲曰白芍藥酸平有小毒 (Li Gao: Bai Shao is sour, NEUTRAL, slightly toxic). The 'cool' line comes from the Mingyi Bielu — 别錄曰酸微寒有小毒 — and is carried by Wu Yiluo 1757 (苦酸微寒) and Wang Ang 1694. Wu Pu preserves the Han-era dissent: 李氏：小寒. So stored 'Cool' has real pre-1900 support, but so does neutral, and the white-specific authority (Li Gao) is on the neutral side. Represent as a contested range, and note the record of slight toxicity that no modern source carries.
results.source_year: 1799 (Sun Xingyan recension of the c. 200 CE Shennong Bencao Jing); 1596 (Bencao Gangmu); 1757 (Ben Cao Cong Xin, for the 微寒 line)
results.evidence:
Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan recension (1799), 卷二·中經: 「==芍藥== 味苦，平。主邪氣腹痛，除血痹，破堅積、寒熱、疝瘕，止痛，利小便，益氣。生川谷及《吳普》曰：芍藥，神農：苦；桐君：甘，無毒；岐伯：咸；李氏：小寒；雷公：酸。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍)

Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (1596), 卷十四 草部芳草類, 「芍藥」{{芍音杓又音勺本經中品}}: 「氣味苦平無毒」 with notes: 「别錄曰酸微寒有小毒　普曰神農苦桐君甘無毒岐伯鹹雷公酸李當之小寒　元素曰性寒味酸氣厚味薄升而微降陽中隂也　杲曰白芍藥酸平有小毒可升可降隂也　好古曰味酸而苦氣薄味厚隂也降也為手足太隂行經藥入肝脾血分　之才曰須丸為之使惡石斛芒消畏消石鼈甲小薊反藜蘆」. And in 發明: 「宗奭曰…然氣虚寒人禁之古人云減芍藥以避中寒誠不可忽　震亨曰芍藥瀉脾火性味酸寒冬月必以酒炒…下痢腹痛必炒用後重者不炒産後不可用者以其酸寒伐生發之氣也必不得已亦酒炒用之　時珍曰白芍藥益脾能於土中瀉木赤芍藥散邪能行血中之滯」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷14

Wu Yiluo, 本草從新 (1757), 白芍藥: 「苦酸微寒。入肝脾血分。（白朮補脾陽、白芍補脾陰、爲手足太陰行經藥。（肺、脾。））瀉肝火…緩中止痛…除煩敛汗。退熱安胎。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新 (mixed simplified glyphs in this transcription; corroborating only).
additions: SHENNONG GRADE — 中品, MIDDLE GRADE (BCGM tags it 「本經中品」; Sun Xingyan 1799 lists 芍藥 in 卷二·中經). Rubric: 「中藥一百二十種為臣，主養性以應人。無毒、有毒，斟酌其宜。欲遏病補羸者，本中經。」 — ministers, for nourishing the nature, SOME TOXIC AND SOME NOT, to be weighed for fitness, for checking disease and building up the weakened. Not the unrestricted daily class that Ju Hua and Chen Pi occupy. That distinction is invisible in the DB and matters for duration-of-use guidance.

TOXICITY ON RECORD, twice — 「别錄曰酸微寒有小毒」 and 「杲曰白芍藥酸平有小毒」 (both BCGM 1596). Two independent pre-1900 authorities record Bai Shao as SLIGHTLY TOXIC (有小毒). No modern monograph carries this. The BCGM head line settles on 無毒; report the split rather than resolving it.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经) — richer than what the row stores. Wang Haogu (BCGM 1596): 「為手足太隂行經藥入肝脾血分」 — it is a HAND-AND-FOOT TAIYIN (Lung and Spleen) channel-CONDUCTING drug that ENTERS THE LIVER AND SPLEEN BLOOD DIVISION. Wu Yiluo 1757 prints both halves side by side: 「入肝脾血分…爲手足太陰行經藥。（肺、脾。）」. The row names Liver and Spleen (correct) but misses the taiyin Lung–Spleen conducting role, which is what justifies the classical 固腠理 / 安脾肺 indications.

WHITE vs RED DOCTRINE — the row's part_used describes the peeling and boiling correctly but carries none of the classical function split. BCGM 1596: 「恭曰赤者利小便下氣白者止痛散血」; 「大明曰赤者補氣白者補血」; 「成無已曰白補而赤瀉白收而赤散」 (white tonifies and red drains; white gathers in and red disperses); 「元素曰白補赤散瀉肝補脾胃」; and Li Shizhen's correction of Rihuazi: 「白芍藥益脾能於土中瀉木赤芍藥散邪能行血中之滯日華子言赤補氣白治血欠審矣」. Also Tao Hongjing: 「白者道家亦服食之」 — the white is what the Daoists took as a dietary supplement. Note the Shennong Bencao Jing has ONE undifferentiated 芍藥; the split is post-Han, which the row already states correctly.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — season-dependent and indication-dependent. Zhu Zhenheng (BCGM 1596): 「冬月必以酒炒」 — in winter months it MUST be dry-fried with wine; 「凡腹痛多是血脈凝濇亦必酒炒用」; 「下痢腹痛必炒用後重者不炒」 — for dysentery with abdominal pain it must be fried, but for TENESMUS do NOT fry it. And the ancient dietetic method (Anqi Sheng, via Su Song, BCGM 1596 附方 服食法): 「凡采得淨洗去皮以東流水煑百沸隂乾停三日又於木甑内蒸之上覆以淨黄土一日夜熟出隂乾擣末以麥飲或酒服三錢七日三服」 — wash clean, PEEL, boil a hundred bubbles in east-flowing water, shade-dry three days, then steam in a wooden steamer under clean yellow earth for a day and night. This is the classical locus for the peeling-and-boiling the row's part_used describes.

CONTRAINDICATIONS, and they are firm. (1) Kou Zongshi: 「然氣虚寒人禁之古人云減芍藥以避中寒誠不可忽」 — FORBIDDEN in people with qi deficiency and cold; the ancients said 'reduce the shaoyao to avoid cold in the middle', and this must not be brushed aside. (2) Zhu Zhenheng: 「産後不可用者以其酸寒伐生發之氣也必不得已亦酒炒用之」 — NOT TO BE USED POSTPARTUM, because its sour-cold cuts down the generating and ascending qi; if unavoidable, use it wine-fried. Li Shizhen glosses the reason: 「産後肝血已虚不可更瀉故禁之」.

INCOMPATIBILITY LIST — Xu Zhicai (BCGM 1596): 「須丸為之使惡石斛芒消畏消石鼈甲小薊反藜蘆」 — Xu Wan is its envoy; it DISLIKES Shi Hu and Mang Xiao; it FEARS Xiao Shi, Bie Jia and Xiao Ji; and it COUNTERACTS LI LU (Veratrum) — the 反 relation, i.e. the classical eighteen-antagonisms prohibition. That last is a hard safety fact with no column anywhere in the schema.

CLASSICAL PAIRINGS — Li Shizhen (BCGM 1596): 「同白术補脾同芎藭瀉肝同人參補氣同當歸補血以酒炒補隂同甘草止腹痛同黄連止瀉痢同防風發痘疹同薑温經散濕」. And Zhang Yuansu's six uses: 「其用凡六安脾經一也治腹痛二也收胃氣三也止瀉痢四也和血脉五也固腠理六也」 — with the licorice pairing named as Zhang Zhongjing's 神方.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, source idiom (本經, via Sun Xingyan 1799): 「主邪氣腹痛，除血痹，破堅積、寒熱、疝瘕，止痛，利小便，益氣。」 The Bielu adds 「通順血脈緩中散惡血逐賊血去水氣利膀胱大小膓消癰腫時行寒熱中惡腹痛腰痛」 — 逐賊血 ('drives out bandit blood') is a striking classical idiom the row's summary flattens.

Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan recension (1799), 木部上品: 「==橘柚== 味辛，溫。主胸中瘕熱逆氣，利水谷。久服，去臭、下氣、通神。一名橘皮。生川谷（舊在果部，非）。《名醫》曰：生南山、江南。十月采。」 followed by the roster line 「上木，上品二十種，舊一十九種。考果部，橘柚當入此。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍)

Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (1596), 卷三十 果部之二, 「橘」{{本經上品}}　校正{{志曰自木部移入此}}, sub-entry 「黃橘皮」: 「氣味苦辛温無毒主治胸中瘕熱逆氣利水穀久服去臭下氣通神{{本經}}」. Preparation notes in the same entry: 「凡橘皮入和中理胃藥則留白入下氣消痰藥則去白其說出於聖濟經去白者以白湯入鹽洗潤透刮去筋膜晒乾用亦有煑焙者各隨本方」; aging: 「𢎞景曰橘皮療氣大勝以東橘為好西江者不如須陳久者為良」 and 「他藥貴新惟此貴陳」 (方勺泊宅編, quoted by Li Shizhen); and 「時珍曰…橘皮性温柑柚皮性冷不可不知」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷30

Wu Yiluo, 本草從新 (1757), 橘皮: 「辛能散，溫能和，苦能燥能瀉。爲脾、肺氣分之藥…入和中藥。則留白。入疏通藥。則去白…氣雖中和。亦損真元。無滯勿用…陳久者良。故又名陳皮。（陳則烈氣消、無燥散之患、半夏亦然、故同用、名二陳湯。）」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新 (mixed simplified glyphs in this transcription; corroborating only).
additions: SHENNONG GRADE — 上品, UPPER GRADE, and confirmed on both routes: the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension places 橘柚 in the 木部上品 roster (「上木，上品二十種」), and Li Shizhen tags the entry 「本經上品」 with 「校正　志曰自木部移入此」 (relocated from the tree section to the fruit section). Upper-grade rubric: 「上藥一百二十種，為君，主養命以應天，無毒。多服、久服不傷人。」 This is the row's strongest warrant for daily use — but see the contraindication below, which qualifies it sharply.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经) — SPLEEN and LUNG, qi division, bidirectional. Li Gao (BCGM 1596): 「橘皮氣薄味厚陽中之隂也可升可降為脾肺二經氣分藥留白則補脾胃去白則理肺氣同白术則補脾胃同甘草則補肺獨用則瀉肺損脾」. Li Shizhen gives the reasoning: 「脾乃元氣之母肺乃攝氣之籥故橘皮為二經氣分之藥但隨所配而補瀉升降也」 — the Spleen is the mother of yuan qi, the Lung is the valve that governs qi. Wu Yiluo 1757 identical. The row's tcm_pattern_match names Spleen, Stomach and Lung; the classical assignment is precisely Spleen and Lung, qi division.

THE AGING DOCTRINE — the whole justification for the 'Chen' in Chen Pi, and the row asserts it without a source. Tao Hongjing (BCGM 1596): 「橘皮療氣大勝以東橘為好西江者不如須陳久者為良」 — must be long-aged to be good. Wang Haogu: 「橘皮以色紅日久者為佳故曰紅皮陳皮去白者曰橘紅也」. And the line worth putting on a label, Li Shizhen quoting 方勺泊宅編: 「他藥貴新惟此貴陳」 — other drugs prize freshness; this one alone prizes age. Wu Yiluo 1757 supplies the mechanism the row lacks: 「陳則烈氣消、無燥散之患」 — aged, the fierce qi is spent, so there is no danger of drying and dispersing; 「故同用、名二陳湯」 (whence Er Chen Tang, the Two-Aged Decoction, which the row already names).

WITH-WHITE / WITHOUT-WHITE — a preparation distinction that changes the indication, and the row has no field for it. 「凡橘皮入和中理胃藥則留白入下氣消痰藥則去白其說出於聖濟經」 (BCGM 1596) — LEAVE the white pith when it goes into harmonizing and stomach-regulating formulas; REMOVE the white when it goes into qi-descending and phlegm-dissolving formulas. Method: 「去白者以白湯入鹽洗潤透刮去筋膜晒乾用亦有煑焙者各隨本方」. Wu Yiluo 1757: 「去白名橘紅。兼能除寒發表」 — de-pithed it becomes JU HONG, which additionally dispels cold and releases the exterior. Wang Ang 1694 records the counter-tradition: 「《聖濟》云∶不去白，反生痰」 (locate-only, simplified transcription). Lei Xiao's older method: 「凡使勿用桔皮皺子皮二件…須去白膜一重剉細以鯉魚皮褁一宿至明取用」 — wrapped in CARP SKIN overnight.

FURTHER PREPARATION BY TARGET (Wu Yiluo 1757): 「治痰咳。童便浸晒。治痰積。薑汁炒。入下焦。鹽水炒。」 — for phlegm-cough, soak in boys' urine and sun-dry; for phlegm accumulation, fry in ginger juice; to reach the lower burner, fry in salt water. One herb, three processings, three targets.

CONTRAINDICATION — and it directly limits the 'daily herb' reading of the upper grade. Li Gao (BCGM 1596): 「獨用則瀉肺損脾…加青皮减半用之去滯氣推陳致新但多用久服能損元氣也」 — used ALONE it drains the Lung and injures the Spleen; and MUCH USE OR PROLONGED USE CAN DAMAGE THE YUAN QI. Wu Yiluo 1757 states the rule flatly: 「氣雖中和。亦損真元。無滯勿用。」 — though its qi is harmonizing, it still injures the true yuan; DO NOT USE WHERE THERE IS NO STAGNATION. Li Shizhen on the Run Xia Wan: 「惟氣實人服之相宜氣不足者不宜用之也」 — suits people of excess qi; unsuitable for the qi-deficient. The row carries none of this.

SPECIES / ADULTERATION, AND A TEMPERATURE INVERSION — 「時珍曰橘皮紋細色紅而薄内多筋胍其味苦辛柑皮紋粗色黄而厚内多白膜其味辛甘柚皮最厚而虚紋更粗色黃内多膜無筋其味甘多辛少但以此别之即不差矣橘皮性温柑柚皮性冷不可不知今天下多以廣中來者為勝江西者次之然亦多以柑皮雜之柑皮猶可用柚皮則懸絶矣」 (BCGM 1596) — TANGERINE peel is WARM but 柑 (gan) and 柚 (pomelo) peels are COLD, and the trade routinely adulterates with them. Li Shizhen gives the identification marks: tangerine peel fine-grained, red, thin, many fibrous veins, bitter-acrid; gan peel coarse-grained, yellow, thick, much white membrane, acrid-sweet; pomelo peel thickest and spongy, coarsest grain, yellow, membranous with no fibres, mostly sweet with little acridity. Wu Yiluo 1757 says the problem worsened: 「化州陳皮…此物真者絕少、無非柚皮而已」 — genuine Huazhou chenpi is exceedingly rare; nearly all of it is pomelo peel. A pre-1900 source stating that the common adulterant carries the OPPOSITE temperature is exactly the sourcing risk a product should surface.

THE FRUIT vs THE PEEL — opposite actions, same plant: 「橘實氣味甘酸温無毒」 with 「時珍曰橘皮下氣消痰其肉生痰聚飲表裏之異如此凡物皆然」 — the PEEL descends qi and dissolves phlegm, while the FLESH generates phlegm and gathers rheum; outside and inside differ this much. Also 𢎞景: 「食之多痰恐非益也」 and 「同螃蟹食令人患軟癰」 (with crab, causes soft abscess).

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, source idiom (本經, via Sun Xingyan 1799): 「主胸中瘕熱逆氣，利水谷。久服，去臭、下氣、通神。」 — masses and heat in the chest with counterflow qi; benefits water and grain; with prolonged use it removes foul odour, descends the qi and OPENS THE SPIRIT (通神). The Bielu adds 「下氣止嘔欬…療脾不能消穀止洩除膀胱留熱停水起淋利小便去寸白蟲」.

results.herb: Coptis / Goldthread (Huang Lian) — Coptis chinensis, dried rhizome
results.pre1900_finding: 氣味苦寒無毒 — bitter, COLD, non-toxic (BCGM 1596 head reading). Shennong layer agrees: 味苦，寒。 Dissenting sub-readings recorded in 1596 are all still cold-side: 别録曰㣲寒 (Bielu: slightly cold) and 李當之小寒 (Li Dangzhi: mildly cold). Qing consensus intensifies it: 大苦大寒 (greatly bitter, greatly cold). No pre-1900 source read it warm or neutral. Stored value stands.
results.source_year: 1596 (BCGM); corroborated 1799 Sun Xingyan recension of the c. 200 CE Shennong Bencao Jing, and 1757 Ben Cao Cong Xin
results.evidence: Li Shizhen 李時珍, Bencao Gangmu 本草綱目 (Siku Quanshu recension), 卷13 草部·山草類下, 1596 — entry headed 「{{SK anchor|黄連}}{{SK notes|本經上品}}」, qi-wei line: 「氣味苦寒無毒」 with attached note 「别録曰㣲寒普曰神農岐伯黄帝雷公苦無毒李當之小寒」. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷13 || Shennong Bencao Jing 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan 孫星衍 recension, 1799: 「==黃連== 味苦，寒。主熱氣目痛、[眥]傷泣出，明目…腸[澼]，腹痛下利，婦人陰中腫痛。久服，令人不忘。一名王連。生川谷。」 and 「《吳普》曰：黃連，神農、岐伯、黃帝、雷公：苦，無毒；李氏：小寒。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) || Wu Yiluo 吳儀洛, Ben Cao Cong Xin 本草從新, 1757, 黃連: 「大苦大寒。入心瀉火。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 上品 (UPPER grade). BCGM 1596 heads the entry 「本經上品」. Upper grade in the Shennong scheme means non-toxic and intended for prolonged/daily use — but note this sits in tension with the Qing warning below, and the 本經 itself endorses long use: 「久服，令人不忘」 (long use makes one not forgetful).

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经): 手少陰心經 — Hand Shaoyin Heart. Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 卷13 脩治: 「黄連入手少隂心經為治火之主藥」 (Huang Lian enters the Hand Shaoyin Heart channel and is the chief medicine for treating fire). Zhang Yuansu, quoted in 發明: 「黄連性寒味苦氣味俱厚可升可降隂中陽也入手少隂經」 (nature cold, taste bitter, qi and flavour both thick, can ascend and can descend, yang within yin).

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — the richest processing passage in the batch. Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 卷13 根脩治, gives eight target-specific fryings: 「治本臓之火則生用之治肝膽之實火則以豬膽汁浸炒治肝膽之虚火則以醋浸炒治上焦之火則以酒炒治中焦之火則以薑汁炒治下焦之火則以塩水或朴消炒治氣分濕熱之火則以茱萸湯浸炒治血分塊中伏火則以乾漆水炒治食積之火則以黄土炒」 — raw for the organ's own fire; pig-bile-soaked and fried for Liver/Gallbladder excess fire; vinegar-soaked and fried for their deficient fire; wine-fried for the upper burner; ginger-juice-fried for the middle; salt water or mirabilite for the lower; Evodia-decoction-soaked for qi-level damp-heat fire; dried-lacquer water for blood-level hidden fire; yellow earth for food-accumulation fire. The governing principle is stated outright: 「盖辛熱能制其苦寒鹹寒能制其燥性」 (acrid-hot controls its bitter-cold; salty-cold controls its drying nature). Earlier method, Lei Xiao 雷斆 quoted ibid.: 「凡使以布拭去肉毛用漿水浸二伏時漉出于栁木火上焙乾用」.

CONTRAINDICATIONS as stated classically (BCGM 1596 卷13, note to the qi-wei line): 「之才曰黄芩龍骨理石為之使惡菊花𤣥参白鮮皮芫花白殭蠶畏款冬牛膝勝烏頭解巴豆毒權曰忌豬肉惡冷水斆曰服此藥至十兩不得食豬肉若服至三年一生不得食也」 — Xu Zhicai: Scutellaria, dragon bone and gypsum are its envoys; it hates Chrysanthemum, Scrophularia, Dictamnus, Daphne genkwa and white silkworm; it fears Tussilago and Achyranthes; it overcomes Aconitum; it resolves croton poison. Zhen Quan: AVOID PORK, hates cold water. Lei Xiao: after ten liang of this drug one must not eat pork; after three years' use, never again.

DOSE-LIMITING WARNING that a daily-herb product should carry. Kou Zongshi 寇宗奭, quoted BCGM 1596 卷13 發明: 「今人多用黄連治痢…又不顧寒熱多少惟欲盡劑由是多致危困若氣實初病熱多血痢服之便止不必盡劑虛而冷者慎勿輕用」 — people use it for dysentery without regard to how much cold or heat is present, insisting on finishing the course, and thereby often bring on crisis; where qi is replete and the disease new and hot, stop as soon as it works, do not finish the course; IN THE DEFICIENT AND COLD, be careful not to use it lightly.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom, 本經 layer (BCGM 1596 卷13): 「主治熱氣目痛眥傷泣出明目腸澼腹痛下痢婦人隂中腫痛乆服令人不忘」. 别録 layer: 「主五臓冷熱乆下洩澼膿血止消渴大驚除水利骨調胃厚腸益膽療口瘡」. Li Shizhen's own addition: 「去心竅惡血解服藥過劑煩悶及巴豆輕粉毒」 (resolves the vexation of an overdose of medicine, and croton and calomel poisoning).

PAIRING DOCTRINE supporting the stored Zuo Jin Wan / San Huang framing, in pre-1900 words. Zhu Zhenheng 朱震亨, BCGM 1596 卷13 發明: 「黄連去中焦濕熱而瀉心火若脾胃氣虚不能轉運者則以茯苓黄芩代之以猪膽汁拌炒佐以龍膽草則大瀉肝膽之火」. Liu Wansu 劉完素, ibid.: 「諸苦寒藥多泄惟黄連黄蘗性冷而燥能降火去濕而止瀉痢故治痢以之為君」 — among bitter-cold drugs most drain, but Huang Lian and Huang Bai alone are cold AND drying.

results.herb: Forsythia (Lian Qiao) — Forsythia suspensa, dried fruit
results.pre1900_finding: The head reading in every pre-1900 text I reached is 平 NEUTRAL, not cool and not slightly cold: 味苦，平 (SNBCJ), 連翹味苦平無毒 (Zhenglei 1108), 氣味苦平無毒 (BCGM 1596). 'Cool' enters the record only as Zhang Yuansu's Jin-dynasty gloss printed inside the 1596 entry — 元素曰性涼味苦 — and 微寒 only later still, in Wang Ang 1694. Li Shizhen's own reading is 微苦辛, no temperature at all. So the stored value is a post-classical reading layered on a neutral head reading; it has pre-1900 warrant but it is not the 本經 assignment, and the DB's parenthetical 'classically slightly cold' misattributes a 17th-century gloss to the classical layer.
results.source_year: 1596 (BCGM); head reading corroborated 1108 (Zhenglei) and in the 1799 Sun Xingyan recension of the c. 200 CE Shennong Bencao Jing
results.evidence: Shennong Bencao Jing 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan 孫星衍 recension, 1799: 「==連翹== 味苦，平。主寒熱、鼠[瘻]，瘰[癧]、癰腫，惡創，癭瘤，結熱蠱毒。一名異翹，一名蘭花，一名軹，一名三廉。生山谷。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) || Tang Shenwei 唐慎微, Zhenglei Bencao 證類本草 (Siku recension), 卷11, 1108: 「連翹味苦平無毒主寒熱鼠瘻瘰[癧]癰腫惡瘡癭瘤結熱蠱毒去白蟲一名異翹一名蘭華一名折根一名軹一名三㢘生太山山谷八月採隂乾」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/證類本草_(四庫全書本)/卷11 || Li Shizhen, Bencao Gangmu 本草綱目 (Siku recension), 卷16, 1596 — entry headed 「{{SK anchor|連翹}}{{SK notes|本經下品}}」: 「氣味苦平無毒」 with note 「元素曰性涼味苦氣味俱薄輕清而浮升也陽也…好古曰隂中陽也入手足少陽手陽明經又入手少隂經時珍曰㣲苦辛」. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷16 || Wang Ang 汪昂, Ben Cao Bei Yao 本草備要, 1694, 连翘: reads 「微寒升浮」 — LOCATED ONLY, not quoted as the 1694 text: the Wikisource transcription is in simplified characters with dropped glyphs and must not be used as a verbatim witness. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草備要
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 下品 (LOWER grade) — and this is the single most product-relevant finding on this herb. BCGM 1596 卷16 heads it 「本經下品」, and the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension places it in 「上草，下品四十九種」. Lower grade in the Shennong scheme encodes short, targeted, symptom-driven use, NOT daily or prolonged use. A product that recommends Forsythia as a daily herb is inverting the classical duration class.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经): Wang Haogu 王好古, quoted BCGM 1596 卷16: 「隂中陽也入手足少陽手陽明經又入手少隂經」 — yang within yin; enters the Hand and Foot Shaoyang (Triple Burner, Gallbladder) and Hand Yangming (Large Intestine) channels, and also the Hand Shaoyin (Heart). Li Shizhen adds, ibid. 發明: 「連翹狀似人心兩片合成其中有仁甚香乃少隂心經厥隂包絡氣分主藥也」 — shaped like a human heart, two halves joined, the kernel highly fragrant; it is the chief qi-level medicine of the Shaoyin Heart and Jueyin Pericardium.

PART DISCIPLINE — the DB stores the FRUIT, but BCGM 1596 卷16 carries the ROOT as a separate drug with a different and colder assignment and its own toxicity: 「翹根氣味甘寒平有小毒」 (sweet, cold/neutral, SLIGHTLY TOXIC), with 「普曰神農雷公甘有毒李當之苦好古曰苦寒」. Zhang Zhongjing's 麻黄連軺赤小豆湯 uses this root, not the fruit — 好古曰此即連翹根也. Do not let the fruit monograph inherit root data or vice versa.

GRADE/GRADING OF THE DRUG ITSELF, supporting the DB's qing qiao / lao qiao note in pre-1900 words. Su Gong 蘇恭, quoted BCGM 1596 卷16 集解: 「此物有两種大翹小翹大翹生下濕地葉狭長如水蘇花黄可愛著子似椿實之未開者作房翹出衆草其小翹生岡原之上葉花實皆似大翹而小細」 — two kinds, da qiao and xiao qiao, distinguished by habitat and size. Note this is a LARGE/SMALL distinction, not the unripe-green vs ripe-split distinction the DB stores; I found no pre-1900 warrant for the qing qiao / lao qiao ripeness grading.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, 本經 layer (BCGM 1596 卷16): 「主治寒熱鼠瘻瘰癧癰腫惡瘡癭瘤結熱蠱毒」 — alternating cold and heat, scrofulous fistula, scrofula, abscess-swellings, malignant sores, goitre and tumour, bound heat, gu-toxin. 别録 adds 「去白蟲」. Zhen Quan: 「通利五淋小便不通除心家客熱」 (frees the five lin, opens blocked urination, removes visiting heat from the Heart) — this is the pre-1900 warrant for the DB's 'guides heat out through the urine'.

STATUS EPITHET, quotable: Zhang Yuansu, BCGM 1596 卷16 發明: 「連翹之用有三瀉心經客熱一也去上焦諸熱二也為瘡家聖藥三也」 — three uses: drains visiting heat from the Heart channel; removes all heat of the upper burner; and is the SAGE MEDICINE FOR SORES. Li Shizhen extends it: 「故為十二經瘡家聖藥」 (the sage medicine for sores of all twelve channels).

PREPARATION: no compulsory processing is recorded in the 1596 entry. The附方 use it simply decocted, powdered, or as a wash — e.g. 「痔瘡腫痛：連翹煎湯熏洗」 (fumigate and wash with the decoction). Contrast Coptis, Phellodendron and Pinellia in this batch, where processing is doctrinally mandatory. No classical contraindication is stated in the BCGM entry.

The Shennong layer agrees exactly: 味苦，寒。 Every pre-1900 witness I reached is cold-side; the Qing texts repeat 苦寒. Stored value stands, and could arguably be strengthened.
