results.evidence: Li Shizhen 李時珍, Bencao Gangmu 本草綱目 (Siku Quanshu recension), 卷36 木部·灌木類, 1596 — entry headed 「{{SK anchor|巵子}}{{SK notes|本經中品}}」, qi-wei line: 「氣味苦寒無毒」 with attached note 「别錄曰酸微寒普曰神農苦雷公酸無毒李當之大寒權曰辛苦元素曰性寒味苦氣厚味薄浮而升微降隂中陽也」 — note: this transcription prints 「呆曰」 for 杲曰 (Li Gao) and 「入乎太隂肺經」 for 入手太隂肺經, two evident transcription slips in the Siku text, flagged rather than silently corrected. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷36 || Shennong Bencao Jing 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan 孫星衍 recension, 1799: 「==卮子== （舊作梔，《藝文類聚》及《御覽》引作支，是） 味苦，寒。主五內邪氣，胃中熱氣，面赤、酒[皰]、[皶]鼻，白[癩]、赤癩，創瘍。一名木丹。生川谷。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) || Wu Yiluo 吳儀洛, Ben Cao Cong Xin 本草從新, 1757, 栀子: 「瀉心肺三焦之火。苦寒。輕飘象肺。色赤入心。瀉心肺之邪熱。使之屈曲下行。由小便出。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 中品 (MIDDLE grade). BCGM 1596 卷36 heads it 「本經中品」 and the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension lists it under 「上木，中品一十七種」. Middle grade encodes symptom-driven use with attention to dosage, between the daily-safe upper grade and the short-course lower grade.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经): Li Gao 李杲, quoted BCGM 1596 卷36: 「沉也隂也入[手]太隂肺經血分」 — sinking, yin, entering the Hand Taiyin LUNG channel at the BLOOD level. Note this is the Lung, not the Heart, despite the herb's classic use for Heart vexation; the Heart connection is by colour signature, Zhang Yuansu: 「巵子輕飄而象肺色赤而象火故能瀉肺中之火」 (light and floating, resembling the Lung; red, resembling fire; therefore it can drain fire from within the Lung). Zhu Zhenheng gives the three-burner claim the DB stores: 「巵子瀉三焦之火及痞塊中火邪最清胃腕之血其性屈曲下行能降火從小便中泄去」.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — part-and-burner specific, and it directly supports the DB's raw / chao / tan trio. Zhu Zhenheng 朱震亨, BCGM 1596 卷36 脩治: 「治上焦中焦連殻用下焦去殻洗去黄漿炒用治血病炒黒用」 — for the upper and middle burner use it WITH the husk; for the lower burner remove the husk, wash off the yellow juice and dry-fry it; for blood disease FRY IT BLACK. Wang Haogu adds a kernel/skin split: 「去心胸中熱用仁去肌表熱用皮」 — to remove heat from heart and chest use the KERNEL; to remove heat from flesh and surface use the SKIN. Lei Xiao 雷斆, ibid.: 「先去皮鬚取仁以甘草水浸一宿漉出焙乾搗篩為末用」 — remove skin and beard, take the kernel, soak overnight in LICORICE WATER, drain, roast dry, pound and sieve.

GRADE OF THE DRUG: Su Song 蘇頌, BCGM 1596 卷36 集解: 「入藥用山巵子方書所謂越桃也皮薄而圓小刻房七稜至九稜者為佳其大而長者雷斆炮炙論謂之伏尸巵子入藥無力」 — the medicinal grade is the small round thin-skinned SHAN ZHI ZI with seven to nine ridges; the large long fruit is what Lei Xiao's Paozhi Lun calls 伏尸巵子 and is WITHOUT POTENCY in medicine.

EMETIC USE — a classical action the DB does not carry. Wang Haogu, BCGM 1596 卷36 發明: 「本草不言巵子能吐仲景用為吐藥巵子本非吐藥為邪氣在上拒而不納食令上吐則邪因以出所謂其高者因而越之也」 — the materia medica does not say Zhi Zi can induce vomiting, yet Zhang Zhongjing used it as an emetic; it is not intrinsically emetic, but where evil qi is lodged above and refuses to be taken in, causing upward vomiting expels it.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, 本經 layer (BCGM 1596 卷36): 「主治五内邪氣胃中熱氣面赤酒皰皶鼻白癩赤癩瘡瘍」 — evil qi in the five viscera, heat qi in the stomach, red face, drink-pimples and brandy-nose, white and red lai (leprous eruptions), sores and ulcers. 别錄 adds 「療目赤熱痛胸心大小腸大熱心中煩悶」. Zhen Quan adds 「解五種黄病利五淋通小便解消渴明目」 — resolves the five kinds of jaundice, the pre-1900 warrant for the damp-heat jaundice indication. Li Shizhen adds 「治吐血衂血血痢下血血淋損傷瘀血及傷寒勞復熱厥頭痛疝氣湯火傷」 — including scald and burn injury, matching the DB's topical trauma note.

CONTRAINDICATION, stated obliquely rather than as a prohibition — Kou Zongshi, BCGM 1596 卷36 發明: 「巵子雖寒而無毒治胃中熱氣既亡血亡津液腑臟無潤養内生虚熱非此物不可去也」 (cold but non-toxic). No absolute contraindication appears in the 1596 entry; the practical limit is carried by the burner-specific processing above.

results.stored_temperature: Cool (functional); DB note concedes classical ushna virya
results.pre1900_finding: Three independent pre-1900 Sanskrit sources assign USHNA VIRYA — HOT potency — and one of them names Guduchi precisely as the exception that proves bitters are otherwise cooling. Caraka: arkāguruguḍūcīnāṃ tiktānām uṣṇam ucyate (of the bitters, arka, aguru and guduchi are said to be HOT). Bhāvaprakāśa: kaṣāyoṣṇā. Rājanighaṇṭu: gurur uṣṇavīryā. There is no pre-1900 Sanskrit reading of śīta for Guduchi that I could find. The one pre-1900 printed source that reports 'cold' is Dymock 1890-93, who reports it as opinion and immediately sets the Unani reading against it. The stored 'Cool' is the herb's clinical EFFECT, not any classical source's virya, and the database is storing an effect in a field that elsewhere holds a source assignment.
results.source_year: 1890-93 for the pre-1900 printed witness (Dymock, Pharmacographia Indica); the load-bearing virya assignments are the Sanskrit originals — Caraka (ancient), Bhāvaprakāśa (16th c.), Rājanighaṇṭu (13th-14th c.)
results.evidence: Agniveśa/Caraka, Carakasaṃhitā, Sūtrasthāna 26.49 (Sanskrit original, pre-Common-Era to c. 200 CE): 「lavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ noṣṇamamlamāmalakaṃ tathā / arkāguruguḍūcīnāṃ tiktānāmuṣṇamucyate //」 — of salts, rock salt is not hot; of sours, amalaki; OF THE BITTERS, ARKA, AGURU AND GUDUCHI ARE SAID TO BE HOT. The Āyurvedadīpikā commentary reinforces it: 「tatra hy uṣṇavīryatā paripanthinī vidyate」. || Bhāvamiśra भावमिश्र, Bhāvaprakāśa Nighaṇṭu, guḍūcyādivarga 8-9 (Sanskrit original, 16th century): 「guḍūcī kaṭukā tiktā svādupākā rasāyanī // saṃgrāhiṇī kaṣāyoṣṇā laghvī balyāgnidīpinī / doṣatrayāmatṛḍdāhamehakāsāṃśca pāṇḍutām // kāmalākuṣṭhavātāsrajvarakrimivamīn haret /」. || Narahari नरहरि, Rājanighaṇṭu 3.17 (Sanskrit original, c. 13th-14th century): 「jñeyā guḍūcī gurur uṣṇavīryā tiktā kaṣāyā jvaranāśinī ca / dāhārtitṛṣṇāvamiraktavātapramehapāṇḍubhramahāriṇī ca //」; and 3.18 for the tuber-borne variety: 「kandodbhavā guḍūcī ca kaṭūṣṇā saṃnipātahā viṣaghnī jvarabhūtaghnī valīpalitanāśinī //」. TRANSLATION-RULE DISCLOSURE: these are the ORIGINAL SANSKRIT, quoted in the original (IAST), from the GRETIL digital corpus (sa_agniveza-carakasaMhitA-parts-comm.xml, sa_bhAvamizra-bhAvaprakAza.xml, sa_narahari-rAjanighaNTu.xml, http://gretil.sub.uni-goettingen.de/). No translation is being cited; my English glosses above are my own reading aid and are not the citation. The digital transcriptions were keyed from 20th-century printed recensions (Benares 1947; Calcutta 1933; Varanasi 1994) — the TEXT is pre-1900, the PRINTING is not, and I state that plainly rather than hide it. || Pre-1900 PRINTED corroboration and the dissent, both: William Dymock, C. J. H. Warden and David Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica, vol. I, p. 55, 1890-93, Tinospora cordifolia: "It is considered to be cold and dry, or according to Arabic and Persian writers, hot and dry in the first degree."
additions: VIPAKA — CONFIRMED and now sourced. Bhāvaprakāśa Nighaṇṭu, guḍūcyādivarga 8: 「svādupākā」 — sweet (svādu = madhura) in pāka, i.e. MADHURA VIPAKA. The DB already asserts this; it now has a 16th-century Sanskrit original behind it instead of a modern pharmacopoeia.

GUNA — the DB's stored claim is WRONG and its attribution is wrong. The DB's secondary citation states 'Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Guduchyadi varga: … guna guru and snigdha …)'. The actual Bhāvaprakāśa text reads 「laghvī」 — LIGHT, the opposite of guru. GURU comes from a different nighantu, Rājanighaṇṭu 3.17 「gurur uṣṇavīryā」. And SNIGDHA (unctuous) appears in NEITHER — I found no pre-1900 Sanskrit source assigning snigdha guna to Guduchi. The two great nighantus genuinely disagree on guna (laghu vs guru); that disagreement should be surfaced, not collapsed, and the fabricated 'snigdha' should be struck. This matters directly: the DB's 'Neutral' moisture value is reasoned FROM the unctuous quality, so the moisture field rests on an unsourced guna.

RASA — the DB stores 'tikta and kashaya'. Bhāvaprakāśa adds a third: 「kaṭukā tiktā」 with kaṣāya implied by 「kaṣāyoṣṇā」 — PUNGENT, bitter and astringent. Rājanighaṇṭu 3.17 gives 「tiktā kaṣāyā」 only. The pungent rasa in Bhāvaprakāśa is part of why the text can assign a hot virya to an otherwise bitter drug.

ADDITIONAL CLASSICAL PROPERTIES the DB has no column for, all from Bhāvaprakāśa Nighaṇṭu 8-9: 「rasāyanī」 (rejuvenative/rasayana), 「saṃgrāhiṇī」 (binding, absorbent — an anti-diarrhoeal property, notable in a herb the DB frames as a clearing alterative), 「balyā」 (strengthening), 「agnidīpinī」 (KINDLES THE DIGESTIVE FIRE — a warming-side action, coherent with ushna virya and inconsistent with a plain cooling reading).

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom, Bhāvaprakāśa Nighaṇṭu 9-10: 「doṣatraya」 (all three doshas — the pre-1900 warrant for tridoshahara), 「āma」 (undigested toxic residue), 「tṛṭ」 (thirst), 「dāha」 (burning), 「meha / prameha」 (urinary and diabetic disorders), 「kāsa」 (cough), 「pāṇḍu」 (anaemia/pallor), 「kāmalā」 (jaundice), 「kuṣṭha」 (skin disease), 「vātāsra」 (vata-rakta, gout), 「jvara」 (fever), 「krimi」 (worms), 「vami」 (vomiting), 「śvāsa」 (dyspnoea), 「arśas」 (piles), 「kṛcchra」 (dysuria), 「hṛdroga」 (heart disease). Rājanighaṇṭu 3.17 adds 「bhrama」 (giddiness) and 「jvaranāśinī」 (fever-destroying).

PREPARATION DOCTRINE. (a) GUDUCHI SATVA, the starch extract the DB mentions, described in a pre-1900 printed source — Dymock, Pharmacographia Indica vol. I p. 55, 1890-93: "from it is prepared a kind of starch known in Hindustani as Giloe-ka-sat, and in some parts of India as Palo. It is prepared by powdering the stem and washing out the starch with water; the latter retains a little of the bitterness of the drug." (b) MEDHYA RASAYANA vehicle and part, Caraka Saṃhitā, Cikitsāsthāna 1.3.30: 「raso guḍūcyāstu samūlapuṣpyāḥ」 — the JUICE of guduchi TOGETHER WITH ROOT AND FLOWER, one of the four medhya rasayanas. Note the part: root and flower with the stem, not the stem alone as the DB stores. (c) Fresh over dry — Dymock ibid.: "The fresh plant is said to be more efficient than the dry; it is taken with milk in rheumatism, acidity of the urine and dyspepsia." Milk is the named vehicle. (d) Dutt 1877 records the vehicle repeatedly: "The fresh juice of the plant is taken with milk as a general tonic"; "a cold infusion of gulancha is given with honey in bilious fever."

SPECIES AND VARIETY DISCIPLINE — two live traps. (1) U. C. Dutt, Materia Medica of the Hindus, 1877, glossary, distinguishes Guduchi = Tinospora cordifolia from Sudarsana = 'Padma gulancha' = Tinospora tomentosa — a different species under a confusable vernacular. Dymock 1890-93 vol. I adds a third: "Tinospora crispa … possesses the bitterness and tonic properties of T. cordifolia, and is known by the same vernacular names." Same vernacular names, different species. (2) Rājanighaṇṭu 3.15-3.18 treats TWO guduchis — the vine and the tuber-borne 「kandodbhavā guḍūcī」 — and gives them DIFFERENT energetics (「kaṭūṣṇā」, pungent and hot, for the tuber-borne). Confirm which plant and which variety before carrying any of these values.

CONTRAINDICATIONS: I found NO classical contraindication stated for Guduchi in the Sanskrit sources examined. Its epithet 「amṛtā」 (nectar, the deathless) and its rasayana status point the other way. This is a genuine absence, not a search failure — but it was not exhaustively searched, and Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya (46 hits, not read) remains untested.

results.herb: Japanese Honeysuckle (Jin Yin Hua) — Lonicera japonica Thunb., flower bud
results.pre1900_finding: There are FOUR conflicting pre-1900 readings and the two oldest both go against 'Cold'. The Mingyi Bielu reading, transmitted verbatim in 1108 and again in 1596, is 甘温 — sweet and WARM. Chen Cangqi dissents inside the 1596 entry with 小寒 and calls the warm reading wrong. Wu Yiluo 1757 reads 甘平, NEUTRAL, and adds that its nature is so temperate it has no contraindications. Only Wang Ang 1694 gives 甘寒, cold — the sole pre-1900 warrant for the stored value. Per the standing rule I am not adjudicating: the stored 'Cold' is defensible but it is a minority reading, and the head reading of the two earliest texts is its opposite. SEPARATE FINDING: this herb is NOT in the Shennong Bencao Jing at all. The 忍冬 that appears there is Wu Pu's alias for 麥門冬 (Ophiopogon), not honeysuckle.
results.source_year: 1108 (Zhenglei Bencao) and 1596 (BCGM) for the warm head reading; 1694 (Ben Cao Bei Yao) for the cold reading; 1757 (Ben Cao Cong Xin) for neutral
results.evidence: Tang Shenwei 唐慎微, Zhenglei Bencao 證類本草 (Siku Quanshu recension), 卷07, 1108: 「忍冬味甘温無毒主寒熱身腫久服輕身長年益壽十二月採隂乾」 — Ren Dong: sweet, WARM, non-toxic. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/證類本草_(四庫全書本)/卷07 || Li Shizhen 李時珍, Bencao Gangmu 本草綱目 (Siku recension), 卷18下 草部·蔓草類, 1596 — entry headed 「{{SK anchor|忍冬}}{{SK notes|别錄上品}}」: 「氣味甘温無毒」 with the dissent attached: 「權曰辛藏器曰小寒云温者非也」 — Zhen Quan: acrid; Chen Cangqi: SLIGHTLY COLD, and those who say warm are wrong. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷18下 || Wu Yiluo 吳儀洛, Ben Cao Cong Xin 本草從新, 1757, 金銀花: 「除熱解毒。甘平。除熱解毒。補虚。…禀春氣以生。性极中和。故無禁忌。其藤葉名忍冬。」 — sweet, NEUTRAL. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新 || Wang Ang 汪昂, Ben Cao Bei Yao 本草備要, 1694, 金银花: reads 「甘寒入肺」 — sweet, COLD, entering the Lung. LOCATED ONLY, not quoted as the 1694 text: the Wikisource transcription is simplified with dropped glyphs. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草備要 || Negative check on the Shennong claim: Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan 孫星衍 recension, 1799, contains 忍冬 exactly once, inside the 麥門冬 entry — 「《吳普》曰：一名馬韭，一名舋冬，一名忍冬，一名忍陵，一名不死藥…」 — as an ALIAS OF OPHIOPOGON. Li Shizhen confirms the same alias at BCGM 卷16 釋名 麥門冬: 「忍冬{{SK notes|呉普}}」. There is no honeysuckle entry in the Shennong Bencao Jing.
additions: GRADE: 别錄上品 — UPPER grade, but of the MINGYI BIELU (Tao Hongjing, c. 500 CE), NOT the Shennong Bencao Jing. BCGM 1596 卷18下 heads it 「别錄上品」. The DB's primary citation for this row should not claim a Shennong grade. Upper grade is still the intended-for-prolonged-use class, and the Bielu indications endorse it explicitly: 「久服輕身長年益壽」 (long use lightens the body, lengthens years, increases lifespan) — which is coherent with a warm-to-neutral tonic reading and awkward for a cold detoxicant reading.

PART DISCIPLINE — the DB stores the FLOWER BUD, but the classical drug is the WHOLE VINE and the classical texts say the parts are interchangeable. Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 卷18下 發明: 「忍冬莖葉及花功用皆同」 — the stem, leaf and flower of Ren Dong are identical in function and use. Wang Ang 1694 concurs (located, not quoted): 花叶同功，花香尤佳. Wu Yiluo 1757: 「其藤葉名忍冬」. So the flower-bud-only drug 金銀花 is a late narrowing; the 1108 and 1596 temperature readings above belong to the VINE, and transferring them to the bud is an inference, not a citation.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, and one hard prohibition. Chen Ziming 陳自明, 外科精要, quoted BCGM 1596 卷18下 附方, 忍冬酒: 「用忍冬藤生取一把以葉入沙盆研爛…其藤只用五兩木槌槌損不可犯鐵」 — take a handful of FRESH vine, grind the leaves to a pulp IN AN EARTHENWARE BASIN; bruise the five liang of vine with a WOODEN MALLET, IT MUST NOT TOUCH IRON. Fresh over dried is stated outright, ibid.: 「如無生者只用乾者然力終不及生者效速」 (if fresh is unavailable use dried, but its strength never matches the speed of fresh). Wu Yiluo 1757 repeats: 「乾者不及生者力速」, and adds the forms 「酿酒代茶。熬膏竝妙」 (brewed as wine in place of tea; decocted to a paste, both excellent) and the dosing note 「須多用乃效」 (must be used in QUANTITY to be effective).

CONTRAINDICATIONS: explicitly NONE. Wu Yiluo, Ben Cao Cong Xin 1757: 「禀春氣以生。性极中和。故無禁忌。」 — it receives the qi of spring in its growth; its nature is extremely central and harmonious; THEREFORE THERE ARE NO PROHIBITIONS. This is a rare affirmative safety statement in a pre-1900 materia medica and is directly usable for a daily-herb product — but note it is made about a herb that the same author calls NEUTRAL, not cold.

ADULTERATION WARNING, still actionable. Wu Yiluo 1757: 「近今有以漆花僞銀花、爲祸最烈、漆花短小梗多、色黑不香爲異、亦易辨爾」 — lately lacquer-tree flower is passed off as honeysuckle flower, and the harm is most severe; lacquer flower is short and small with many stalks, black in colour and not fragrant, and is easy enough to tell apart.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS. 别錄 layer (BCGM 1596 卷18下): 「主治寒熱身腫久服輕身長年益壽」. Zhen Quan: 「治腹脹滿能止氣下澼」. Chen Cangqi: 「熱毒血痢水痢濃煎服」 (heat-toxin bloody dysentery and watery dysentery, taken as a strong decoction) — the pre-1900 warrant for the DB's damp-heat dysentery indication. Li Shizhen: 「治飛尸遁尸風尸沉尸尸注鬼擊一切風濕氣及諸腫毒癰疽疥癬楊梅諸惡瘡散熱解毒」. Note Li Shizhen's own historiographical remark, ibid. 發明: 「昔人稱其治風除脹解痢逐尸為要藥而後世不復知用後世稱其消腫散毒治瘡為要藥而昔人並未言及」 — the ancients called it essential for wind, distension, dysentery and corpse-possession, which later ages forgot; later ages call it essential for reducing swelling and resolving toxin, which the ancients never mentioned. The 'cooling detoxicant' identity the DB stores is, by Li Shizhen's own account, the LATE identity.

NO CHANNEL ENTRY (归经) is given in the BCGM 1596 entry. Wang Ang 1694 assigns 入肺 (enters the Lung) — located only, not quotable from the available transcription. The DB's 'Lung, Heart, and Stomach channels' has no pre-1900 warrant that I could find and should be treated as unsourced.

results.herb: Ophiopogon (Mai Men Dong, Dwarf Lilyturf) — Ophiopogon japonicus, dried root tuber
results.pre1900_finding: 氣味甘平無毒 — sweet, NEUTRAL, non-toxic is the head reading in both the Shennong layer (味甘，平) and BCGM 1596. 微寒 is real but it is a SUB-reading, printed as the Mingyi Bielu's dissent (别録曰微寒) and endorsed later by Li Gao (甘微苦微寒) and Wu Yiluo 1757 (微苦微寒). Against it, Li Dangzhi read 甘小温 — SLIGHTLY WARM. So the stored 'slightly cold' has genuine pre-1900 warrant, but calling it the classical reading is wrong: the 本經 assignment is neutral, and the ancient variant readings straddle it in both directions.
results.source_year: 1596 (BCGM); head reading corroborated in the 1799 Sun Xingyan recension of the c. 200 CE Shennong Bencao Jing; 微寒 sub-reading corroborated 1757
results.evidence: Li Shizhen 李時珍, Bencao Gangmu 本草綱目 (Siku Quanshu recension), 卷16 草部·隰草類, 1596 — entry headed 「{{SK anchor|麥門冬}}{{SK notes|本經上品}}」, qi-wei line: 「氣味甘平無毒」 with attached note 「别録曰微寒普曰神農岐伯甘平黄帝桐君雷公甘無毒李當之甘小温杲曰甘微苦微寒陽中微隂降也入手太隂經氣分之才曰地黄車前為之使惡款冬苦瓠苦芺畏苦參青蘘木耳伏石鍾乳」. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷16 || Shennong Bencao Jing 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan 孫星衍 recension, 1799: 「==麥門冬== 味甘，平。主心腹結氣，傷中、傷飽，胃絡脈絕，羸瘦短氣。久服，輕身、不老、不飢。生川谷及堤阪。」 with the Wu Pu variants: 「神農、岐伯：甘，平；黃帝、桐君、雷公：甘，無毒；李氏：甘，小溫；扁鵲：無毒。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) || Wu Yiluo 吳儀洛, Ben Cao Cong Xin 本草從新, 1757, 麥門冬: 「潤肺清心、瀉熱。味甘。微苦微寒。潤肺清心，瀉熱除煩。」 and 「性寒而潤。虚寒泄瀉者勿用。肥白而大者佳。去心。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 上品 (UPPER grade), the strongest daily-use warrant in this batch. BCGM 1596 卷16 heads it 「本經上品」, and the 本經 text itself licenses prolonged use: 「久服，輕身、不老、不飢」 (long use lightens the body, prevents ageing, prevents hunger). Tao Hongjing, BCGM 1596 卷16 主治: 「斷穀為要藥」 (an essential drug for abstaining from grain).

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经): Li Gao 李杲, quoted BCGM 1596 卷16: 「甘微苦微寒陽中微隂降也入手太隂經氣分」 — sweet, slightly bitter, slightly cold; slight yin within yang; DESCENDING; entering the Hand Taiyin LUNG channel at the QI level. Note qi level, not blood; and Lung only — the DB's Stomach and Heart attributions have no channel-entry warrant in this entry, only indication warrant.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — one MANDATORY step with a stated failure mode. Tao Hongjing 陶弘景, BCGM 1596 卷16 根脩治: 「凡用取肥大者湯澤抽去心不爾令人煩大抵一斤須减去四五兩也」 — always take the plump large ones, moisten with hot water and DRAW OUT THE CORE; IF YOU DO NOT, IT MAKES PEOPLE VEXED; from each catty about four or five liang must be discarded. Li Shizhen's method, ibid.: 「凡入湯液以滚水潤濕少頃抽去心或以瓦焙軟乗熱去心若入丸散須瓦焙熱即於風中吹冷如此三四次即易燥且不損藥力或以湯浸搗膏和藥亦可滋補藥則以酒浸擂之」 — for decoctions, moisten with boiling water and draw the core; for pills and powders, tile-roast hot then cool in a draught, three or four times, which dries it easily WITHOUT DESTROYING THE DRUG'S POWER; FOR TONIC PREPARATIONS, SOAK IN WINE AND GRIND. Wu Yiluo 1757 repeats the rule tersely: 「肥白而大者佳。去心。」

CONTRAINDICATIONS, and they are firm. Kou Zongshi 寇宗奭, BCGM 1596 卷16 發明: 「其味苦但専泄而不専收寒多人禁服」 — its taste is bitter, it only drains and does not gather; THOSE WITH MUCH COLD ARE FORBIDDEN TO TAKE IT. Li Shizhen, ibid.: 「此方惟火盛氣壯之人服之相宜若氣弱胃寒者必不可餌也」 — suitable only for those with exuberant fire and robust qi; THOSE OF WEAK QI AND COLD STOMACH MUST ABSOLUTELY NOT TAKE IT. Wu Yiluo 1757: 「性寒而潤。虚寒泄瀉者勿用。」 — cold and moistening in nature; DO NOT USE IN DEFICIENCY-COLD DIARRHOEA. Incompatibilities, BCGM 1596 卷16: 「地黄車前為之使惡款冬苦瓠苦芺畏苦參青蘘木耳伏石鍾乳」 — Rehmannia and Plantago are its envoys; it hates Tussilago, bitter gourd and Cirsium; it fears Sophora flavescens, sesame leaf and wood-ear; it subdues stalactite.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, 本經 layer (BCGM 1596 卷16): 「主治心腹結氣傷中傷飽胃絡脈絶羸瘦短氣久服輕身不老不饑」. 别録 layer: 「療身重目黄心下支滿虚勞客熱口亁燥渇止嘔吐愈痿蹷强隂益精消穀調中保神定肺氣安五臟令人肥健美顔色有子」. Zhang Yuansu adds the pre-1900 warrant for the DB's Lung-fire and blood indications: 「治肺中伏火補心氣不足主血妄行及經水枯乳汁不下」.

FORMULA DOCTRINE in pre-1900 words, supporting the DB's Sheng Mai San note. Zhang Yuansu, BCGM 1596 卷16 發明: 「麥門冬治肺中伏火脈氣欲絶者加五味子人参三味為生脈散補肺中元氣不足」 — for hidden fire in the Lung with the pulse-qi about to expire, add Schisandra and Ginseng, the three making SHENG MAI SAN. Li Gao explains the division of labour: 「人参之甘寒瀉熱火而益元氣麥門冬之苦寒滋燥金而清水源五味子之酸温瀉丙火而補庚金」. Kou Zongshi for the yin-and-blood pairing: 「與地黄阿膠麻仁同為潤經益血復脈通心之劑與五味子枸杞子同為生脈之劑」.

NOMENCLATURE TRAP worth recording in the DB: 忍冬 is a Wu Pu alias of MAI MEN DONG (BCGM 1596 卷16 釋名: 「忍冬{{SK notes|呉普}}」), and it is the ONLY 忍冬 in the Shennong Bencao Jing. A text search for 忍冬 in the Shennong classic returns Ophiopogon, not honeysuckle — the trap that would otherwise mis-source herb H180 in this same batch.

results.herb: Phellodendron (Amur Cork Tree, Huang Bai) — Phellodendron amurense, dried inner bark
results.pre1900_finding: 氣味苦寒無毒 — bitter, COLD, non-toxic (BCGM 1596 head reading), matching the Shennong layer exactly: 味苦，寒。 Zhang Yuansu inside the 1596 entry: 性寒味苦氣味俱厚沈而降陰也 (nature cold, taste bitter, qi and flavour both thick, sinking and descending, yin). Wang Ang 1694 concurs with 苦寒微辛. No pre-1900 dissent found. Stored value stands.
results.source_year: 1596 (BCGM); corroborated in the 1799 Sun Xingyan recension of the c. 200 CE Shennong Bencao Jing, and located in 1694 Ben Cao Bei Yao
results.evidence: Li Shizhen 李時珍, Bencao Gangmu 本草綱目 (Siku Quanshu recension), 卷35上 木部·喬木類, 1596 — entry headed 「{{SK anchor|蘗木}}{{SK notes|本經上品}}」, 釋名 「黄蘗{{SK notes|别錄}}根名檀桓」, qi-wei line: 「氣味苦寒無毒」 with attached note 「元素曰性寒味苦氣味俱厚沈而降陰也又云苦厚微辛隂中之陽入足少陰經為足太陽引經藥好古曰黄芩栀子入肺黄連入心黄蘗入腎燥濕所歸各從其類也…之才曰惡乾漆伏硫黄」. Li Shizhen also settles the orthography: 「俗作黄柏者省寫之謬也」. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷35上 || Shennong Bencao Jing 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan 孫星衍 recension, 1799, 檗木 (the heading glyph is a lacuna in this transcription, printed 「==木==」; the entry is identified by its alias 一名檀桓 and by the 案 note 「張揖云：檗木，可染者」): 「味苦，寒。主五臟、腸胃中結熱，黃膽，腸痔，止泄利，女子漏下赤白，陰陽蝕創，一名檀桓。生山谷。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) || Wang Ang 汪昂, Ben Cao Bei Yao 本草備要, 1694, 黄柏: reads 「苦寒微辛，沉阴下降」 — LOCATED ONLY, not quoted as the 1694 text (simplified transcription with dropped glyphs). https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草備要
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 上品 (UPPER grade) — and this one deserves a flag, because the grade and the Ming/Qing clinical warning point opposite ways. BCGM 1596 卷35上 heads it 「本經上品」 and the 别錄 indications even end 「久服通神」 (long use penetrates the spirit); yet Li Shizhen warns against exactly that long use (below). An upper-grade classification is NOT, for this herb, a licence for daily use.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经): 足少陰腎經, with 足太陽膀胱 as guided channel. Zhang Yuansu, BCGM 1596 卷35上: 「入足少陰經為足太陽引經藥」 — enters the Foot Shaoyin (KIDNEY) channel and is a GUIDING herb for the Foot Taiyang (Bladder). Wang Haogu gives the three-yellows channel map in one line, ibid.: 「黄芩栀子入肺黄連入心黄蘗入腎燥濕所歸各從其類也」 — Scutellaria and Gardenia enter the Lung, Coptis the Heart, Phellodendron the KIDNEY; each drying dampness according to its own class. This is the pre-1900 warrant for the DB's San Huang upper/middle/lower-burner scheme.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — and it confirms the DB's salt-frying note in Li Shizhen's own words. BCGM 1596 卷35上 修治, Li Shizhen: 「黄蘗性寒而沈生用則降實火熟用則不傷胃酒制則治上鹽制則治下蜜制則治中」 — cold and sinking; USED RAW it descends and drains EXCESS fire, USED COOKED it does not injure the stomach; WINE-processed treats the upper, SALT-processed treats the LOWER, HONEY-processed treats the middle. Zhang Yuansu's rule of degree, ibid.: 「二制治上焦單制治中焦不制治下焦也」 — doubly processed for the upper burner, singly for the middle, UNPROCESSED for the lower. Lei Xiao's honey method, ibid.: 「凡使蘗皮削去粗皮用生蜜水浸半日漉出晒乾用蜜塗文武火炙令蜜盡為度每五兩用蜜三兩」 — pare off the coarse outer bark, soak half a day in raw honey water, drain and sun-dry, coat with honey and roast over a moderate-then-fierce fire until the honey is spent; three liang of honey to every five liang of bark.

CONTRAINDICATIONS, unusually explicit and directly relevant to any long-term product. Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 卷35上 發明: 「然必少壯氣盛能食者用之相宜若中氣不足而邪火熾甚者久服則有寒中之變近時虚損及縱慾求嗣之人用補陰藥往往以此二味為君日日服餌降令太過脾胃受傷真陽暗損精氣不暖致生他病蓋不知此物苦寒而滑滲且苦味久服有反從火化之害故葉氏醫學統㫖有四物加知母黄蘗久服傷胃不能生陰之戒」 — suitable only for the young, strong, replete-qi and good-eating; where central qi is insufficient though evil fire blazes, LONG USE BRINGS ON COLD IN THE MIDDLE; people nowadays with depletion, or seeking offspring, TAKE IT DAILY as sovereign in yin-supplementing formulas, so that the descending order is overdone, the spleen and stomach are injured, the true yang is covertly lost and the essence-qi loses its warmth, generating other diseases — not knowing that this substance is bitter-cold AND slippery-draining, and that long use of bitterness carries the harm of paradoxically transforming into fire. Hence Ye's Yixue Tongzhi warns that Si Wu Tang plus Anemarrhena and Phellodendron, taken long, INJURES THE STOMACH AND CANNOT ENGENDER YIN. Incompatibilities, ibid.: 「之才曰惡乾漆伏硫黄」.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, 本經 layer (BCGM 1596 卷35上): 「主治五臟腸胃中結熱黄疸腸痔止洩痢女子漏下赤白隂傷蝕瘡」. 别錄 adds 「療驚氣在皮間肌膚熱赤起目熱赤痛口瘡久服通神」. Zhang Yuansu adds the lower-burner and Kidney indications: 「瀉膀胱相火補腎水不足堅腎壯骨髓療下焦虛諸痿癱瘓利下竅除熱」. Zhu Zhenheng gives the DB's Zhi Bai pairing in pre-1900 words: 「得知母滋隂降火得蒼术除濕清熱為治痿要藥得細辛瀉膀胱火治口舌生瘡」.

MINISTERIAL-FIRE DOCTRINE, quotable and precise. Zhu Zhenheng 朱震亨, BCGM 1596 卷35上 發明: 「火有二君火者人火也心火也可以濕伏可以水滅可以直折黄連之屬可以制之相火者天火也龍雷之火也陰火也不可以水濕折之當從其性而伏之惟黄蘗之屬可以降之」 — there are two fires: sovereign fire is human fire, Heart fire, subduable by damp, extinguishable by water, breakable head-on, and Coptis and its kind control it; MINISTERIAL fire is heaven's fire, dragon-and-thunder fire, YIN fire, which cannot be broken by water or damp but must be subdued by following its nature, and ONLY Phellodendron and its kind can bring it down. This is the exact pre-1900 basis for the DB's 'empty fire of spent Kidney water' framing.

SPECIES TRAP, visible inside the source itself. BCGM 1596 卷35上 carries 小蘗 (Berberis) as a SEPARATE appended entry immediately after Huang Bai, with a DIFFERENT assignment: 「氣味苦大寒無毒主治口瘡疳䘌殺諸蟲去心腹中熱氣」 — bitter, GREATLY cold. Chen Cangqi is quoted there confusing the two on bark colour, and Li Shizhen distinguishes them: 「小蘗山間時有之小樹也其皮外白裏黄狀如蘗皮而薄小」. This is the same Phellodendron/Berberis conflation that F. Porter Smith 1871 committed; do not let a Berberis reading enter a Huang Bai monograph.

results.herb: Pinellia (Ban Xia) — Pinellia ternata, processed rhizome
results.pre1900_finding: The temperature is PROCESSING-DEPENDENT, and the pre-1900 sources say so explicitly. The head reading is 辛平有毒 — acrid, NEUTRAL, TOXIC (BCGM 1596), matching the Shennong layer 味辛，平。 The Mingyi Bielu then splits it by preparation: 生微寒熟温 — RAW it is slightly cold, COOKED it is WARM — a formula transmitted verbatim in 1108 and again in 1596. Only from Zhang Yuansu onward does 溫 become the flat head reading (性温), which Wu Yiluo 1757 fixes as 辛溫. So the stored 'Warm' is correct FOR THE PROCESSED DRUG the DB actually stores, and wrong as an unqualified assignment. Given the DB's part_used already says 'processed only', this is a refinement of the reasoning, not a correction of the value.
results.source_year: 1596 (BCGM); the raw/cooked split corroborated 1108 (Zhenglei); neutral head reading corroborated in the 1799 Sun Xingyan recension of the c. 200 CE Shennong Bencao Jing; flat 辛溫 in 1757
results.evidence: Li Shizhen 李時珍, Bencao Gangmu 本草綱目 (Siku Quanshu recension), 卷17下 草部·毒草類, 1596 — entry headed 「{{SK anchor|半夏}}{{SK notes|本經下品}}」, qi-wei line: 「根氣味辛平有毒」 with attached note 「别録曰生微寒熟温生令人吐熟令人下湯洗盡滑用元素曰味辛苦性温氣味俱薄沉而降隂中陽也好古曰辛厚苦輕陽中隂也入手陽明太隂少隂三經」. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷17下 || Tang Shenwei 唐慎微, Zhenglei Bencao 證類本草 (Siku recension), 卷10, 1108: 「半夏味辛平生㣲寒熟温有毒主傷寒寒熱心下堅下氣喉咽腫痛頭[眩]胷脹欬逆腸鳴止汗…消癰腫墮胎療痿黄恱澤面目生令人吐熟令人下用之湯洗令滑盡」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/證類本草_(四庫全書本)/卷10 || Shennong Bencao Jing 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan 孫星衍 recension, 1799: 「==半夏== 味辛，平。主傷寒寒熱，心下堅，下氣，喉咽腫痛，頭眩胸脹，咳逆腸鳴，止汗。一名地文，一名水玉。生川谷。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) || Wu Yiluo 吳儀洛, Ben Cao Cong Xin 本草從新, 1757, 半夏: 「燥溼痰、宣通陰陽。辛溫。体滑性燥。能走能散。和胃健脾。除溼化痰。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 下品 (LOWER grade), the lowest duration class, and it comes with declared toxicity in every layer — 有毒 (BCGM 1596 and Zhenglei 1108), 有大毒 GREAT toxicity (Yaoxing Lun, quoted Zhenglei 1108). Lower grade encodes short, targeted courses under supervision. A daily-herb product should not carry Pinellia the way it carries an upper-grade herb.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经): Wang Haogu 王好古, quoted BCGM 1596 卷17下: 「辛厚苦輕陽中隂也入手陽明太隂少隂三經」 — acrid thick, bitter light, yin within yang; entering THREE channels, Hand Yangming (Large Intestine), Taiyin (Lung) and Shaoyin (Heart). He then splits the action by channel, ibid. 發明: 「止嘔吐為足陽明除痰為足太隂柴胡為之使故今柴胡湯中用之」 — stopping vomiting is Foot Yangming (Stomach), removing phlegm is Foot Taiyin (Spleen); Bupleurum is its envoy, hence its use in the Bupleurum decoctions.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — MANDATORY, with the failure mode named. Tao Hongjing 陶弘景, BCGM 1596 卷17下 修治: 「凡用以湯洗十許過令滑盡不爾有毒㦸人咽喉方中有半夏必須用生薑者以制其毒故也」 — in all use, wash with hot water some ten times until the slipperiness is entirely gone; IF NOT, IT IS TOXIC AND STABS THE THROAT; ANY FORMULA CONTAINING BAN XIA MUST USE FRESH GINGER, TO CONTROL ITS TOXICITY. Lei Xiao 雷斆, ibid.: 「修事半夏四兩用白芥子末二兩釅醋二兩攪濁将半夏投中洗三遍用之若洗涎不盡令人氣逆肝氣怒滿」 — four liang of Ban Xia to two liang of white mustard seed powder and two liang of strong vinegar, stirred cloudy, the Ban Xia thrown in and washed three times; IF THE DROOL IS NOT FULLY WASHED OUT IT CAUSES QI COUNTERFLOW AND ANGRY FULLNESS OF LIVER QI. The Yaoxing Lun, quoted Zhenglei 1108 卷10: 「有大毒湯淋十遍去涎方盡其毒以生薑等分制而用之」 — great toxicity; drench ten times with hot water to remove the drool and only then is the toxin spent; process with an EQUAL WEIGHT of fresh ginger.

THE THREE STANDARD FORMS, named in 1596 — this is where Jiang/Fa/Qing Ban Xia come from. Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 卷17下 修治: 「或研為末以薑汁入湯浸澄三日瀝去涎水晒乾用謂之半夏粉或研末以薑汁和作餅子日乾用謂之半夏餅或研末以薑汁白礬湯和作餅楮葉包置藍中待生黄衣日乾用謂之半夏麴」 — BAN XIA POWDER (ginger juice, three days' settling, drool poured off); BAN XIA CAKE (ginger juice, sun-dried); BAN XIA LEAVEN 半夏麴 (ginger juice and ALUM solution, wrapped in paper-mulberry leaves, set in a basket until a yellow coat grows, then sun-dried).

PHLEGM-TYPE-SPECIFIC LEAVENS — a whole doctrine the DB has no field for. Bai Feixia 白飛霞, Yitong, quoted BCGM 1596 卷17下: 「治濕痰以薑汁白礬湯和之治風痰以薑汁及皂莢煑汁和之治火痰以薑汁竹瀝或荆瀝和之治寒痰以薑汁[煎]湯入白芥子末和之此皆造麴妙法也」 — for DAMP phlegm blend with ginger juice and alum solution; for WIND phlegm with ginger juice and gleditsia decoction; for FIRE phlegm with ginger juice and bamboo or vitex sap; for COLD phlegm with ginger-juice decoction plus white mustard powder. Wu Yiluo 1757 expands this to eight named leavens including 皂角曲, 竹瀝曲, 麻油曲, 牛胆曲, 開郁曲, 硝黃曲, 海粉曲 and 霞天膏, each for a named phlegm type.

CONTRAINDICATIONS — the fullest set in this batch, and one is absolute. BCGM 1596 卷17下, note to the qi-wei line: 「射干為之使惡皂莢畏雄黄生薑乾薑秦皮龜甲反烏頭權曰柴胡為之使忌羊血海藻飴糖…多用則㵼脾胃諸血證及口渇者禁用為其燥津液也孕婦忌之用生薑則無害」 — Belamcanda is its envoy; it HATES gleditsia; it FEARS realgar, fresh ginger, dried ginger, Fraxinus bark and tortoise shell; it OPPOSES ACONITE (fan wu tou, one of the Eighteen Antagonisms); AVOID sheep's blood, Sargassum and malt sugar; USED IN QUANTITY IT DRAINS THE SPLEEN AND STOMACH; FORBIDDEN in all BLOOD disorders and in THIRST, because it dries the fluids; PREGNANT WOMEN MUST AVOID IT, though with fresh ginger there is no harm. Note Zhenglei 1108 卷10 files Aconite under 畏 rather than 反: 「畏雄黄生薑乾薑秦皮龜甲及烏頭」 — a real 1108-vs-1596 divergence in the antagonism class, worth recording rather than smoothing. Separately, the 别錄 lists 墮胎 (CAUSES ABORTION) among its actions, in both 1108 and 1596 — the pregnancy prohibition is an action statement, not merely a caution.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, 本經 layer (BCGM 1596 卷17下): 「主治傷寒寒熱心下堅胷脹欬逆頭[眩]咽喉腫痛腸鳴下氣止汗」. 别録 adds 「消心腹胸膈痰熱滿結欬嗽上氣心下急痛堅痞時氣嘔逆消癰腫療痿黄悦澤面目墮胎」. Zhang Yuansu adds the cold-phlegm picture the DB stores: 「治寒痰及形寒飲冷傷肺而欬消胸中痞膈上痰除胸寒和胃氣燥脾濕治痰厥頭痛消腫散結」. Li Shizhen adds 「除腹脹目不得瞑白濁夢遺帶下」.

A DIRECT CHALLENGE TO THE 'DRY' MOISTURE VALUE, from Li Shizhen himself. BCGM 1596 卷17下 發明: 「半夏能主痰飲及腹脹者為其體滑而味辛性温也涎滑能潤辛温能散亦能潤故行濕而通大便利竅而泄小便…世俗皆以南星半夏為性燥誤矣濕去則土燥痰涎不生非二物之性燥也」 — its body is SLIPPERY and its taste acrid and nature warm; the slippery drool can MOISTEN, and acrid-warm can disperse and also moisten, hence it moves damp and frees the stool, opens the orifices and drains urine… THE WORLD ALL TAKES NAN XING AND BAN XIA TO BE DRYING BY NATURE, AND THIS IS AN ERROR: when damp is gone the earth is dry and phlegm-drool is not engendered — the dryness is not the nature of these two substances. Wu Yiluo 1757 preserves the same tension in four characters: 「体滑性燥」 (body slippery, nature drying). The DB's flat 'Dry' is the folk reading Li Shizhen explicitly rejects.

SUBSTITUTION WARNING: Wang Ji 汪機, BCGM 1596 卷17下 發明: 「俗以半夏性燥有毒多以貝母代之貝母乃太隂脾經之藥半夏乃太隂脾經陽明胃經之藥何可代也」 — people substitute Fritillaria for Pinellia because the latter is drying and toxic, but Fritillaria is a Taiyin Spleen drug while Pinellia is a Taiyin Spleen AND Yangming Stomach drug; they are not interchangeable. He then lists the cases where Fritillaria is right and 「半夏乃禁用之藥」 (Pinellia is a forbidden drug): cough with blood, consumptive blood loss, sore throat, throat closure, lung abscess, lung atrophy, and difficult lactation.

results.stored_temperature: Neutral. Classically balanced (ping), neither warming nor cooling, so Fu Ling can be added to hot and cold formulas alike.
results.pre1900_finding: 氣味甘平無毒 — sweet, NEUTRAL (平), non-toxic. Identical in the Han-layer text (味甘，平) and in Li Shizhen 1596. The 伏神 (Fu Shen) portion carries its own, identical line: 伏神氣味甘平無毒. No pre-1900 dissent found on the thermal value.

results.evidence: Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (Bencao Gangmu), 卷三十七 木之四 寓木類, entry 茯苓, Siku Quanshu recension, 1596: 「{{SK anchor|茯苓}}{{SK notes|本經上品}}」… 「{{SK anchor|氣味甘平無毒}}」… 「{{SK anchor|伏神氣味甘平無毒}}」. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷37 — Ancient layer, Sun Xingyan & Sun Fengyi recension of the 神農本草經 (Shennong Bencao Jing), 1799, 卷一·上經 (the entry heading is missing in this recension; located by its alias string 一名茯菟): 「味甘，平。主胸脅逆氣（《御覽》作疝氣），憂恚，驚邪，悸心下結痛，寒熱煩滿咳逆，口焦舌乾，利小便。久服，安魂、養神，不飢、延年。一名茯菟」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) — variant readings preserved in the same place: 「《吳普》曰：茯苓通神，桐君：甘；雷公、扁鵲：甘，無毒。」
additions: SHENNONG GRADE — 上品 (upper/superior), stated explicitly in the BCGM head note 「茯苓{{SK notes|本經上品}}」 and confirmed by its position in 卷一·上經 of Sun Xingyan 1799. The DB's claim of superior-grade listing is verified. Upper grade sanctions sustained daily use; the Ben Jing itself says 久服，安魂、養神，不飢、延年 (long use settles the hun, nourishes the shen, staves off hunger, prolongs years).

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), and it is PART-SPECIFIC — 好古曰：白者入手太隂足太陽經氣分，赤者入足太隂手少隂太陽氣分 (Wang Haogu: WHITE Poria enters the qi aspect of the hand-taiyin/Lung and foot-taiyang/Bladder channels; RED Poria enters foot-taiyin/Spleen, hand-shaoyin/Heart and taiyang). 杲曰：白者入壬癸，赤者入丙丁. The DB has no channel column and does not separate Bai Fu Ling from Chi Fu Ling energetically.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, with a safety reason attached — 修治：斆曰凡用皮去心，搗細，于水盆中攪濁，浮者濾去之，此是茯苓赤筋，若誤服餌，令人瞳子并黑睛㸃小，兼盲目 (Lei Xiao: peel and de-core, pound fine, stir in a basin of water and filter off the floating turbid matter — that is Poria's red fibre; taken by mistake it shrinks the pupil and the black of the eye, and blinds). 𢎞景曰：作丸散者先煮二三沸乃切暴乾用.

CONTRAINDICATIONS AND INCOMPATIBILITIES, classically stated — 忌米醋及酸物 (avoid rice vinegar and sour things); 惡白斂，畏牡䝉、地榆、雄黄、秦芃、鱉甲; 元素曰：如小便利或數者多服則損人目，汗多人服之亦損元氣 (in free or frequent urination, heavy dosing injures the eyes; in a heavily sweating person it drains the yuan qi); 震亨曰：若隂虛者恐未為宜…此物有行水之功，久服損人 (Zhu Danxi: not suitable in yin deficiency; long use harms). None of this is in the DB row, which presents Fu Ling as broadly safe and universally combinable.
CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom — 本經: 胸脇逆氣，憂恚，驚邪恐悸，心下結痛，寒熱煩滿欬逆，口焦舌乾，利小便. 别録 adds 止消渴好睡，大腹淋瀝，膈中痰水，水腫淋結，開胸腑，調臟氣，伐腎邪，長隂益氣力，保神氣.

A DOCTRINAL DISPUTE the DB flattens — 陶弘景/張元素 hold 白補赤瀉 (white supplements, red drains); 李時珍 rejects the fire/water channel split and rules 赤入血分，白入氣分 (red enters the blood aspect, white the qi aspect), 「不當以丙丁壬癸分也」.

results.pre1900_finding: Temperature CONFIRMED as neutral, but the classical reading is PART-SPECIFIC and the DB has merged two different values. The head line 酸棗氣味酸平無毒 is the FRUIT: sour, neutral. Li Shizhen states separately that the KERNEL is different: 時珍曰仁味甘氣平 — the kernel is sweet in flavour, NEUTRAL in qi. A dissent is printed alongside: 宗奭曰微熱 (Kou Zongshi: slightly WARM). The DB's blended taste 'sweet and sour' collapses the fruit's 酸 and the kernel's 甘 into one row for a herb whose stated part is the kernel alone.

results.evidence: Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (Bencao Gangmu), 卷三十六 木之三 灌木類, entry 酸棗, Siku Quanshu recension, 1596: 「{{SK anchor|酸棗}}{{SK notes|本經上品}}」… 「{{SK anchor|酸棗氣味酸平無毒}}{{SK notes|宗奭曰微熱　時珍曰仁味甘氣平　斆曰用仁以葉拌蒸半日去皮尖　之才曰惡防己}}」. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷36 — Ancient layer, 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan & Sun Fengyi recension, 1799, 卷一·上經, ==酸棗==: 「味酸，平。主心腹寒熱，邪結氣聚，四肢酸疼，濕痹。久服，安五臟，輕身、延年。生川澤。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍)
additions: SHENNONG GRADE — 上品 (upper), per the BCGM head note 「酸棗{{SK notes|本經上品}}」 and its placement in 卷一·上經 of Sun Xingyan 1799. The DB's claim is verified.

CHANNEL ENTRY, and it CONTRADICTS the DB's framing — 時珍曰：…其仁甘而潤，故熟用療膽虚不得眠、煩渴、虚汗之證；生用療膽熱好眠，皆足厥隂少陽藥也。今人專以為心家藥，殊昧此理 (Li Shizhen: both raw and roasted are foot-JUEYIN/Liver and SHAOYANG/Gallbladder medicines; 'people today treat it exclusively as a Heart-family medicine, quite missing this principle'). The DB row is built on Heart-and-Liver blood deficiency and on Heart shen; Li Shizhen in 1596 names the Gallbladder, not the Heart.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — RAW AND ROASTED DO OPPOSITE THINGS, which the DB's single 'traditionally crushed and dry-fried' note obscures. 志曰按五代史後唐刋石藥騐云：酸棗仁睡多生使，不得睡炒熟 (for excessive sleep use it RAW; for sleeplessness roast it). 時珍: 熟用療膽虚不得眠…生用療膽熱好眠. Also 斆曰用仁以葉拌蒸半日，去皮尖 (Lei Xiao: steam the kernel with the leaves half a day, then remove skin and tip).

A FRUIT/KERNEL INVERSION recorded as a live 16th-century problem — 𢎞景曰：東人噉之以醒睡，與經文療不得眠正相反 (Tao Hongjing: easterners eat the fruit to stay awake, exactly the reverse of what the classic says); 恭曰：本經用實療不得眠，不用言仁，今方皆用仁 (Su Gong: the Ben Jing used the FRUIT, and said nothing of the kernel; present formulas all use the kernel). The Shennong upper-grade pedigree the DB cites therefore attaches to the fruit, not to the seed the product would sell.
CONTRAINDICATION / INCOMPATIBILITY — 之才曰惡防己 (Xu Zhicai: antagonised by Fang Ji, Stephania). Not in the DB row.
CLASSICAL INDICATIONS — 本經: 心腹寒熱，邪結氣聚，四肢酸疼，濕痹；久服安五臟，輕身延年. 别錄: 煩心不得眠，臍上下痛，血轉，久洩，虚汗，煩渴，補中，益肝氣，堅筋骨，助隂氣，能令人肥健. 甄權: 筋骨風，炒仁研湯服.

BOTANICAL DISPUTE worth carrying — the BCGM 集解 records a running argument over whether 酸棗 is a sour large jujube, the 棘 (thorn shrub) fruit, or a distinct tree; 宗奭 resolves it as one plant at two sizes: 小則為棘，大則為酸棗…其實一本也, and notes 科小者氣味薄，木大者氣味厚 (small plants give thin qi-and-flavour, large trees thick).

additions: SHENNONG GRADE — 上品 (upper), per 「芎藭{{SK notes|本經上品}}」 and its position in 卷一·上經 of Sun Xingyan 1799. The DB cites the Shennong Bencao Jing but records no grade; this is new.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经) — 元素曰：…少陽本經引經藥，入手足厥隂氣分 (Zhang Yuansu: it is the channel-conducting herb for the shaoyang benjing, and enters the qi aspect of the hand and foot jueyin, i.e. Pericardium and Liver). Li Gao's headache channel-guide rule sits in the same entry: 頭痛必用川芎，如不愈加各引經藥，太陽羗活，陽明白芷，少陽柴胡，太隂蒼术，厥隂吳茱茰，少隂細辛.

THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING FOR A DAILY-HERB PRODUCT — an explicit classical prohibition on long or solo use, which the DB row does not carry at all. 宗奭曰：沈栝《筆談》云，一族子舊服芎藭，醫鄭叔見之云：芎藭不可久服，多令人暴死…又朝士張子通之妻病腦風，服芎藭甚久，一日暴亡，皆目見者。此皆単服既久則走散真氣；若使他藥佐使，又不久服，中病便已，則焉能至此哉 (must not be taken long; taken alone and long it scatters the true qi — with assistant herbs, and stopped once the illness yields, no such harm). 虞摶曰：骨蒸多汗及氣弱之人不可久服，其性辛散，令真氣走洩而隂愈虚也 (steaming-bone heat with copious sweat, and qi-weak people, must not take it long). 時珍: 若単服既久，則辛喜歸肺，肺氣偏勝，金来賊木，肝必受邪，久則偏絶，豈不夭亡.
PAIRING AND INCOMPATIBILITY DOCTRINE — 之才曰：白芷為之使，畏黄連，伏雌黄；得細辛療金瘡止痛，得牡蠣療頭風吐逆.
CLASSICAL INDICATIONS — 本經: 中風入腦頭痛，寒痺，筋攣緩急，金瘡，婦人血閉無子. 别録: 除腦中冷動，面上遊風去来，目淚出多涕唾，忽忽如醉，諸寒冷氣，心腹堅痛，中惡卒急腫痛，脇風痛，温中内寒. 時珍 adds 燥濕，止瀉痢，行氣開鬱 — and gives a working note: 予治濕瀉每加二味（麥麴、鞠藭），其應如響.
LI SHIZHEN'S ONE-LINE ENERGETIC DEFINITION, better than any modern paraphrase — 芎藭，血中氣藥也。肝苦急，以辛補之，故血虚者宜之；辛以散之，故氣鬱者宜之 ('a qi medicine within the blood').

REGIONAL GRADE NAMES, which bear on sourcing — 其出關中者呼為京芎，亦曰西芎；出蜀中者為川芎；出天台者為台芎；出江南者為撫芎，皆因地而名也. Note for species discipline: the pre-1900 identification is by drug-name continuity (芎藭 → 川芎, the Sichuan-grown form), not by a Linnaean binomial; Ligusticum chuanxiong is a modern name applied to that cultivated stock.

results.pre1900_finding: 术（白术也）氣味甘温無毒 — White Atractylodes is sweet, WARM, non-toxic. Companion line for the other zhu: 蒼术…氣味苦温無毒 (Cang Zhu bitter, warm). Both warm, so the DB temperature holds either way. Refinement on taste and pedigree: the Han-layer text knows only an undivided 術 and reads it 味苦，溫 (BITTER, warm) — the 甘 (sweet) in the DB's 'Bitter and Sweet' is a post-Song attribution to the white form, not a Shennong reading.

A PEDIGREE PROBLEM THE DB INHERITS SILENTLY, structurally identical to the Gou Qi Zi case. Li Shizhen states plainly that the classic did not distinguish the two atractylodes: 古方及本經止言术，不分蒼白二種 (Kou Zongshi) and 昔人用术不分赤白，自宋以来始言蒼术苦辛氣烈、白术苦甘氣和，各自施用 (Li Shizhen: the split dates only from the Song). A Bai Zhu monograph citing the Shennong Bencao Jing is therefore citing a head-reading (苦溫, bitter-warm) that was never specific to the white form.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), six channels — 好古曰：入手太陽、少隂，足太隂、陽明、少隂、厥隂六經 (Small Intestine and Heart; Spleen, Stomach, Kidney and Liver). For Cang Zhu, separately: 入足太隂陽明手太隂陽明太陽之經. Also 杲曰：味苦而甘，性温，味厚氣薄，陽中隂也，可升可降 (thick flavour, thin qi; yin within yang; can ascend or descend).

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, and it is unusual enough to be worth quoting whole — 嘉謨曰：咀後人乳汁潤之，制其性也；脾病以陳壁土炒，遇竊土氣以助脾也 (Chen Jiamo: after cutting, moisten with human breast milk to temper its nature; in Spleen disease dry-fry with aged wall-earth, borrowing the earth qi to aid the Spleen). For Cang Zhu the doctrine differs: 時珍曰蒼术性燥，故以糯米泔浸去其油，切片焙乾用；亦有用脂麻同炒以制其燥者.
DIETARY CONTRAINDICATIONS, absent from the DB — 權曰：忌桃李、菘菜、雀肉、青魚 (Zhen Quan: avoid peach, plum, Chinese cabbage, sparrow flesh, black carp). Pairing: 之才曰：防風、地榆為之使.

ZHANG YUANSU'S NINE USES, a compact classical indication list — 白术除濕益燥，和中補氣，其用有九：温中一也；去脾胃中濕二也；除胃中熱三也；强脾胃進飲食四也；和胃生津液五也；止肌熱六也；四肢困倦嗜卧、目不能開、不思飲食七也；止渇八也；安胎九也. Wang Haogu's rule for sweating: 無汗則發，有汗則止 (in the absence of sweat it releases, in its presence it stops it) — which grounds the DB's Yu Ping Feng San / spontaneous-sweating claim in a 1596 text.
A FORMULA-LEVEL DISTINCTION the DB does not make — 杲曰：蒼术…能除濕下安太隂，使邪氣不傳入脾也；以其經泔浸火炒，故能出汗，與白术止汗特異，用者不可以此代彼 (Cang Zhu promotes sweating, Bai Zhu stops it; they must not be substituted for one another).

results.stored_temperature: Warm (Ayurvedic virya: ushna). The tannic astringency reads as cooling to the touch, yet the operative potency is warming and drying, which is why it reduces cold, damp kapha.
results.pre1900_finding: uṣṇavīryaṃ himasparśaṃ — HOT IN VIRYA, THOUGH COLD TO THE TOUCH. The classical text states in so many words the exact paradox the DB row narrates, and states it as doctrine rather than as inference. RASA — the DB records astringent with a bitter note. The Bhāvaprakāśa gives kaṣāya alone; the Rājanighaṇṭu gives kaṭus tiktaḥ kaṣāya, i.e. three rasas including PUNGENT. The pungent is not in the DB.

PART DISCIPLINE, with the classical reason — the fruit rind and the kernel are separate drugs with separate energetics. vibhītamajjā (the kernel) is laghu, kaṣāya, removes thirst, vomiting, kapha and vāta, and is MADAKṚT — intoxicating. Dutt 1877 and Dymock 1891 both render this 'narcotic'. The DB correctly restricts the drug to the rind; this is the pre-1900 grounds for that restriction.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE (Dutt 1877, from the Sanskrit formularies): 'Belleric myrobalans are fried in clarified butter; they are then covered with a paste of wheat-flour and slightly roasted on a fire. The cortical portion of the fruits thus prepared, is recommended to be kept in the mouth for the relief of sore throat, cough and catarrh.' Also given with rock salt and long pepper, rubbed into a paste with butter-milk, as a linctus for hoarseness.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's idiom — bhedana (breaking/purgative), kāsanāśana (cough), netrahita / cakṣuṣya (eye-benefiting), keśya (hair), palitaghna (destroys greying), kṛmi-vaisvarya-nāśana (worms and hoarseness), kapha-pitta-nut.

Dymock 1891 records the practical consequence: the tree 'is avoided by the Hindus of Northern India, who will not sit in its shade, as it is supposed to be inhabited by demons.'

CHINESE CHANNEL ENTRY (归经) for the same heartwood — 元素曰：陽中微陰，入手太陰、足少陰，通行陽明經 (Zhang Yuansu: slight yin within yang; enters hand-taiyin/Lung and foot-shaoyin/Kidney, and passes through the yangming). 杲曰：白檀調氣，引芳香之物上至極髙之分…為理氣要藥.

CHINESE GRADE, and it bears directly on a daily-use product — 别録下品, LOWER grade of the Mingyi Bielu. Sandalwood is absent from the Shennong Bencao Jing entirely. Lower grade in the classical scheme means short, targeted, disease-directed use, not sustained daily use.

THE CROSS-TRADITION CONTRADICTION, now verifiable rather than asserted — the DB row states this divergence but sources it to Bensky. The 1596 original says it directly: white sandal 辛温 (acrid, warm), red sandal 鹹微寒 (salty, slightly cold), and Li Shizhen assigns them to different aspects (白檀…氣分之藥也；紫檀…血分之藥也). Note the inversion against Ayurveda, where BOTH sandalwoods are śīta. This is a genuine two-tradition conflict on one species and should not be adjudicated in the row.

PREPARATION AND GRADING DOCTRINE — Bhāvaprakāśa 12 gives the acceptance criteria for the best drug: bitter in taste, yellow when rubbed, red at the cut, white in the body, with knots and hollows. Rājanighaṇṭu 12.10-13 distinguishes beṭṭa (cut while still moist, 'beṭṭacandanam atīva śītalaṃ' — extremely cooling) from sukvaḍi (self-dried), and 12.13 notes the moist form is used in lepa (external paste), the dry form otherwise. Bhāvaprakāśa 20: all sandalwoods are alike in rasa; the difference is fragrance.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS — Bhāvaprakāśa: śrama (fatigue), śoṣa (wasting), viṣa (poison), kapha, tṛṣṇā (thirst), pitta, asra (blood disorder), dāha (burning). Rājanighaṇṭu adds bhrānti (giddiness), vami (vomiting), jvara, krimi, saṃtāpa; vṛṣya (aphrodisiac) and, applied, it 'spreads lustre (kānti) over the body'. Chinese: 消風熱腫毒；止心腹痛、霍亂、腎氣痛；散冷氣，引胃氣上升，進飲食；噎膈吐食.

A CONTRADICTION WITHIN THE DB'S OWN LOGIC — the row assigns vṛṣya/aphrodisiac-adjacent Ayurvedic material no place, while the Unani reading Dymock quotes calls it ANTAPHRODISIAC. The two pre-1900 traditions disagree on this too (Rājanighaṇṭu 12.8: vṛṣyaṃ).

RASA CORRECTION — tikta + kaṭu. Astringent (kaṣāya) is not in the Rājanighaṇṭu verse. The DB's 'Bitter (Tikta) and Astringent (Kashaya), the two classical rasas' overstates its warrant.

SIXTEEN CLASSICAL NAMES (Rājanighaṇṭu 6.47-48), one of which is a whole doctrine in a word — bhiṣaṅmātā, 'mother of physicians'. Also vāsaka, vāsā, siṃhikā, vasādanī, āṭarūṣa, siṃhamukhī 'lion-mouthed', siṃhī, kaṇṭhīravī, vṛṣa, śitaparṇī, vājidantā, nāsā, pañcamukhī, siṃhaparṇī, mṛgendrāṇī. Dymock 1893 independently confirms Vasaka, Vansa, Vrisha, Sinha-mukhi, Sinha-parni, Atarusha.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's idiom — kāsaghnī (cough-destroying), raktapittajit (conquers raktapitta, the classical heat-driven bleeding syndrome), and it removes kāmalā (jaundice), kapha, vaikalya, jvara (fever), śvāsa (dyspnoea/asthma), kṣaya (consumption). The DB's 'Lung Heat and the Heat that drives reckless bleeding' mapping is a fair rendering of raktapittajit; the JAUNDICE indication is classical and missing from the DB.

PREPARATION AND VEHICLE DOCTRINE (Dutt 1877, from Śārṅgadhara and the Bhāvaprakāśa) — 'The fresh juice or decoction of the leaves in doses of one tolá, is given with the addition of honey and long pepper in cough.' Vāsāvaleha (electuary): juice of vāsaka leaves four seers, white sugar one seer, long pepper sixteen tolás, clarified butter sixteen tolás, boiled to the consistence of an extract; 'when cool add honey one seer'. The honey is added OFF the heat — a preparation rule with a reason behind it. Also a ghṛta made with the decoction and a root paste, for phthisis, and Vāsāchandanádi taila for external use.

PART DISCIPLINE — the DB gives leaf primarily. Pre-1900 sources make the ROOT co-equal: Dutt's compound decoctions are built on vāsaka ROOT, and Dymock 1893 records the Makhzan-el-Adwiya assigning distinct offices to each part — 'the flowers are useful in hectic, heat of blood, and gonorrhoea, the root in cough, asthma, febrile disturbances'. The flower is a separate drug in the Unani reading.
NO CLASSICAL CONTRAINDICATION FOUND — I looked and did not find one in the pre-1900 sources reached. Record that as an absence, not as safety.

additions: MOISTURE CONFIRMED FROM A PRE-1900 SOURCE — Dymock 1891 reports the Nighaṇṭas as 'bitter, pungent, hot, AND DRY'. The DB's Dry (rūkṣa guṇa) claim, which it currently sources to the modern Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia, now has an 1891 witness naming Eclipta alba.

THE RASAYANA CLAIM IS VARIETY-SPECIFIC, and the DB does not say so — Rājanighaṇṭu 6.5 states 'bhṛṅgarājas tridhā mataḥ', three kinds are recognised, and 6.137-139 name them: the ordinary/dark (mārkava, keśarañjana, pitṛpriya, keśya, kuntalavardhana), a YELLOW one (pīta, svarṇabhṛṅgāra, harivāsa, haripriya, devapriya), and a BLUE-BLACK one (nīla, mahānīla, mahābhṛṅga, nīlapuṣpa, śyāmala). Verse 6.140 then says 'tatra nīlo rasāyanaḥ' — only the DARK one is the rasāyana. The DB's 'rasayana king of hair' framing attaches, in the classical source, to one variety of three.

SPECIES FLAG, and it needs a founder decision — the DB names Eclipta prostrata. Dutt 1877 assigns the Sanskrit name Bhringaraja principally to WEDELIA CALENDULACEA and reserves Kesaraja for Eclipta alba (= E. prostrata), and states outright that Wedelia 'is the plant used in medicine at present'. Dymock 1891 records the confusion running the other way and treats Wedelia as a variety of Eclipta. So the pre-1900 record does not cleanly separate the two plants, and the strongest hair-oil formulas Dutt prints are specified with Wedelia. A monograph on Eclipta prostrata is defensible but should carry the ambiguity, not hide it.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's idiom — cakṣuṣya (eye-benefiting), keśarañjana (hair-dyeing/darkening), keśya and kuntalavardhana (hair-promoting, hair-increasing), kapha-śopha-viṣa-ghna (destroys phlegm, swelling and poison). Dymock 1891 adds, from practice, 'principally used as a tonic and deobstruent in hepatic and splenic enlargements, and in various chronic skin diseases', and from the Nighaṇṭas 'removing phlegm and wind, increasing the appetite, and curing diseases of the skin, eye and head'. The APPETITE and WIND (vāta) indications are classical and absent from the DB.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — the operative internal form is the FRESH LEAF JUICE (svarasa) used as a bhāvanā liquid, e.g. Dutt 1877: pills are made by soaking mineral preparations 'in the juice of Eclipta prostrata (kesarájá)'. The signature external form, in Dutt's own words: 'Bhringarája taila. Take of sesamum oil four seers, juice of bhringarája leaves, sixteen seers, iron rust, the three myrobalans and the root of Ichnocarpus frutescens (syámalatá), reduced to a paste, in all one seer, and prepare an oil in the usual way. This oil is said to remove scurf from the head, turn grey hairs black and cure alopecia.' Note the 16:4 juice-to-oil ratio and the iron rust — the classical oil is not a simple infusion. Shadbindu taila is a NASYA: 'Six drops of this oil, drawn in through the nostrils, are said to relieve headache and other affections of the head.'

AN EXTERNAL-USE CAUTION IMPLICIT IN THE RECORD — Dutt 1877 quotes the tattooing use: 'In tattooing the natives after puncturing the skin, rub the juicy green leaves of Eclipta prostrata over the part; which gives the desired indelible colour, namely a deep bluish black.' Dymock 1891 confirms 'the juice of the plant is used in tatooing to communicate a blue colour to the punctures'. A permanent dye on broken skin is worth surfacing for any topical product.
NO CLASSICAL CONTRAINDICATION FOUND in the pre-1900 sources reached. Record as an absence, not as safety.

VIPAKA: NOT STATED in any pre-1900 source reached. The DB's 'madhura vipaka' is unsupported by the Bhavaprakasha entry, which gives rasa and virya but no paka for this herb. Flag as unverified.

additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 上品 UPPER GRADE. BCGM 1596 heads the entry '茜草【本經上品】'; the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension places 茜根 in 卷一·上經. Upper grade = the long-duration, daily-use class, and the classic says so: '久服益精氣輕身' (long use benefits essence-qi and lightens the body). BUT Li Shizhen flags a head-on conflict in the tradition and refuses to resolve it: '名醫别錄言其久服益精氣輕身，日華子言其泄精，殊不相合，恐未可憑' — the Bielu says long use augments essence, Rihuazi says it DRAINS essence; the two do not agree and may not be relied on. Directly load-bearing for a product recommending daily herbs.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经): 手足厥陰血分 — the hand and foot Jueyin blood level, i.e. LIVER and PERICARDIUM. Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596. Ben Cao Cong Xin 1757 prints it as '入厥陰血分（心包、肝）'. The DB's TCM text names only the Liver channel; the Pericardium is missing.

PART DISCIPLINE: the 名醫別錄 assigns the ABOVE-GROUND vine-root (苗根) a different value entirely — '別錄曰苗根鹹平無毒' (salty, NEUTRAL, non-toxic) — against 苦寒 for the root. Root and vine are not the same drug. The DB's part_used is root and rhizome, so the 苦寒 head-reading is the right one to inherit, but the split should be recorded.

GUNA: गुरु (guru, HEAVY) per Bhavaprakasha 2.191. The DB stores moisture 'Dry. The bitter and astringent tastes dry the fluids' — that is a derivation, not a classical statement, and the only classical guna reached says heavy.

RASA: BPN gives मधुरा तिक्ता कषाया (sweet, bitter, astringent) — matches the DB exactly. The Chinese texts print five competing flavours in one entry: 苦 (head), 甘 (Zhen Quan), 酸 (Da Ming), 微酸鹹 (Zhang Yuansu). BCGM notes Da Ming's rider: '酸，入藥炒用' — sour, and to be DRY-FRIED before use.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE: Lei Xiao in BCGM 1596 — '凡使用銅刀於槐砧上剉，日乾，勿犯鉛鐵氣' — cut with a COPPER knife on a locust-wood block, sun-dry, and never let it touch lead or iron. Ben Cao Cong Xin 1757 repeats: '忌鐵'. The DB records nothing about metal contact.

CONTRAINDICATION: Ben Cao Cong Xin 1757 — '無瘀滯者忌投' (do not give where there is no blood stasis). BCGM 1596 — '之才曰畏鼠姑' (fears Shu Gu). Dymock 1891 records a dose-toxicity warning from Playfair's translation of the Talif-i-sharif: about 3 drachms several times daily 'powerfully affects the nervous system, inducing temporary delirium, &c., with evident determination to the uterine system.'

ADULTERANT WARNING (BCGM 1596): '勿用赤柳草根，真相似，只是味酸濇，誤服令人患内障眼，速服甘草水止之，即毒氣散' — a red-willow root looks identical but tastes sour-astringent; taken by mistake it causes cataract, to be checked at once with licorice water.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, Chinese: 本經 — '主寒濕風痹，黃疸，補中'; 別錄 — '止血，內崩下血，膀胱不足，踒跌，蠱毒'; 時珍 — '通經脈，治骨節風痛，活血行血'. Sanskrit (BPN 2.190-191): स्वरवर्णकृत् (improves the VOICE and the complexion — the DB has complexion but not voice), विष (poison), श्लेष्म, शोथ (swelling), योनि-अक्षि-कर्ण-रुक् (disease of the vulva, EYE and EAR), रक्तातीसार (bloody diarrhoea), कुष्ठ, अस्र, विसर्प (erysipelas), व्रण, मेह.

FOUNDER DECISION NEEDED: this herb has four pre-1900 temperature readings (ushna / han / wen / [vine] ping) and the DB's cited primary source says the opposite of the stored value. It sits alongside the 枸杞子 case already flagged in project memory. The DB needs a way to represent a contested temperature rather than collapsing it.

Dymock 1891 independently reports the nighantas as 'bitter, pungent, hot, astringent, appetizing and light'. Two independent pre-1900 lines agree on both temperature and moisture.

additions: GUNA, stated explicitly in the 16th-c. Sanskrit and worth a column: तीक्ष्ण (tikshna, sharp/penetrating), रूक्ष (ruksha, dry), लघु (laghu, light). Dymock's nighanta digest independently confirms 'light'. The DB carries all three in prose only.
वह्निकर (vahnikara) — 'fire-making', i.e. it kindles the digestive fire. This is a distinct classical attribute, not a restatement of ushna, and Dymock's 'appetizing' renders the same idea.
VIPAKA: NOT STATED in the Bhavaprakasha entry or in Dymock. The DB's 'katu vipaka' has no pre-1900 support in the sources reached. Flag as unverified.

RASA DISAGREEMENT between two pre-1900 sources: BPN 2.112 gives only कटु (pungent); Dymock's nighanta digest gives 'bitter, pungent... astringent'. The DB stores pungent + astringent + a bitter note, which straddles both. Both readings are pre-1900; do not collapse.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom (BPN 2.112): शूल (colic), आध्मान (flatulent distension), उदर (abdominal disease), श्लेष्म (kapha), कृमि (worms), वात, विबन्ध (constipation). Dymock's digest: 'removal of abdominal pains, worms, wind and skin diseases.'

PREPARATION AND VEHICLE DOCTRINE, four separate pre-1900 rules the DB has no column for: (a) Susruta, via U. C. Dutt, The Materia Medica of the Hindus, 1877, p. 200 — the seeds are used WITH LIQUORICE ROOT 'for the purpose of strengthening the body and preventing the effects of age', i.e. as a rasayana pair, not solo; (b) Dutt 1877 — for worms, the powder in drachm doses WITH HONEY, or an infusion of the seeds; (c) Mir Muhammad Husain (Makhzan), via Dymock 1891 — dose fixed at three dirhems of the powder, 'directs it to be given with FRESH MILK'; (d) Dymock 1891 — 'A purgative should be given to PREPARE the patient for the drug', a required pre-treatment before dosing.
PAEDIATRIC FOLK USE (Dymock 1891): 'It is a common practice to put a few berries of this plant in the milk that is given to young children; they are supposed to prevent flatulence.'

DIAGNOSTIC WARNING (Dymock 1891): 'the berries are used to adulterate pepper' (Roxburgh) — a sourcing risk that runs in both directions. Also: Mir Muhammad Husain 'notices that it turns the urine red' — a harmless expected effect worth telling a customer.
SANSKRIT SYNONYMS: BPN 2.111 — कृमिघ्न, जन्तुनाशन, तण्डुल, वेल्ल, अमोघा, चित्रतण्डुल. Dymock adds वृषनाशन (Vrisha-nasana, 'destroyer of the enemy [worm]') and सुचित्रबीज.

CHINESE SIDE: absent from the Bencao Gangmu (1596) and the Shennong Bencao Jing. No 氣味, no 归经, no Shennong grade exists. The DB's TCM mapping is explicitly flagged as an analogy — correct, keep the flag.

In the Bhavaprakasha vermifuge properties are attributed to it, and in the Rajanighantu it is called Krimikaraka.' additions: ग्राही (grahi) — bowel-binding / fluid-absorbing. A formal Ayurvedic action class, stated first among the actions, that the DB's 'astringent' only partly covers.
वर्ण्य (varnya) — complexion-improving. Not in the DB at all.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom (BPN 5.48): दोष (deranged doshas), अपची (apachi — scrofulous glandular swelling), तृषा (thirst), दाह (burning sensation), कृमि (WORMS), शोष (wasting/consumption), विष (poison), अस्र (blood disorders). NOTE WHAT IS ABSENT: menorrhagia and uterine bleeding are NOT in the nighantu indication list. The uterine reputation the DB leads with is documented by Dutt 1877, Dymock 1890 and Watt 1893 as the CURRENT practice of Hindu physicians, not as a classical nighantu indication. That is a real distinction for copy that claims classical provenance.

VERMIFUGE, an indication the DB omits entirely: BPN gives कृमि; Dymock 1890 confirms 'In the Bhavaprakasha vermifuge properties are attributed to it, and in the Rajanighantu it is called Krimikaraka.'

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, specified to the tola and consistent across three pre-1900 sources (Chakradatta, via Dutt 1877 p. 143, Dymock 1890 and Watt 1893): a decoction of the bark IN MILK — 8 tolas of bark boiled with 8 tolas of MILK and 32 tolas of water 'till the latter is evaporated', the whole given in two or three divided doses across the day, in menorrhagia. The milk is the vehicle and the water is the driven-off carrier; this is not a water decoction. Also Asoka ghrita: a decoction of the bark with clarified butter plus a number of aromatics in the form of a paste.
VIPAKA and GUNA: NOT STATED for Ashoka in the Bhavaprakasha entry. Nothing to record; do not infer.

SANSKRIT SYNONYMS (BPN 5.47): हेमपुष्प (Hemapushpa), वञ्जुल (Vanjula), ताम्रपल्लव (Tamrapallava, 'copper-leaved'), कङ्केलि (Kankeli), पिण्डपुष्प (Pindapushpa), गन्धपुष्प (Gandhapushpa), नट (Nata). Watt 1893 adds वञ्जुल and कङ्केलि from the vernacular lists.

IDENTITY TRAP, pre-1900 and still live (Dymock 1890): 'Bombay gardeners call the Guattena longifolia (Anonaceae) Asoka and have an idea that it is the male of Saraca indica.' A different family sold under the same name.

PHYSICAL AUTHENTICATION (Dymock 1890): the bark is 'externally greyish-brown and scabrous; its substance white when freshly cut from the tree, but turning rapidly red after exposure to the air. The taste is mildly astringent and acidulous.' Useful for incoming-goods QC.
CHINESE SIDE: no Chinese source. Absent from BCGM 1596 and the Shennong classic; no 氣味, no 归经, no grade.
