BCGM 1596 heads the entry '苦參【本經中品】', and the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension places it under 卷二·中經, whose rubric reads '中藥一百二十種為臣，主養性以應人。無毒、有毒，斟酌其宜' — middle-grade drugs are ministers, some toxic and some not, and their fitness must be weighed case by case. This is the opposite of an indefinite daily herb, and it matters for a product that recommends daily use.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经): 足少陰腎經 — the FOOT SHAOYIN KIDNEY channel, and specifically as 君藥 (sovereign drug). Zhang Yuansu, quoted in BCGM 1596 發明: '元素曰苦參味苦氣沉，純陰，足少陰腎經君藥也，治本經須用，能逐濕'. Ben Cao Cong Xin 1757: '沉降入腎'. The DB's TCM text names skin, Large Intestine, Lower Burner and Liver/Gallbladder and DOES NOT NAME THE KIDNEY, which is the one channel every classical source assigns.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, fully specified (Lei Xiao 雷斅, in BCGM 1596 根修治): '采根用糯米濃泔汁浸一宿，其腥穢氣並浮在水面上，須重重淘過，即蒸之，從巳至申，取晒切用' — soak the root overnight in thick GLUTINOUS-RICE washing water so the rank matter floats to the surface, wash it through repeatedly, then STEAM it from the si hour to the shen hour (roughly 9am to 5pm), sun-dry and slice. Ben Cao Cong Xin 1757 gives the same in short: '糯米泔浸去腥氣。蒸。' The DB has no preparation column; this is a mandatory processing step, not an optional refinement.

CONTRAINDICATIONS as stated classically: (a) BCGM 1596, Xu Zhicai — '之才曰玄參為之使，惡貝母、菟絲、漏蘆，反藜蘆' — Xuan Shen is its envoy; it HATES Bei Mu, Tu Si Zi and Lou Lu; it OPPOSES (反) Li Lu, i.e. it is one of the classic 十八反 incompatible pairs. (b) Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 發明 — '惟腎水弱而相火勝者用之相宜，若火衰精冷，真元不足及年高之人，不可用也' — suitable ONLY where kidney-water is weak and ministerial fire prevails; must NOT be used where fire is declining, essence is cold, the true origin is insufficient, or in THE AGED. (c) Ben Cao Cong Xin 1757 — '肝腎虚而無熱者忌' (contraindicated where Liver and Kidney are deficient without heat).

LONG-USE WARNING, directly load-bearing for a daily-herb product: BCGM 1596 quotes Kou Zongshi citing Shen Kuo's Mengxi Bitan on two officials who rubbed their teeth with Ku Shen for years and developed heavy, disabling loins — '此乃病齒數年，用苦參揩齒，其氣味入齒傷腎所致也…後悉不用之，腰疾皆愈'. Li Shizhen then generalises from the Suwen: '氣增而久，夭之由也' (sustained augmentation of one qi is how a life is cut short) and '久服黃連苦參而反熱者，此其類也' — LONG USE OF KU SHEN CAN PARADOXICALLY PRODUCE HEAT, the opposite of its own nature. Zhu Zhenheng dissents from the kidney-injury reading: '苦參能峻補陰氣，或得之而致腰重者，因其氣降而不升也，非傷腎之謂也'. Report both; do not adjudicate.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS beyond the 本經 line: 別錄 — '養肝膽氣，安五臟，平胃氣，令人嗜食，輕身定志，益精，利九竅，除伏熱腸澼，止渴醒酒，小便黃赤，療惡瘡下部'; 甄權 — '治熱毒風，皮肌煩躁生瘡，赤癩眉脫，除大熱嗜睡，治腹中冷痛，中惡腹痛'; 時珍 — '殺疳蟲，炒存性米飲服，治腸風瀉血并熱痢'. Note 時珍's own preparation rider: 炒存性 (fry until charred but retaining its nature) and米飲 (rice-water) as the vehicle for the bleeding indication.
SYNONYMS (BCGM 釋名): 苦蘵 (本經), 苦骨 (綱目), 地槐/水槐/菟槐/驕槐/野槐, 白莖, 芩莖, 陵郎, 虎麻. Li Shizhen's etymology: '苦以味名，參以功名，槐以葉形名也'.
INCOMPATIBILITY NOTE for formulation: 反藜蘆 (opposes Veratrum) is a hard classical prohibition, not a caution. If the DB ever drives formula suggestions, this pair must be blocked.

results.herb: Codonopsis / Dang Shen 黨參 (Codonopsis pilosula)
results.pre1900_finding: 味甘性平 — sweet in flavour, NEUTRAL in nature. Zhao Xuemin's Bencao Gangmu Shiyi 本草綱目拾遺 卷三 states it twice, once under 上黨參 and once under 防風黨參; Wu Yiluo's Ben Cao Cong Xin 1757, the earliest monograph, gives '甘平補中'. Both pre-1900, both traditional-orthography for the Shiyi text.
results.source_year: 1765 compiled / 1871 first printed (Bencao Gangmu Shiyi); 1757 (Ben Cao Cong Xin); 1848 (Zhiwu Mingshi Tukao)
results.evidence: (1) Zhao Xuemin 趙學敏, Bencao Gangmu Shiyi 本草綱目拾遺, 卷三, 上黨參 (compiled from 1765, first printed 1871): '《本經逢原》云：產山西太行山者，名上黨人參。雖無甘溫峻補之功，卻有甘平清肺之力。不似沙參之性寒，專洩肺氣也。…味甘性平，治肺虛，能益肺氣。' And under 防風黨參: '味甘平，補中益氣，和脾胃，除煩惱，解渴。中氣微虛，用以調補，甚爲平安。' URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目拾遺/卷三 (2) Wu Yiluo 吳儀洛, Ben Cao Cong Xin 本草從新, 1757, 黨參: '補中氣、生津。甘平補中。益氣。和脾胃。除煩渴。中氣微虛。用以調補。甚爲平妥。' https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新 (simplified-mixed transcription; the traditional text at (1) carries the same assignment and is the one quoted). (3) Wu Qijun 吳其濬, Zhiwu Mingshi Tukao 植物名實圖考, 1848, 卷七 黨參 — gives botany and a polemic but NO thermal quality: '黨參山西多產，長根至二三尺，蔓生，葉不對節，大如手指，野生者根有白汁，秋開花如沙參，花色靑白…此草味甜有汁，養脾助氣，亦應功亞黃耆'. URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:植物名實圖考(七).djvu/93
additions: NO SHENNONG GRADE EXISTS, and the DB must not let it inherit ginseng's. 黨參 is absent from the Shennong Bencao Jing and from Li Shizhen's Bencao Gangmu (1596) — verified by search of both texts. Its first monographs are Ben Cao Cong Xin (1757) and Bencao Gangmu Shiyi. For a product that uses Shennong grade to signal duration of use, Dang Shen simply has no ancient warrant either way.

A CLEARING ACTION THE DB OMITS: Zhang Lu, 本經逢原 (1695), quoted verbatim in the Shiyi — '雖無甘溫峻補之功，卻有甘平清肺之力' — it lacks ginseng's sweet-WARM drastic tonifying power but has a sweet-NEUTRAL power to CLEAR THE LUNG (清肺). The DB frames it purely as a tonic; the classical source gives it a mild clearing action as well, and contrasts it with Sha Shen, '不似沙參之性寒，專洩肺氣也' (unlike Sha Shen, whose nature is COLD and which only drains lung qi).

ORGAN DIRECTION as stated (no formal 归经 line exists in these texts): 治肺虛，能益肺氣 (Lung); 補中益氣，和脾胃 (middle burner, Spleen and Stomach); 除煩惱，解渴 / 除煩渴 (relieves vexation and thirst). The DB's channel attribution should be marked as derived, not classically stated.

CONTRAINDICATION, stated bluntly by Wu Qijun 1848: '若傷冒時疫，以此橫塞中焦，羸尪雜症，妄冀蘇起沉疴，未覩其益，必蒙其害' — in acute chill or seasonal epidemic illness it BLOCKS THE MIDDLE BURNER crosswise; hoping to raise a wasted patient with it, you will see no benefit and will certainly meet harm. He also reports the common adverse effect: '服者亦多胸滿氣隔之患' — many who take it suffer chest fullness and qi blockage. The DB records no contraindication for this herb at all.

AUTHENTICATION DOCTRINE, unusually detailed and commercially useful (Shiyi 卷三, quoting 從新 and 翁有良辨誤): '惟防黨性味和平足貴，根有獅子盤頭者真，硬紋者僞也' — only Fang Dang is worth having, and the genuine root carries a LION'S-HEAD CROWN (獅子盤頭); hard-striated roots are counterfeit. '白黨即將此參煮曬已成，原汁已出，不堪用' — white dang has been boiled and dried, its juice already driven out, unusable. '近今有川黨…皮白味淡，類乎桔梗，無獅頭…入藥亦殊劣不可用' — recent Sichuan dang has white skin and bland taste, resembles Platycodon, lacks the lion's head, and is markedly inferior. Grading by age: '嫩而小枝者，名上黨參；老而大者，名防黨參'. Provenance ranking: 山西太行山潞安州 best, 陝西 second.

SPECIES AND NAME TRAP, pre-1900 and serious: '上黨參 / 上黨人參' originally denoted TRUE PANAX from Shangdang, and the Shiyi preserves the transition — Zhang Lu 1695 still calls the Shanxi product 上黨人參 while noting it lacks ginseng's power. The Codonopsis reading is secured by two things: the 獅子盤頭 root-crown description, and Wu Qijun's 1848 plate plus botany (creeping vine, leaves not opposite at the node, thick as a finger, white latex in the wild root, autumn flowers like Sha Shen, bluish-white). Any pre-1900 quote using 上黨人參 must be checked against these before being carried to a Codonopsis monograph.

THE 'AFTER 1949' CLAIM IN THE DB IS WRONG. The DB states it became the routine ginseng substitute after 1949. Zhang Lu (1695) and the Shiyi already treat it as a stand-in, and 翁有良 states flatly '黨參功用，可代人參' — Dang Shen's function can replace ginseng. The substitution is at least 18th-century, not mid-20th.

A DIFFERENT ANALOGY THAN THE DB'S: Wu Qijun 1848 twice likens it not to ginseng but to ASTRAGALUS — '氣味則近黃耆' (its qi and flavour approach Huang Qi) and '亦應功亞黃耆' (its efficacy should rank just below Huang Qi). He is openly hostile to the ginseng framing: '舉世以代神草，莫知其非' — the whole world substitutes it for the divine herb and no one knows it is wrong.

PREPARATION NOTE from the neighbouring 土人參 entry, useful for not confusing the two: the Shiyi's 土人參 (粉沙參) is '甘、微寒，須蒸之極透，則寒去' — sweet and slightly cold, and must be steamed until thoroughly penetrated to drive the cold off. That is a DIFFERENT drug from 黨參, and 紅黨 is explicitly said to be made from it: '紅黨即將此參去皮淨煮極熟陰乾而成，味淡無用'.

results.herb: Punarnava (Boerhavia diffusa L., syn. B. repens in the pre-1900 literature)
results.pre1900_finding: Two pre-1900 sources give opposite temperatures, and the one that matches the DB's own named species contradicts the DB. Bhavaprakasha Nighantu 4.233, describing the RED punarnava — the form the DB names as the officinal plant — assigns हिमा (hima = COLD). Dymock 1893 reports the nighantas as 'pungent, dry, HOT, sweet and bitter'. The DB's 'Warm' is supported by Dymock and contradicted by the Bhavaprakasha for the red variety.
results.source_year: 1893 (Dymock, Pharmacographia Indica vol. III) and 16th century (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu) — the two disagree
results.evidence: (1) Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Bhavamishra, 16th c.), Guduchyadi Varga 4.231-233, Sanskrit original, WHITE then RED: 'पुनर्नवा श्वेतमूला शोथघ्नी दीर्घपत्रिका । कटु कषायानुरसा पाण्डुघ्नी दीपनी परा । शोफानिलगरश्लेष्महरी ब्रघ्नोदरप्रणुत् ॥२३१॥ पुनर्नवाऽपरा रक्ता रक्तपुष्पा शिलाटिका । शोथघ्नी क्षुद्र वर्षाभूर्वर्षकेतुः कठिल्लकः ॥२३२॥ पुनर्नवाऽरुणा तिक्ता कटुपाका हिमा लघुः । वातला ग्राहिणी श्लेष्मपित्तरक्तविनाशिनी ॥२३३॥' — the red is bitter, KATU-VIPAKA, HIMA (cold), LAGHU (light), VATALA (vata-increasing), GRAHINI (binding). URL: https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/भावप्रकाशः/पूर्वखण्डे_भावप्रकाशनिघण्टुः (2) William Dymock, C. J. H. Warden & David Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica, vol. III, 1893, p. 130-131, BOERHAAVIA REPENS: 'This plant is called by Sanskrit medical writers Punar-nava, Punar-bhava, and Punar-bhu, on account of its perennial habit, and Sothagni from its use as a remedy for dropsy. It is described in the Nighantas as pungent, dry, hot, sweet and bitter, and is recommended as a laxative, diuretic, and stomachic in jaundice, strangury, dropsy, and internal inflammations.' Full text: https://archive.org/download/b2129737x_0003/b2129737x_0003_djvu.txt
additions: VIPAKA CONFIRMED against the 16th-century Sanskrit: कटुपाका — katu (pungent) vipaka, exactly as the DB stores it. This is the one energetic in the DB's Punarnava row that a pre-1900 source verifies outright.

VATA CLAIM REVERSED: BPN 4.233 says the red punarnava is वातला (vatala) — it INCREASES vata. The DB's ayurvedic_dosha_match is 'Kapha, Vata', i.e. it reduces both. The nighantu says the opposite for the red form. This is a second, independent contradiction on a field the DB does hold.
GUNA: लघु (laghu, LIGHT) per BPN for the red form. Dymock's nighanta digest says 'dry' (ruksha). The DB stores 'Dry'. Neither source states the other's term; both are pre-1900. Record both.
ग्राहिणी (grahini) — binding/absorbent for the red form. Absent from the DB, and it sits oddly beside a diuretic reputation; worth surfacing rather than smoothing.

TWO PLANTS, TWO PROFILES — the classical texts already split what the DB half-splits. BPN 4.231 white punarnava (श्वेतमूला 'white-rooted', दीर्घपत्रिका 'long-leaved', शोथघ्नी 'oedema-killer'): कटु, कषाय-अनुरस (pungent with an astringent AFTER-taste), पाण्डुघ्नी (destroys pandu — anaemia/jaundice), दीपनी परा (supremely digestion-kindling); removes शोफ (oedema), अनिल (wind), गर (compound poison), श्लेष्म; conquers ब्रघ्न (hernia/inguinal swelling) and उदर. NO VIRYA IS STATED FOR THE WHITE. BPN 4.232-233 red punarnava (रक्ता, रक्तपुष्पा, शिलाटिका, वर्षाभू 'born of the rains', वर्षकेतु, कठिल्लक). The DB's own note that bazaar 'shweta punarnava' is often Trianthema portulacastrum is a real and pre-1900-attested confusion; the two coloured forms are separate drugs with separate properties in the classical text, and only the red one has a stated virya.

NAME DOCTRINE (Dymock 1893): पुनर्नवा / पुनर्भव / पुनर्भू, 'on account of its perennial habit' — literally 'renewed again'; and शोथघ्नि (Sothagni) 'from its use as a remedy for dropsy'. BPN independently gives शोथघ्नी for both the white and the red.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom: (BPN red 4.233) श्लेष्म, पित्त, रक्त — destroys kapha, pitta and blood disorders; (BPN white 4.231) शोफ, अनिल, गर, श्लेष्म, ब्रघ्न, उदर, पाण्डु; (Dymock 1893) 'a laxative, diuretic, and stomachic in jaundice, strangury, dropsy, and internal inflammations'.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE the DB has no column for: (a) Punarnavashtaka, a compound decoction (Dymock 1893) — roots of punarnava + dried neem bark + Trichosanthes dioica leaves + dried ginger + Picrorhiza kurroa root + chebulic myrobalan + Tinospora cordifolia stem + dried Berberis wood, EACH ONE QUARTER TOLA, in 32 tolas of water boiled down to one-fourth, the whole taken over 24 hours; an oil and an electuary are also used. (b) Ainslie, via Dymock — the root in powder, a teaspoonful twice daily, as a laxative. (c) Vilva taila (Chakradatta, via U. C. Dutt 1877, p. 131) — punarnava root is one of the pastes boiled into a sesamum oil with belas fruit decoction, 'used externally in chronic bowel complaints'. (d) Sarangadhara's inflammatory poultice (Dutt 1877, p. 241) — punarnava root + Berberis asiatica wood + Moringa root + ginger + mustard seed, equal parts, ground to a paste WITH FERMENTED RICE WATER.

FOOD-VS-MEDICINE PROCESSING RULE (Dymock 1893): eaten as a potherb in the rains, it must be 'well boiled TO REMOVE ITS MEDICINAL PROPERTIES'. A pre-1900 statement that the culinary preparation is deliberately deactivating.
DOSE WARNING (Dymock 1893): 'it is said to act as an EMETIC when given in large doses.' Confirmed by French experience in the Antilles, where the plant is called Patagon.

FOUNDER DECISION NEEDED: the stored 'Warm' cannot be presented as settled. One pre-1900 nighantu digest (Dymock 1893) says hot; the Bhavaprakasha says cold for the red-flowered plant the DB itself names as officinal. Both must be surfaced, or the temperature must be qualified by variety.

results.pre1900_finding: हिमः (hima = COLD) with रूक्ष (dry). Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, Guduchyadi Varga 4.118: 'कुटजः कटुको रूक्षो दीपनस्तुवरो हिमः'. Dymock 1891 independently: the bark 'is described in the Nighantas as bitter, astringent, cold and digestive'. Two independent pre-1900 lines agree on both the temperature and the dryness.
results.source_year: 1891 (Dymock, Pharmacographia Indica vol. II); 16th century (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu)
results.evidence: (1) Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Bhavamishra, 16th c.), Guduchyadi Varga 4.116-118, Sanskrit original: 'कुटजः कूटजः कौटो वत्सको गिरिमल्लिका ॥११६॥ कालिङ्गः शक्रशाखी च मल्लिकापुष्प इत्यपि । इन्द्रो यवफलः प्रोक्तो वृक्षकः पाण्डुरद्रुमः ॥११७॥ कुटजः कटुको रूक्षो दीपनस्तुवरो हिमः । अर्शोऽतिसारपित्तास्रकफतृष्णाऽमकुष्ठनुत् ॥११८॥' URL: https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/भावप्रकाशः/पूर्वखण्डे_भावप्रकाशनिघण्टुः (the Devanagari transcription prints 'पित्तास्न' for 'पित्तास्र' at 4.118 — an orthographic slip in the digitisation, not a variant reading). (2) William Dymock, C. J. H. Warden & David Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica, vol. II, 1891, p. 392, HOLARRHENA ANTIDYSENTERICA: 'The bark is one of the most important articles in the Hindu Materia Medica, and is described in the Nighantas as bitter, astringent, cold and digestive; a remedy for piles, dysentery, bile, leprosy and phlegmatic humours.' Full text: https://archive.org/download/b20413415_002/b20413415_002_djvu.txt
additions: GUNA रूक्ष (ruksha, DRY) is stated outright in the 16th-c. Sanskrit and echoed by Dymock's 'digestive' pairing. This upgrades the DB's 'Dry' from a derivation to a sourced classical value.

दीपन (dipana) — kindles the digestive fire. Both sources give it (Dymock renders it 'digestive'). Notable because a COLD + DIPANA drug is an unusual combination; the DB's cool/drying/astringent framing carries none of the digestive-kindling half, which is exactly what makes it usable in a depleted gut rather than only a hot one.

RASA DISAGREEMENT between two pre-1900 sources, do not collapse: BPN 4.118 gives कटुक (katuka, pungent/acrid) + तुवर (astringent); Dymock's nighanta digest gives 'bitter, astringent'. The DB stores bitter + astringent, which matches Dymock but not the Bhavaprakasha.
VIPAKA: NOT STATED in either source. The DB's 'Pungent (Katu)' vipaka has no pre-1900 support in what was reached. Flag as unverified.

PART DISCIPLINE — BARK AND SEED ARE DIFFERENT DRUGS, and the DB merges them. BPN 4.117 names the seed separately: 'इन्द्रो यवफलः प्रोक्तो' (Indra, the seed-fruit). U. C. Dutt, The Materia Medica of the Hindus, 1877, p. 192: 'The seeds called Indrayava in Sanskrit and Indrajav in the vernacular, are also used in medicine, they being regarded as astringent, febrifuge and useful in fever, dysentery, diarrhoea, and intestinal worms.' Dymock 1891 gives the seed synonyms इन्द्रयव, भद्रयव, वत्सकबीज, शक्रबीज, and notes the Arabic/Persian trade name Lisan-el-asafir-el-murr. The bark's classical profile and the seed's are not the same.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom (BPN 4.118): अर्श (piles), अतिसार (diarrhoea), पित्तास्र (pitta and blood disorders), कफ, तृष्णा (thirst), आम (undigested residue), कुष्ठ (skin disease). Dymock's digest: 'a remedy for piles, dysentery, bile, leprosy and phlegmatic humours'.

SUSRUTA'S WIDER INDICATION LIST (via Dymock 1891, and it is much broader than the DB's dysentery framing): 'expectorant, an antidote to poisons, cures dysuria, urinary and skin diseases, checks nausea and vomiting, removes pruritus, improves the condition of bad ulcers, relieves pains of the stomach, and checks the derangement of the three humours, viz., phlegm, air and bile.'

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, the most detailed in this batch — Kutajarishta, the fermented wine of Sarangadhara (Dymock 1891): take FRESH ROOT bark 12.5 seers, raisins 6.25 seers, flowers of Bassia latifolia and bark of Gmelina arborea 80 tolas each; boil together in 256 seers of water down to 64 seers and strain; then add Woodfordia floribunda flowers 2.5 seers and treacle 12.5 seers, and let it FERMENT FOR A MONTH IN A COOL PLACE, 'it is usually buried under the ground'; draw off and bottle. Dymock's verdict: 'This preparation has an agreeable flavour, is not bitter, and is an excellent remedy in chronic dysentery and diarrhoea.' Note the doctrine points: fresh ROOT bark (not stem bark), and fermentation rather than decoction as the way to make it palatable.

OTHER CLASSICAL PREPARATIONS: Kutajaleha (confection) and Pathadya churna of Chakradatta; Pradarani lauha, which combines the drug with IRON (Dymock 1891). Dutt 1877, p. 192: the expressed juice of the bark given WITH HONEY; a fluid extract given with ginger and atis; a compound decoction called Kutajashtaka. EXTERNAL ROUTE, which the DB omits entirely: 'Plasters and oils, containing Conessi bark combined with astringents and aromatics, are also used by the Hindus. They are applied over the part of the abdomen which is most painful.'

NOMENCLATURE TRAP, flagged in the pre-1900 literature itself (Dymock 1891, vol. II): 'The bark and wood of the different species of Strychnos appears to be the Katukavalli of the Raja Nirghanta, often confounded with Kutaja, the bark of Holarrhena antidysenterica.' He explains why: 'In the vernaculars the Sanskrit Katu, bitter, becomes Kadu, Karu, Kadva, Karva, Karo, Kaura... These names are very loosely applied to many bitter' drugs. A Kutaj sourced on vernacular name alone can be a Strychnos.
SANSKRIT SYNONYMS (BPN 4.116-117): कुटज, कूटज, कौट, वत्सक, गिरिमल्लिका, कालिङ्ग, शक्रशाखी, मल्लिकापुष्प, वृक्षक, पाण्डुरद्रुम. Dymock adds शक्रासन ('Indra's food') and वत्सक glossed 'cow tree'.

CHINESE SIDE: no Chinese source. Absent from BCGM 1596 and the Shennong classic; no 氣味, no 归经, no grade. The DB's Bai Tou Weng / Huang Lian correspondence is explicitly flagged as an analogy — correct, keep the flag.

results.herb: Epimedium / Horny Goat Weed (Yin Yang Huo) — Epimedium brevicornu
results.pre1900_finding: The value is CONTESTED across pre-1900 China and the database has collapsed it. The Ben Cao Gang Mu head-line reads 氣味辛寒無毒 (acrid, COLD, non-toxic), and the Shennong Ben Cao Jing in the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension reads 味辛，寒。 Li Shizhen then prints five dissenting readings in the attached note, including his own 甘香微辛溫 (warm). By 1694 and 1757 the tradition had settled on 辛香甘溫 (acrid, aromatic, sweet, WARM). So 'Warm' matches the 17th–18th-century consensus but flatly contradicts the 本經/BCGM head reading. CRITICAL: the database's own primary citation asserts the Shennong Ben Cao Jing records Yin Yang Huo as 'an acrid, warming tonic'. It does not. It says 寒, cold. That specific attribution is false.
results.source_year: 1596 (Bencao Gangmu); 1799 recension of a c. 200 CE text (Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan); 1757 (Bencao Congxin)
results.evidence: (1) Li Shizhen 李時珍, 本草綱目 (四庫全書本) 卷十二下, 淫羊藿, 1596: 「{{SK anchor|淫羊藿}}{{SK notes|本經中品}} … {{SK anchor|氣味辛寒無毒}}{{SK notes|普曰神農雷公辛，李當之小寒，權曰甘平可單用，保昇曰性温，時珍曰甘香微辛温，之才曰薯蕷紫芝為之使，得酒良}}」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷12下 . (2) 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan 孫星衍 recension, 1799: 「淫羊藿　味辛，寒。主陽痿絕傷，莖中痛，利小便，益氣力，強志。一名剛前。生山谷。《吳普》曰：淫羊藿，神農、雷公：辛；李氏：小寒。堅骨（《御覽》）。《名醫》曰：生上山郡陽山。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) . (3) Wu Yiluo 吳儀洛, 本草從新, 1757: 「淫羊藿　補腎命門。辛香甘溫。入肝腎。補命門。益精氣。堅筋骨。利小便。治絕陽不兴。絕陰不產。冷風劳氣。四肢不仁。（手足麻木。）相火易动。遠之。…去枝。羊脂拌炒。山藥爲使。得酒良。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 中品 (MIDDLE grade). Stated twice independently — BCGM tags the entry 「本經中品」, and Sun Xingyan's 1799 recension lists 淫羊藿 in 「上草，中品四十九種」. Middle grade encodes therapeutic-course use, NOT open-ended daily use. This matters directly for a product that recommends daily herbs.

CHANNEL ENTRY (歸經), pre-1900: Wu Yiluo 1757 gives 「入肝腎」 — enters LIVER and KIDNEY. This is the earliest clean pre-1900 warrant for the Liver/Kidney assignment the database already carries. A second, different pre-1900 reading exists: Wang Ang, 本草備要 1694, quotes 時珍 as making it a 「手足陽明、三焦、命門藥」 (hand and foot Yangming, Sanjiao, and Mingmen). Two pre-1900 channel maps, not one. (The 1694 Wikisource transcription is simplified with dropped glyphs — used to LOCATE only, not quoted as the 1694 text.)

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom, 本經 layer via Sun Xingyan 1799: 「主陽痿絕傷，莖中痛，利小便，益氣力，強志」 — impotence and severed/exhausted injury, pain within the stalk, disinhibits urination, boosts qi and strength, strengthens the will. 別錄 layer added in BCGM: 「堅筋骨，消瘰癧赤癰，下部有瘡洗出蟲，丈夫乆服令人有子」 — hardens sinew and bone, disperses scrofula and red abscess, washes worms from sores of the lower body, long use gives a man children.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, explicit and pre-1900: Lei Xiao 雷斆 quoted in BCGM 1596: 「凡使時呼仙靈脾，以夾刀夾去葉四畔花枝，每一斤用羊脂四兩拌炒，待脂盡為度」 — clip away the flower-stalks around the leaf margin with pinching shears, then stir-fry each catty with FOUR LIANG of rendered sheep/goat fat until the fat is fully taken up. Wu Yiluo 1757 repeats it in four characters: 「去枝。羊脂拌炒。」 This is a mandatory processing step in the classical record, not an optional refinement — the database mentions lamb-fat processing but carries no pre-1900 citation for it. Now it has one.

VEHICLE / SYNERGIST DOCTRINE: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai, quoted BCGM 1596) 「薯蕷、紫芝為之使，得酒良」 — Chinese yam and purple reishi are its envoys; it is improved by wine. Wu Yiluo 1757 shortens this to 「山藥爲使。得酒良。」 The 本經 wine-extraction is spelled out in BCGM's 附方: 仙靈脾酒, one catty steeped in one dou of wine for three days.

CONTRAINDICATION as stated classically: Wu Yiluo 1757, 「相火易动。遠之。」 — where the ministerial fire is easily stirred, KEEP AWAY FROM IT. This is a pre-1900 warrant for the yin-deficiency-with-fire caution the database currently sources only to a 2010 modern text.

SPECIES CAVEAT: no pre-1900 source can resolve to Epimedium brevicornu Maxim. BCGM 1596 describes 「一莖二椏，一椏三葉」 and the folk name 三枝九葉草 (three-branch nine-leaf herb) — a genus-level, not species-level, determination. Any claim that the classical text speaks specifically of E. brevicornu is unsupportable.

results.pre1900_finding: Ben Cao Gang Mu 1596 assigns the ROOT 「氣味甘微苦温無毒」 — sweet, slightly bitter, WARM, non-toxic. This matches the stored temperature and the stored taste exactly, character for character. Li Shizhen restates it in the 發明: 「此藥氣温味甘微苦」. Confirmed again by Wu Yiluo 1757, 「甘苦微溫」. Note that San Qi is a NEW entry in the BCGM (tagged 綱目) — it is not in the Shennong Ben Cao Jing at all, so the database's primary_text_citation, which files this under author 'Shennong Ben Cao Jing' with year 'c. 200 CE' while its title text names the 1596 BCGM, is internally inconsistent metadata and should be repaired to Li Shizhen 1596.
results.evidence: Li Shizhen 李時珍, 本草綱目 (四庫全書本) 卷十二下, 三七, 1596: 「根氣味甘微苦温無毒。主治止血散血定痛，金刃箭傷、跌撲杖瘡血出不止者，嚼爛塗，或為末摻之，其血即止。亦主吐血衂血、下血血痢、崩中經水不止、産後惡血不下、血運血痛、赤目癰腫、虎咬蛇傷諸病。」 and 發明: 「大抵此藥氣温味甘微苦，乃陽明厥隂血分之藥，故能治一切血病，與麒麟竭、紫釧相同。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷12下 . Corroborated: Wu Yiluo 吳儀洛, 本草從新, 1757, 「三七　一名山漆　瀉、散瘀定痛。甘苦微溫。散血定痛。…能損新血。無瘀者勿用。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: CHANNEL ENTRY (歸經), pre-1900 and in Li Shizhen's own words: 「乃陽明厥隂血分之藥」 — a medicine of the BLOOD LEVEL of the Yangming and Jueyin channels. Yangming = Stomach/Large Intestine, Jueyin = Liver/Pericardium. The database's 'Liver and Stomach channels' is therefore correct but was carried without a pre-1900 warrant; it now has one, with the important refinement that classically it is specifically the BLOOD DIVISION (血分) of those channels, not the channels at large.

SHENNONG GRADE: NONE. San Qi is absent from the Shennong Ben Cao Jing. BCGM tags it 綱目, i.e. first admitted to the materia medica by Li Shizhen himself, who writes 「此藥近時始出，南人軍中用為金瘡要藥」 — this drug has only lately appeared; southern troops use it as an essential remedy for metal-weapon wounds. It carries no upper/middle/lower grade and therefore no classical duration-of-use signal.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS: 止血散血定痛 (stops bleeding, disperses blood, settles pain); 金刃箭傷 (metal-blade and arrow wounds); 跌撲杖瘡 (falls, blows, and flogging wounds); 吐血衂血 (vomiting and nose-bleeding of blood); 下血血痢 (blood in the stool, bloody dysentery); 崩中經水不止 (flooding, unceasing menses); 産後惡血不下 (post-partum lochia failing to descend); 血運血痛 (blood dizziness, blood pain); 赤目癰腫 (red eyes, abscess swelling); 虎咬蛇傷 (tiger bite, snake bite).

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, several distinct vehicles, all pre-1900: chew raw to a pulp and apply, or powder and sprinkle on the wound (嚼爛塗，或為末摻之); powder taken down with rice congee water 米湯 for haematemesis and post-partum bleeding; with 米泔水 (rice-washing water) for red and bloody dysentery; with 淡白酒 (weak white liquor) for large-intestine bleeding; ground with rice vinegar 米醋 and applied for unnamed abscess. PROPHYLACTIC DOSING, a striking classical detail: 「若受杖時，先服一二錢，則血不衝心」 — if you are about to be flogged, take 1–2 qian BEFOREHAND and the blood will not rush the heart.

CONTRAINDICATION as stated classically (Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757): 「能損新血。無瘀者勿用。」 — it can damage fresh blood; DO NOT USE WHERE THERE IS NO STASIS. The database's tcm_pattern_match currently presents San Qi's dual action as an unqualified virtue ('stops bleeding without causing stasis, dispels stasis without causing bleeding'); the 1757 text supplies the missing limit.

SPECIES CAVEAT raised by Li Shizhen himself: after describing the true Guangxi drug (root 「味微甘而苦，頗似人參之味」, tested by dissolving pig's blood), he describes a SECOND plant sold as 三七 with chrysanthemum-and-mugwort-like leaves, red-ridged stems, yellow flowers and a burdock-sized root, and says 「與南中來者不類，恐是劉寄奴之屬」 — unlike the southern drug, probably a relative of Artemisia anomala. The market adulteration is documented in 1596; the database should not treat classical 三七 quotations as automatically referring to Panax notoginseng.

results.pre1900_finding: The Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Bhavamishra, 16th c.) assigns Shankhapushpi 「कषायोष्णा」 — kashaya (astringent) in rasa and USHNA, HOT, in virya. The database stores Cool. That is a direct reversal of the classical virya, not a nuance. The database's moisture value ('Moist, snigdha, unctuous') is likewise unsupported: the verse gives kashaya, an astringent and therefore drying quality, and no snigdha guna anywhere. SEPARATE AND EQUALLY SERIOUS: the botanical identity is wrong for the pre-1900 record. U. C. Dutt (1877), working from the Sanskrit medical works, identifies Sanskrit Sankhapushpi as CANSCORA DECUSSATA (Gentianaceae), not Convolvulus. Dutt gives that plant no virya at all, only actions.
results.source_year: 16th century (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu); 1877 (Dutt)
results.evidence: (1) भावमिश्र, भावप्रकाशनिघण्टुः, गुडूच्यादिवर्गः, 16th century: 「शङ्ख्नपुष्पी तु शङ्खाह्वा मङ्गल्यकुसुमाऽपि च। शङ्खपुष्पी सरा मेध्या वृष्या मानसरोगहृत् ॥२६९॥ रसायनी कषायोष्णा स्मृतिकान्तिबलाग्निदा। दोषापस्मारभूताश्रीकुष्ठक्रिमिविषप्रणुत् ॥४.२७०॥」 — https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/भावप्रकाशः/पूर्वखण्डे_भावप्रकाशनिघण्टुः (Sanskrit original; the English glosses in this report are my own reading of the Sanskrit, not a cited translation). (2) U. C. Dutt, The Materia Medica of the Hindus, Compiled from Sanskrit Medical Works, Calcutta, 1877, p. 201: 「CANSCORA DECUSSATA, R. et Sch. Syn. Pladera decussata, Roxb. Sans. Sankhapushpi. Vern. Dankuni, Beng. Sankhahuli, Hind. THIS little plant is regarded as laxative, alterative and tonic and is much praised as a nervine. It is used in insanity, epilepsy and nervous debility.」 — https://archive.org/details/materiamedicaofh00duttuoft
additions: VIRYA: उष्णा (ushna, HOT). RASA: कषाय (kashaya, astringent). The verse gives no vipaka and no guna term, so vipaka for Shankhapushpi is NOT recoverable from this source and must be left blank rather than inferred.

CLASSICAL ACTIONS in the source's own idiom: सरा (sara — mobile, moving, mildly laxative); मेध्या (medhya — intellect-promoting, the medhya rasayana class the database already invokes, here confirmed from a pre-1900 Sanskrit text rather than a modern one); वृष्या (vrishya — aphrodisiac / generative-tissue tonic, an action the database does NOT record at all); मानसरोगहृत् (manasa-roga-hrit — removes disorders of the mind); रसायनी (rasayani — a rasayana, a rejuvenative); स्मृति-कान्ति-बल-अग्नि-दा (gives memory, lustre/complexion, strength, and DIGESTIVE FIRE — agni-da is itself a warming action word consistent with the ushna virya, not with 'cool').

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS: दोष (humoral derangement), अपस्मार (apasmara — epilepsy), भूत (bhuta — possession disorders), कुष्ठ (kushtha — skin disease/leprosy group), क्रिमि (krimi — worms), विष (visha — poison). Note that epilepsy, possession, skin disease, worms and poisoning are absent from the database's entry, which reads Shankhpushpi narrowly as an anxiolytic and nootropic.

SPECIES / IDENTITY DISPUTE, which the database does not surface at all and which is the load-bearing problem here. Pre-1900 Sanskrit-derived scholarship assigns Shankhapushpi to CANSCORA DECUSSATA (Dutt 1877, p. 201, and again in his Glossary of Indian Plants, p. 316: 'Sankhapushpi | Dankuni, B., Sankhahuli, H. | Canscora decussata, R. et Sch.'). Separately, Dymock, Warden and Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica, vol. II, 1891, p. 543, treat EVOLVULUS ALSINOIDES as Sanskrit Vishnukranta while recording its Marathi vernacular as 'Shankaval' — a second vector for the confusion. Convolvulus pluricaulis is a THIRD candidate and I found no pre-1900 source that names it. Before this row can be trusted, the founder must decide which plant the product means.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, pre-1900 (Dutt 1877, pp. 202 and 213, for Canscora decussata): fresh juice about one ounce given WITH HONEY and pachak root for insanity; a paste of the entire plant including roots and flowers taken WITH MILK as a nervine and alterative tonic; and it is a paste ingredient of Brahmi ghrita, boiled with old clarified butter and brahmi juice until the watery portion evaporates. Vehicle discipline (honey, milk, ghee) is explicit in the classical record and absent from the database.
NO CONTRAINDICATION is stated in either pre-1900 source. Record that as an admitted gap, not as 'none known'.

results.stored_temperature: Warm, trending hot (stored field also asserts Ayurvedic ushna and tikshna, and asserts the Chinese drug A Wei is 'warm and acrid-bitter')
results.pre1900_finding: The two traditions disagree and the database has silently merged them. INDIAN: confirmed hot. Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (16th c.) reads 「हिङ्गूष्णं … तीक्ष्णं」 — ushna (HOT) and tikshna (SHARP), exactly the two terms the database asserts, now with a pre-1900 warrant. CHINESE: contradicted. Ben Cao Gang Mu 1596 assigns 阿魏 「氣味辛平無毒」 — acrid, NEUTRAL, non-toxic; Wu Yiluo 1757 repeats 「辛平」. No pre-1900 Chinese source I read calls A Wei warm, and none calls it bitter. The tcm_pattern_match field's 'warm and acrid-bitter' is therefore unsupported and should be corrected to 辛平. Also flag: the row's secondary_citation is Grieve, A Modern Herbal, 1931 — post-1900 and inadmissible under the project rule; the primary (King's American Dispensatory 1898) is admissible.
results.source_year: 16th century (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu); 1596 (Bencao Gangmu); 1757 (Bencao Congxin); 1891 (Pharmacographia Indica); 1877 (Dutt)

(2) Li Shizhen 李時珍, 本草綱目 (四庫全書本) 卷三十四, 阿魏, 1596: 「氣味辛平無毒。主治殺諸小蟲，去臭氣，破癥積，下惡氣，除邪鬼蟲毒{{唐本}}。治風邪鬼疰，心腹中冷{{李珣}}。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷34 . (3) Wu Yiluo 吳儀洛, 本草從新, 1757: 「阿魏　瀉、消积殺虫。辛平。入脾胃。消肉积。殺細虫。去臭氣。…治心腹冷痛。瘧痢。…虚人虽有痞积。當先養胃氣。胃强則堅积漸磨而消矣。不宜用此。臭烈更傷胃氣。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新 . (4) Dymock, Warden and Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica, vol. II, 1891, p. 142: 'In Sanskrit it is called Hingu … In the Nighantas it bears various synonyms … it is described as hot, digestive, appetizing, pungent; a remedy for phlegm, rheumatism, griping, flatulence, diseases of the belly, satiety and worms.' — https://archive.org/details/mobot31753000263373
additions: VIRYA and GUNA, Indian: उष्ण (ushna, hot) and तीक्ष्ण (tikshna, sharp/penetrating). Dosha action: वातबलासनुत् (vata-balasa-nut — destroys vata and kapha/balasa), which underwrites the stored Vata/Kapha dosha match.

CONTRAINDICATION, Indian, explicit and currently missing from the database: 「पित्तवर्द्धनम्」 — it INCREASES PITTA. A pre-1900 Sanskrit warning that hing aggravates the pitta constitution, stated in the same verse that gives its virtues.

CONTRAINDICATION, Chinese, also missing (Wu Yiluo 1757): 「虚人虽有痞积。當先養胃氣。…不宜用此。臭烈更傷胃氣。」 — in a DEFICIENT person, even where there is a fixed lump, first nourish stomach qi; this is not the right medicine, and its foul pungency will further injure stomach qi. That is a serious classical limit on a drug the database presents as a stagnation-breaker.

CHANNEL ENTRY (歸經), pre-1900: Wu Yiluo 1757, 「入脾胃」 — enters SPLEEN and STOMACH. The database's tcm_pattern_match adds Liver; I found no pre-1900 warrant for the Liver entry and it should be marked inferred.

SHENNONG GRADE: NONE. 阿魏 first enters the Chinese materia medica in the 唐本草 (Tang Xinxiu Bencao, 659 CE); BCGM tags it 唐本草 with the note 「校正：自草部移入此」 — Li Shizhen reclassified it from the herb section into the wood section. No upper/middle/lower grade.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, and this is the strongest harvest here because two traditions agree independently. INDIAN: Dutt 1877, p. 175: 'It is fried before being used internally. Raw or unfried assafoetida is said to cause vomiting.' Dymock 1891, p. 142: 'Hindu medical writers direct it to be fried before being used.' CHINESE: BCGM 1596 quotes 雷斆 — 「凡用，乳鉢研細，熱酒器上滚過入藥」 — grind fine in a stone mortar, roll it over a hot wine vessel, then add to the formula. Two independent pre-1900 traditions both require heat-processing before internal use. This is a real product-safety and dosing instruction, not a stylistic note.

AUTHENTICATION DOCTRINE, pre-1900, worth carrying as provenance: BCGM 1596 records the proverb 「黄芩無假，阿魏無真」 (there is no counterfeit Scutellaria and no genuine asafoetida) alongside Liu Chun's rejoinder 「阿魏無真却有真，臭而止臭乃為珍」. It then prints Lei Xiao's three physical assay tests, including leaving half a zhu on a heated copper vessel overnight and looking for a silver-mercury white with no red.

SPECIES CAVEAT, from the pre-1900 record itself: Dymock 1891, p. 142, distinguishes the drugs — 'The gum resin of F. alliacea is the Hing of the natives of India, the other kind being seldom used by them', and p. 143, the drug of European commerce is 'the produce of Ferula fetida, Regel, and not that of F. alliacea, Boiss., which produces the Hing of India.' So Indian hing (Ferula alliacea), European asafoetida (F. foetida) and the database's F. assa-foetida are three distinct determinations in the pre-1900 literature. King's American Dispensatory 1898, the row's own primary citation, drew the official drug from F. foetida, which the part_used field already concedes. The row's latin_name should be reconciled against the tradition being quoted.

results.pre1900_finding: Confirmed independently in both traditions. The Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (16th c.) reads 「कारवेल्लं हिमं भेदि लघुतिक्तमवातलम्」 — Karavella is HIMA (COLD), purgative, light, bitter. The Ben Cao Gang Mu 1596 assigns the fruit 「氣味苦寒無毒」 — bitter, COLD, non-toxic. Two pre-1900 primaries, two traditions, same verdict. The stored bitter taste is confirmed by both (तिक्त / 苦). results.evidence: (1) भावमिश्र, भावप्रकाशनिघण्टुः, शाकवर्गः, 16th century: 「कारवेल्लं कटिल्लं स्यात्कारवेल्ली ततोलघुः। कारवेल्लं हिमं भेदि लघुतिक्तमवातलम् ॥६३॥ ज्वरपित्तकफास्रघ्नं पाण्डुमेहकृमीन् हरेत्। तद्गुणा कारवेल्ली स्याद्विशेषाद्दीपनी लघुः ॥६४॥」 — https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/भावप्रकाशः/पूर्वखण्डे_भावप्रकाशनिघण्टुः . (2) Li Shizhen 李時珍, 本草綱目 (四庫全書本) 卷二十八, 苦瓜 (釋名 錦荔枝、癩葡萄), 1596: 「𤓰氣味苦寒無毒。主治除邪熱，解勞乏，清心明目{{時珍，生生編}}。子氣味苦甘無毒。主治益氣壯陽{{時珍}}。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷28
additions: GUNA: लघु (laghu, LIGHT) — stated twice, for both the larger Karavella and the smaller Karavelli. The database's moisture field says 'Dry'; laghu is the classical term that supports it. No snigdha/ruksha term is given, and NO VIPAKA is stated for Karavella in this verse, so vipaka must be left blank rather than inferred.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, Indian: ज्वर (fever), पित्त, कफ, अस्र (blood disorders), पाण्डु (panduroga — anaemia/jaundice), मेह (prameha — the urinary/diabetic disorder group the database already invokes), क्रिमि (worms). Additional action: भेदि (bhedi — purgative/breaking). The smaller variety Karavelli is specifically दीपनी (agni-kindling) and लघु.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, Chinese (BCGM 1596): 除邪熱 (eliminates evil heat), 解勞乏 (relieves taxation fatigue), 清心明目 (clears the Heart and brightens the eyes). The 'clears the Heart' is a pre-1900 warrant for the Heart channel in the database's tcm_pattern_match; I found no pre-1900 warrant for the Spleen or Stomach entries it also claims, nor for the damp-heat and xiao ke framing, which should be marked inferred.

MAJOR ADDITION THE DATABASE MISSES — PART DISCIPLINE. Li Shizhen assigns the SEED a different qi-wei and an opposite action from the fruit: 「子氣味苦甘無毒。主治益氣壯陽。」 — the seed is bitter AND SWEET, non-toxic, and it BOOSTS QI AND INVIGORATES YANG. The fruit is a cold heat-clearer; the seed is a yang tonic. The row's part_used field currently steers users away from the seed on safety grounds (vicine, red aril) without recording that the classical text assigns it a distinct and opposite energetic. Both facts should stand together.

SPECIES DISCIPLINE, satisfied: BCGM 1596 describes 「結𤓰長者四五寸，短者二三寸，青色，皮上痱㿔如荔枝殻狀，熟則黄色自裂，内有紅瓤褁子」 — warty lychee-like skin, splitting yellow when ripe, RED ARIL wrapping the seeds. That is unambiguously Momordica charantia and not M. dioica.

UNANI CROSS-READING, pre-1900, gives ACTIONS only and NO temperature: Dymock, Warden and Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica, vol. II, 1891, p. 79, report that 'The author of the Makhzan-el-Adwiya describes the fruit as tonic and stomachic', with anthelmintic properties, and warn that 'some have erroneously supposed it to be identical with the Katha-el-himar of the Arabs, which is a violent purgative.' Tonic and stomachic are action words, not a thermal assignment, and must not be counted as one.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, pre-1900: Dymock 1891, p. 78, 'It requires, however, to be steeped in salt water before being cooked' — the classical de-bittering/tempering step. Same page records external application of the whole plant compounded with cinnamon, long pepper, rice and Hydnocarpus oil for scabies and cutaneous disease, and the leaf juice at one-eighth of a seer as an emetic and purgative in bilious affections.

results.pre1900_finding: No pre-1900 source assigns this fungus a temperature, because no pre-1900 source contains it. The Ben Cao Gang Mu 1596 mushroom section (卷二十八, 菜之五, 芝栭類) enumerates fifteen fungi — 芝, 木耳, 杉菌, 皂角蕈, 香蕈, 葛花菜, 天花蕈, 蘑菰蕈, 雞㙡, 舵菜, 土菌, 竹蓐, 雚菌, 地耳, 石耳 — and 雲芝 is NOT among them. Its 芝 entry is the 本經 six coloured zhi (青赤黃白黑紫), all Ganoderma-type, five of them 平 and 紫芝 甘溫. The Shennong Ben Cao Jing in the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension likewise carries only 赤芝, 青芝, 白芝, 黃芝, 黑芝, 紫芝. The only occurrence of the string 雲芝 anywhere in BCGM 卷28 is inside a quoted Baopuzi list of fabulous zhi names (青雲芝, 雲氣芝) with no temperature and no botanical content. CONSEQUENCE: the row's primary_text_citation — 'Li Shizhen, Ben Cao Gang Mu (Compendium of Materia Medica, 1596), Yun Zhi (the cloud mushroom, Trametes/Coriolus versicolor)' — describes an entry that does not exist. It should be struck. The row's secondary_citation is MSKCC About Herbs, Herbal Reality and modern oncology reviews, all post-1900 and inadmissible.

additions: Nothing can be harvested, because there is nothing to harvest from. 雲芝 as a drug name for Trametes versicolor is not attested in the pre-1900 Chinese materia medica I was able to reach. Any vipaka, guna, channel entry, Shennong grade, classical indication, preparation doctrine or contraindication now attached to Turkey Tail in the database is unsourceable to a pre-1900 primary and should be flagged as modern.

WHAT THE 芝 ENTRY WOULD GIVE IF THE FOUNDER EVER WANTS THE GANODERMA LINE INSTEAD, since it is genuinely 本經上品: SHENNONG GRADE 上品 (UPPER grade — the daily, long-term, non-toxic class, which is exactly the grade a daily-use product wants). Five of the six zhi are 平 (neutral), matching Turkey Tail's stored Neutral by coincidence rather than by evidence. 紫芝 is 甘溫, with 甄權 dissenting 平. Preparation and synergist doctrine, 之才 quoted in BCGM 1596: 「青赤黄白黒紫六芝，並以薯蕷為之使，得髪良，得蔴子仁、白瓜子、牡桂甚益人，惡常山，畏扁青、茵蔯蒿」. Indications for 紫芝 (本經): 「耳聾，利闗節，保神益精氣，堅筋骨，好顔色，久服輕身不老」. This is a DIFFERENT ORGANISM and must not be quietly substituted into the Turkey Tail row.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: either mark H243 as having no classical energetic lineage and present it honestly as a modern addition, or ask the founder whether the row should be rebuilt around a fungus that does have one. Do not let the fabricated BCGM 'Yun Zhi' citation ship.

results.pre1900_finding: Three independent pre-1900 sources all assign Longan 平, NEUTRAL, not warm. Shennong Ben Cao Jing (Sun Xingyan 1799 recension): 「味甘，平。」 Ben Cao Gang Mu 1596: 「實氣味甘平無毒」. Ben Cao Cong Xin 1757: 「甘平潤」. Li Shizhen goes further and makes the neutrality the whole point of the herb, contrasting it explicitly with lychee: 「荔枝性熱而龍眼性和平也」 — lychee's nature is HOT while longan's nature is harmonious and NEUTRAL. Only Su Gong dissents in the BCGM note (「恭曰甘酸温」). The stored 'Warm' therefore reproduces the minority reading and discards the one Li Shizhen argues for by name. The stored 'Moist' IS supported — Wu Yiluo 1757 writes 甘平潤, sweet, neutral, MOISTENING.
results.source_year: 1799 recension of a c. 200 CE text (Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan); 1596 (Bencao Gangmu); 1757 (Bencao Congxin)
results.evidence: (1) 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan 孫星衍 recension, 1799: 「龍眼　味甘，平。主五臟邪氣，安志厭食。久服，強魂、聰明、輕身、不老，通神明。一名益智。生山谷。《吳普》曰：龍眼，一名益智。《要術》：一名比目（《御覽》）。《名醫》曰：其大者，似檳榔。生南海松樹上。五月采，陰乾。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) . (2) Li Shizhen 李時珍, 本草綱目 (四庫全書本) 卷三十一, 龍眼, 1596: 「實氣味甘平無毒{{恭曰甘酸温。李廷飛曰：生者沸湯瀹過食，不動脾}}。主治五臟邪氣，安志厭食，除蠱毒，去三蟲，久服強魂聰明，身輕不老，通神明{{别録}}。開胃益脾，補虚長智{{時珍}}。」 and 發明: 「時珍曰：食品以荔枝為貴，而資益則龍眼為良。葢荔枝性熱而龍眼性和平也。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷31 . (3) Wu Yiluo 吳儀洛, 本草從新, 1757: 「龍眼肉　俗呼圓眼。補心脾。甘平潤。補心長智。（一名益智。）悦胃培脾。療健忘與怔忡。能安神而熟寐。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 中品, MIDDLE grade — but the sources disagree about which book it belongs to and the disagreement should be preserved, not resolved. Sun Xingyan's 1799 recension places 龍眼 in the 本經 middle grade (「上木，中品一十七種」). Li Shizhen tags the entry 「别録中品」, i.e. middle grade of the Mingyi Bielu rather than the 本經. Either way it is MIDDLE grade, not upper — a therapeutic-course herb by classical reckoning, not an indefinitely-daily one. That is a live constraint for a product that recommends daily herbs.

CHANNEL ENTRY (歸經), pre-1900: the 開寶本草 line quoted in BCGM 1596 states 「甘味歸脾，能益人智，故名益智」 — the sweet flavour RETURNS TO THE SPLEEN, hence the alias 益智 (benefits the wit). Wu Yiluo 1757 titles the entry 「補心脾」 — supplements HEART and SPLEEN, and states 「悦胃培脾」 (gladdens the stomach, banks up the spleen). So the database's Heart-and-Spleen assignment is correct and now has a pre-1900 warrant. Do NOT confuse this 益智 with 益智子 (Alpinia oxyphylla) — Tao Hongjing flags the collision in BCGM: 「廣州有龍眼，非益智也」.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom (本經/別錄 layer): 「主五臟邪氣，安志厭食，除蠱毒，去三蟲。久服強魂、聰明、輕身、不老，通神明。」 — governs evil qi of the five viscera, settles the will and quiets aversion to food, eliminates gu toxin, expels the three worms; long use strengthens the hun-soul, sharpens hearing and sight, lightens the body, prevents ageing, and opens communication with the spirit light. Li Shizhen's own addition: 「開胃益脾，補虚長智」.

FORMULA PROVENANCE, pre-1900, which validates a claim the database currently sources to a modern text: BCGM 1596 附方 prints 歸脾湯 in full and attributes it to 嚴用和, 濟生方 — 「治思慮過度，勞傷心脾，健忘怔忡，虚煩不眠，自汗驚悸。用龍眼肉、酸棗仁炒、黄茋炙、白术焙、伏神各一兩，木香半兩，炙甘草二錢半，㕮咀。每服五錢，薑三片、棗一枚，水二鍾煎一鍾温服。」 The database cites Yan Yonghe's Ji Sheng Fang (1253) for Gui Pi Tang; here is the 1596 text carrying the formula and its attribution.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, two distinct and both pre-1900. (a) BCGM 1596: 「其木性畏寒，白露後方可采摘，晒焙令乾成朶，乾者名龍眼錦」 — pick only after the White Dew solar term, then sun-dry and oven-dry in clusters. And 李廷飛曰：「生者沸湯瀹過食，不動脾」 — the FRESH fruit should be blanched in boiling water before eating, and then it will not disturb the spleen. (b) A Daoist method, Wu Yiluo 1757: 「道家用龍眼肉細嚼，待津液生，和津汨汨而咽，此即服玉泉之法也」 — chew the flesh slowly, wait for the saliva to well up, and swallow it together with the saliva; this is the method of ingesting the Jade Spring. Neither appears in the database.
ADDITIONAL PART, pre-1900, absent from the database: 「核主治胡臭。六枚同胡椒二七枚碾，遇汗出即擦之{{時珍}}」 — the SEED, six of them ground with fourteen peppercorns and rubbed on when sweat appears, governs body odour.

NO CONTRAINDICATION is stated in any of the three pre-1900 sources. Record that as an admitted gap. The one caution present is a food-preparation note (blanch the fresh fruit so it does not disturb the spleen), not a patient exclusion.

results.herb: Cordyceps (Dong Chong Xia Cao) — Ophiocordyceps sinensis
results.pre1900_finding: The database's own cited source says the opposite of what the database stores. Wu Yiluo's Ben Cao Cong Xin (1757) — named in this row's primary_text_citation — assigns Dong Chong Xia Cao 「甘平」, sweet and NEUTRAL, not warm. This is confirmed in a traditional-orthography pre-1900 witness: Wu Qijun's Zhiwu Mingshi Tukao (1848) quotes the Ben Cao Cong Xin verbatim as 「冬蟲夏草甘平」. Two pre-1900 texts, ninety-one years apart, both 平. The stored 'Warm' has no pre-1900 support that I could find, and the row's whole 'warms Kidney yang' framing rests on it. The row's secondary_citation is Bensky, MSKCC, RxList, Drugs.com and NCCIH — all post-1900 and inadmissible.
results.source_year: 1848 (Zhiwu Mingshi Tukao, traditional, quoting the 1757 Bencao Congxin); 1757 (Bencao Congxin)
results.evidence: (1) 吳其濬 Wu Qijun, 植物名實圖考 卷之十, 冬蟲夏草, 1848 (Daoguang woodblock recension, traditional characters, quoting the 1757 本草從新): 「冬蟲夏草。本草從新：冬蟲夏草甘平，保肺益腎，止血化痰，止勞嗽。產雲貴。冬在土中，身如老蠶，有毛能動，至夏則毛出土上，連身俱化為草，若不取，至冬復化為蟲。按此草兩廣多有之，根如蠶，葉似初生茅草，羊城中採以饌，云鮮美，蓋與啖禾蟲同。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/植物名實圖考_(道光刻本)/第十卷/冬蟲夏草 , text layer at https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:植物名實圖考(十).djvu/65 . (2) 吳儀洛 Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757, 卷一草部: 「冬虫夏草　補肺腎。甘平保肺。益腎止血。化痰已劳嗽。四川嘉定府所產者最佳。雲南贵州所出者次之。冬在土中。身活如老蚕。有毛能动。至夏則毛出土上。連身俱化爲草。若不取。至冬則復化爲虫。」 — https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新 (this transcription is partly simplified with variant glyphs, so it is used to LOCATE; the 1848 traditional witness above is the quotable text).
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: NONE, and this is a substantive finding rather than a gap. Dong Chong Xia Cao is absent from the Shennong Ben Cao Jing, the Zhenglei Bencao and the Ben Cao Gang Mu entirely. The 1757 Ben Cao Cong Xin is its first detailed materia medica description. It has no upper/middle/lower grade and therefore NO classical warrant for indefinite daily use. The database currently presents it as a building tonic for chronic depletion; the classical record gives no duration guidance at all, which should be said plainly rather than filled in.

CHANNEL ENTRY (歸經), pre-1900: Wu Yiluo 1757 heads the entry 「補肺腎」 — supplements LUNG and KIDNEY, and the 1848 quotation preserves 「保肺益腎」 (safeguards the Lung, boosts the Kidney). This confirms the database's Lung/Kidney assignment with a pre-1900 citation. It does NOT support the database's further claims that it tonifies Kidney YANG specifically, augments jing, or tonifies Lung yin — none of those terms appear.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, complete and short, in the source's own words: 「保肺益腎，止血化痰，止勞嗽」 — safeguards the Lung, boosts the Kidney, stops bleeding, transforms phlegm, stops taxation cough (劳嗽). That is the entire classical indication set. The database's impotence, cold sore low back and knees, low libido, fertility, premature ageing, dyspnoea, haemoptysis and convalescence list has NO pre-1900 warrant in the sources I read.

PROVENANCE / GRADING DOCTRINE, pre-1900 and commercially useful: Wu Yiluo 1757 grades the drug by origin — 「四川嘉定府所產者最佳。雲南贵州所出者次之。」 Sichuan (Jiading prefecture) material is BEST, Yunnan and Guizhou material second. Wu Qijun 1848 records the Guangdong reading differently (「產雲貴」) and adds a sceptical note that a plant sold under this name in the two Guang provinces is eaten as a delicacy in Guangzhou. A classical origin hierarchy the database does not carry.

NATURAL-HISTORY DOCTRINE, quoted because it is the classical rationale for the drug's name and reputation: 「冬在土中，身如老蠶，有毛能動，至夏則毛出土上，連身俱化為草，若不取，至冬復化為蟲」 — in winter it lies in the earth with a body like an aged silkworm, haired and able to move; by summer the hairs emerge above the soil and the whole body transforms into grass; if it is not gathered, by winter it turns back into a worm.

NO PREPARATION DOCTRINE and NO CONTRAINDICATION are stated in either pre-1900 source. Record both as admitted gaps. In particular, the database's claim that cultured Cs-4 mycelium carries comparable efficacy 'with less toxicity' is sourced to Bensky, a post-1900 text, and has no classical counterpart — the 1757 and 1848 texts describe only the wild whole caterpillar-fungus.

results.stored_temperature: Cool (classically sweet, bland, and slightly cool; some texts read it as slightly cold)
results.pre1900_finding: 氣味甘微寒無毒 — sweet, SLIGHTLY COLD (wei han), non-toxic. The classical head-reading is 微寒 in all three pre-1900 texts checked, not 涼 (cool). The DB has the emphasis inverted: it presents 'slightly cool' as the classical reading and 'slightly cold' as a minority view. The genuine minority view is 平 (NEUTRAL), recorded by Meng Shen inside Li Shizhen's own qi-wei line.
results.source_year: 1596 (BCGM); 1799 recension of a c. 200 CE text (SNBCJ); 1757 (BCCX)
results.evidence: Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (Bencao Gangmu), 1596, 卷23 穀之二, entry 薏苡仁 headed 【本經上品】: 「氣味甘微寒無毒」 with the inline dissent 「詵曰平」 (Meng Shen: neutral). Indications: 「主治筋急拘攣不可屈伸久風濕痺下氣久服輕身益氣」【本經】. URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷23 — CROSS-CHECK, Han layer: Shennong Bencao Jing in the Sun Xingyan & Sun Fengyi recension, 1799, s.v. 薏苡仁: 「味甘，微寒。主筋急，拘攣不可屈神[伸]，風濕痹，下氣。久服，輕身、益氣。其根，下三虫。」 URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) — CROSS-CHECK, Qing layer: Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757, s.v. 薏苡仁: 「甘淡微寒而屬土。陽明藥也。（胃、）」 URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 上品 (UPPER class). BCGM 1596 heads the entry 【本經上品】. The Sun Xingyan 1799 preamble defines what that means for duration of use: 「上藥一百二十種，為君，主養命以應天，無毒。多服、久服不傷人。欲輕身益氣，不老延年者，本上經。」 — 120 upper drugs, the sovereigns; non-toxic; TAKEN IN QUANTITY AND OVER LONG PERIODS THEY DO NOT INJURE. This is the strongest classical licence for daily use of any herb in this batch.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经): Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 發明: 「薏苡仁屬土陽明藥也故能健脾益胃」 — it belongs to Earth and is a YANGMING medicine. Su Song, quoted in the same 發明: 「薏苡仁心肺之藥」 — a HEART AND LUNG medicine. Wu Yiluo 1757 heads the entry 「補脾肺、通行水」 and glosses the channel as 「陽明藥也。（胃、）」. So the classical channel set is Yangming/Stomach plus Spleen, Lung and Heart — the DB records no channels at all.

TASTE, the 淡 (bland) claim verified: BCGM 1596 gives only 甘 (sweet). The bland quality the DB asserts is attested in Wu Yiluo 1757: 「甘淡微寒」, with the mechanism spelled out — 「甘益胃。土勝水。淡滲溼。瀉水所以益土。故健脾。」 (sweet benefits the Stomach; Earth overcomes Water; the BLAND percolates damp; draining water is how it benefits Earth, hence it strengthens the Spleen).

PREPARATION DOCTRINE: Lei Xiao, quoted in BCGM 1596 修治: 「凡使每一兩以糯米一兩同炒熟去糯米用亦有更以鹽湯煮過者」 — for every liang, dry-fry with an equal liang of glutinous rice, then discard the rice; some also boil it in salt water first. Wu Yiluo 1757: 「炒熟微研」 (fry until done, grind lightly).

DOSE DOCTRINE: both texts warn the drug is weak. BCGM 1596 發明, Kou Zongshi: 「此藥力勢和緩凡用須加倍即見效」. Wu Yiluo 1757: 「其力和緩。用之須倍於他藥。」 — its force is mild and slow, it MUST BE DOSED AT DOUBLE other herbs to show effect.

CONTRAINDICATIONS, classically stated and CONTESTED: Wu Yiluo, 本草從新 1757: 「大便燥结。因寒筋急。勿用。」 — do not use in dry constipation, nor where the cramping is caused by COLD. This descends from Kou Zongshi in BCGM 1596 發明: 「若素問言因寒則筋急者不可更用此也」. Wang Ang, 本草備要 1694, rejects it: 「《衍義》云∶因寒筋急者不可用，恐不然」 (locate-only text, simplified with dropped glyphs — not quotable as the 1694 wording). Report both; do not adjudicate.

PREGNANCY: the DB attributes the pregnancy contraindication to a 2013 modern source. Wang Ang, 本草備要 1694, states it classically — 「杀蛔堕胎」 (kills roundworm, CAUSES ABORTION). Flagged as a LEAD, not a citation: that Wikisource transcription is simplified with dropped glyphs and is locate-only. A traditional scan is needed before this can be quoted.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom, layered by attribution in BCGM 1596: 本經 — 「筋急拘攣不可屈伸久風濕痺下氣久服輕身益氣」; 別錄 — 「除筋骨中邪氣不仁利腸胃消水腫令人能食」; 甄權 — 「治肺痿肺氣積膿血欬嗽涕唾上氣煎服破毒腫」; 孟詵 — 「去乾濕脚氣大驗」; 時珍 — 「徤脾益胃補肺清熱去風勝濕炊飯食治冷氣煎飲利小便熱淋」.

results.pre1900_finding: NO PRE-1900 SOURCE ASSIGNS THIS HERB A VIRYA. The Bhavaprakasha Nighantu verse — the classical locus, quoted verbatim in a pre-1900 printed Sanskrit lexicon — gives rasa, guna and karma but NO ushna and NO sita/hima. Five pre-1900 works were searched in full text (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu 16th c. Sanskrit; Vachaspatyam 1873-84; Dutt 1877; Dymock 1890; Watt 1891; Wise 1845) and not one states a potency. What the classical verse DOES assign is madhura + tikta rasa, GURU (heavy) guna, and — in direct tension with a hot potency — कफपित्तास्रनाशिनी, destroying kapha AND pitta.
results.source_year: 16th century (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, Sanskrit original); attested in print 1873-1884 (Vachaspatyam)
results.evidence: Bhavamishra, भावप्रकाशनिघण्टुः (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu), 16th century, गुडूच्यादिवर्गः verses 129-131, Sanskrit original: 「कपिच्छूरात्मगुप्ता वृष्या प्रोक्ता च मर्कटी । अजडा कण्डुरा व्यङ्गा दुःस्पर्शा प्रावृषायणी ॥१२९॥ लाङ्गली शूकशिम्बी च सैव प्रोक्ता महर्षिभिः । कपिकच्छूर्भृशं वृष्या मधुरा बृंहणी गुरुः । तिक्ता वातहरी बल्या कफपित्तास्रनाशिनी ॥४.१३०॥ तद्बीजं वातशमनं स्मृतं वाजीकरं परम् ॥१३१॥」 URL: https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/भावप्रकाशः/पूर्वखण्डे_भावप्रकाशनिघण्टुः — PRE-1900 PRINTED ATTESTATION of that exact verse, with attribution: Taranatha Tarkavachaspati, वाचस्पत्यम् (Vachaspatyam), 1873-1884, s.v. कपिकच्छू: 「तद्गुणा भावप्र० उक्ता यथा “कपिकच्छूर्भृशं वृष्या मधुरा ष्टंहणो[बृंहणी] गुरुः । तिक्ता वातहरी वल्या[बल्या] कफपित्तास्रनाशिनी । तद्वीजं वातशमनं स्मृतं वाजीकरं परम्”」 URL: https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/वाचस्पत्यम्/कदन — CORROBORATING NEGATIVES: Uday Chand Dutt, The Materia Medica of the Hindus, 1877, pp. 147-148, gives Susruta and the Bhavaprakasha on this drug and assigns no potency: "Susruta describes the seeds as a powerful aphrodisiac" (https://archive.org/download/materiamedicaofh00duttuoft/materiamedicaofh00duttuoft_djvu.txt). Dymock, Warden & Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica, 1890, I.447, likewise none.
additions: GUNA, explicitly given where virya is not: गुरु (guru, HEAVY) and बृंहणी (brimhani, bulk-building / anabolic). The DB records moisture as 'Moist' with no source; the pre-1900 text gives HEAVY, which is a different axis and is stated outright.

VIPAKA: NOT STATED in any pre-1900 source found. The DB asserts 'post-digestive taste (vipaka) is Sweet (Madhura)'. The Bhavaprakasha Nighantu verse gives no vipaka for Kapikacchu, and neither does Vachaspatyam 1873-84 quoting it. This is an unsourced modern attribution.
RASA: मधुरा (madhura, sweet) AND तिक्ता (tikta, bitter). The DB says 'Sweet (Madhura) ... with a Bitter (Tikta) edge' — this part IS confirmed by the 16th-century verse.

DOSHA ACTION, and it cuts against the stored 'hot': the verse reads वातहरी (removes vata) and कफपित्तास्रनाशिनी (destroys KAPHA, PITTA and rakta/blood disorders). A drug of ushna virya would be expected to provoke pitta, not destroy it. The DB's own hedge ('some describe it as broadly tridoshic') is closer to the classical text than its headline 'Warm'.

PART DISCIPLINE: the verse separates plant and seed. 4.130 describes कपिकच्छू (the plant/drug generally); 4.131 singles out the seed — 「तद्बीजं वातशमनं स्मृतं वाजीकरं परम्」, THE SEED is remembered as vata-pacifying and the SUPREME vajikarana. The specifically aphrodisiac claim is the seed's, per the classical text.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, verbatim from a pre-1900 source. The Bhavaprakasha's वानरी वटी, as given by Dutt 1877 p.148: "Take of the seeds of Mucuna pruriens thirty two tolas, boil them in four seers of cow's milk till the latter becomes thick. The seeds should now be decorticated and pounded, then fried in clarified butter and made into a confection with double their weight of sugar. The mass should then be divided into balls which should be steeped in honey. Dose, about a tola." Milk-boiling, decortication and ghee-frying are doctrine, not options — the raw seed is not the drug.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, Sushruta layer, via Dutt 1877 p.147: the seeds are aphrodisiac, given with the fruits of Tribulus terrestris (gokshura) in equal parts, about a drachm, with sugar and tepid milk. ROOT (a separate drug the DB treats as 'minor'): Dutt 1877 p.148 — "The root of Mucuna pruriens is considered tonic and useful in diseases of the nervous system, such as facial paralysis, hemiplegia etc.", used in the compound decoction Masha-baladi kvatha.

SPECIES/USE CORRECTION, load-bearing. The DB states the stinging pod hairs 'are used traditionally as a mechanical anthelmintic to dislodge intestinal worms', implying Indian tradition. Dymock, Warden & Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica, 1890, I.447-448 contradicts this squarely: "The use of the hairs of the Mucuna pod as a vermifuge to expel ascarides appears to have originated in the West Indies, no mention of such an employment of them being found in native Indian works. They were introduced to the notice of English physicians by Bancroft about 1769". Watt, Dictionary of the Economic Products of India, 1891, V.287 repeats the finding independently. The anthelmintic use is a West Indian import, not Ayurvedic.
SANSKRIT SYNONYM SET as the classical text gives it (useful for further source work): कपिच्छू, आत्मगुप्ता, मर्कटी, अजडा, कण्डुरा, व्यङ्गा, दुःस्पर्शा, प्रावृषायणी, लाङ्गली, शूकशिम्बी.

CITATION HYGIENE: the DB's primary_text_citation for this herb is Grieve, A Modern Herbal, 1931 — a forbidden post-1900 source — and its secondary is the modern Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia plus a 2004 clinical paper. Neither can support the temperature. No pre-1900 replacement exists for that field.

results.pre1900_finding: 氣味甘平無毒 — sweet, NEUTRAL (ping), non-toxic. Two independent pre-1900 Chinese texts agree exactly, and the Han-dynasty layer and the 1596 compendium give the identical reading with no dissent recorded by either.
results.source_year: 1596 (BCGM); 1799 recension of a c. 200 CE text (SNBCJ)
results.evidence: Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (Bencao Gangmu), 1596, 卷35下 木之二, entry 合歡 headed 【本經中品】: 「木皮」【去粗皮炒用】「氣味甘平無毒主治安五臟和心志令人歡樂無憂久服輕身眀目得所欲」【本經】. URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷35下 — CROSS-CHECK, Han layer: Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan & Sun Fengyi recension, 1799, s.v. 合歡: 「味甘，平。主安五臟，利心志（《藝文類聚》作和心志，《御覽》作和心氣）。令人獻[歡]樂無憂。久服，輕身、明目、[得]所欲。生山谷。」 URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍)
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 中品 (MIDDLE class), and this is now verified two ways. BCGM 1596 heads the entry 【本經中品】, and in the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension the 合歡 entry is the last of its group, immediately followed by the tally line 「上木，中品一十七種，舊同。」 Duration-of-use meaning, from the 1799 middle-grade preamble: 「中藥一百二十種為臣，主養性以應人。無毒、有毒，斟酌其宜。欲遏病補羸者，本中經」 — the ministers; nurture the disposition; SOME ARE TOXIC AND SOME NOT, SO WEIGH THEIR SUITABILITY. Middle grade is not the open-ended daily licence that 上品 is.

THE DB'S OWN CLAIM, now verified verbatim in the original. The tcm_pattern_match field asserts the Shennong records the bark as 'comforting the five zang, harmonizing the mind and will, and making one joyful and free of worry' but cites no text. The actual line is 「安五臟和心志令人歡樂無憂久服輕身眀目得所欲」 (BCGM 1596, attributed 【本經】). The paraphrase is accurate. The last clause the DB drops is 得所欲 — 'one obtains what one desires'.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, stated inline in the qi-wei header itself: 「木皮」【去粗皮炒用】 — the BARK, with the coarse outer bark removed, DRY-FRIED before use. For fractures the 附方 specifies frying further: 「夜合樹皮即合歡皮去粗皮炒黑色四兩芥菜子炒一兩爲末每服二錢温酒卧時服以滓傅之接骨甚妙」 (Wang Qiu, 百一選方, quoted in BCGM 1596) — fried to BLACK, with mustard seed, two qian in warm wine at bedtime, the dregs applied externally.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS by attribution layer, BCGM 1596: 本經 — quiets the five zang, harmonizes heart and will, makes one joyful and free of worry, long use lightens the body and brightens the eyes; 大明 — 「煎膏消癰腫續筋骨」 (decoct to a paste, disperses abscesses and swellings, knits sinew and bone); 陳藏器 — 「殺蟲搗末和鐺下墨生油調塗蜘蛛咬瘡用葉洗衣垢」; 寇宗奭 — 「折傷疼痛研末酒服二錢匕」; 時珍 — 「和血消腫止痛」. Note how much of this record is TRAUMA and ABSCESS medicine; the DB's 'happiness bark' framing captures only the 本經 line.

ADDITIONAL CLASSICAL THEORY: Zhu Zhenheng, quoted in BCGM 1596 發明: 「合歡属土補陰之功甚㨗長肌肉續筋骨概可見矣與白蠟同入膏用神效而外科家末曾錄用何也」 — it belongs to EARTH, its power to supplement YIN is very swift; combined with white wax in a paste it is marvellously effective, and he complains the external-medicine specialists have never recorded its use.

THE FLOWER is a separate classical drug and BCGM 1596 gives it no independent qi-wei line in this entry; the 附方 uses 夜合花枝 (flowering branch) decocted for infant lockjaw. The DB describes He Huan Hua as 'a gentler, more purely spirit-calming preparation' — that characterisation is NOT in the 1596 text.
NO CONTRAINDICATION is stated in either pre-1900 source. Record that as an absence, not as safety.

CITATION HYGIENE: the DB's primary_text_citation for this herb is internally broken — the author field reads 'King's American Dispensatory' with year 1898 and a henriettes-herb.com URL, while the title field describes the Shennong Bencao Jing. results.pre1900_finding: 莖葉氣味辛温無毒 — stem and leaf: acrid, WARM, non-toxic. Confirmed in the 1596 compendium and independently in 1757. Separately: Perilla is NOT in the Shennong Bencao Jing at all, contrary to the DB's citation — BCGM heads it 【别錄中品】.
results.evidence: Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (Bencao Gangmu), 1596, 卷14 草之三, entry 蘇 headed 【别錄中品】, 釋名 紫蘇: 「莖葉氣味辛温無毒」【李廷飛曰不可同鯉魚食生毒瘡】; seed separately 「子氣味辛温無毒」.
