additions: GRADE / PROVENANCE CORRECTION: 別錄中品 — first recorded in the 名醫別錄 (Mingyi Bielu, c. 500 CE) at MIDDLE grade, NOT in the Shennong Bencao Jing. The DB's primary_text_citation names the author as 'Shennong Ben Cao Jing' with year 'c. 200 CE'. That attribution is wrong on the herb's own terms and the 1799 Shennong recension says so explicitly.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经): Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 發明: 「紫蘇近世要藥也其味辛入氣分其色紫入血分」 — its acrid taste enters the QI ASPECT, its purple colour enters the BLOOD ASPECT. Su Song, quoted in the same entry: 「通心經益脾胃煑飲尤勝與橘皮相宜」 — opens the HEART channel, benefits Spleen and Stomach. The DB records 'Lung and Spleen' with no source; the 1596 text gives qi-aspect/blood-aspect plus Heart, Spleen and Stomach.

CONTRAINDICATION AGAINST DAILY USE — the single most important finding for a product recommending daily herbs, and it is stated twice in BCGM 1596 發明. Wang Ji: 「宋仁宗命翰林院定湯飲奏曰紫蘇熟水第一以其能下胸膈浮氣也盖不知其久則泄人真氣焉」 — Emperor Renzong's academy ranked perilla water the finest of drinks, not knowing that TAKEN LONG IT DRAINS A PERSON'S TRUE QI. Kou Zongshi: 「今人朝暮飲紫蘇湯甚無益醫家謂芳草致豪貴之疾者此有一焉若脾胃寒人多致滑泄往往不覺」 — people who drink perilla decoction morning and evening get no benefit at all; this is one of the 'aromatic herbs that bring on the diseases of the rich'; those with a COLD SPLEEN AND STOMACH often fall into slippery diarrhoea without noticing. Wu Yiluo 1757 restates it and adds a flat prohibition: 「氣虚表虚者禁之。（俗喜其芳香、旦暮恣食、不知泄真元之氣、古稱芳草致豪贵之疾、此類是也。）」 — FORBIDDEN in qi deficiency and exterior deficiency.

DIETARY INCOMPATIBILITY, classically stated inside the qi-wei line: 李廷飛曰不可同鯉魚食生毒瘡 (BCGM 1596) — must not be eaten with CARP, it raises poisonous sores. Wu Yiluo 1757 compresses it to a rule: 「宜橘皮。忌鯉魚。」 — suits tangerine peel; AVOID CARP.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE: Lei Xiao, quoted in BCGM 1596 集解: 「薄荷根莖真似紫蘇但葉不同爾薄荷莖燥紫蘓莖和入藥須以刀刮去青薄皮用之」 — mint and perilla stems look alike; for the perilla stem, scrape off the thin green skin with a knife before use. Su Song: 「若宣通風毒則單用莖去節尢良」 — to disperse wind-toxin use the stem alone with the nodes removed.

PART DISCIPLINE, three drugs with separate readings in BCGM 1596: 莖葉 (stem and leaf) 辛温無毒 — releases the exterior; 子 (seed) 辛温無毒, 「主治下氣除寒温中」【别錄】 — descends qi. Wu Yiluo 1757 adds the stem as a third: 「蘇梗（宣、順氣。）順氣安胎。功力稍緩、挟虛者宜之。」 and gives each its own contraindication: 「表弱氣虚者忌用葉，腸滑氣虚者忌用子」 (per BCBY 1694, same doctrine) — the LEAF is forbidden in weak exterior and qi deficiency; the SEED is forbidden in slippery intestines and qi deficiency.

PAIRING DOCTRINE, Li Shizhen BCGM 1596 發明, verbatim: 「同橘皮砂仁則行氣安胎同藿香烏藥則温中止痛同香附麻黃則發汗解肌同芎藭當歸則和血散血同木瓜厚朴則散濕解暑治霍亂脚氣同桔梗枳殻則利膈寛膓同杏仁菜菔子則消痰定喘也」 — the same herb is steered to seven different actions by its partner. Note the first pair is with Sha Ren (H265 in this batch).

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS by layer, BCGM 1596: 別錄 — 「下氣除寒中其子尤良」; 孟詵 — 「除寒熱治一切冷氣」; 日華 — 「補中益氣治心腹脹滿止霍亂轉筋開胃下食止脚氣通大小膓」; 甄權 — 「以葉生食作羮殺一切魚肉毒」; 時珍 — 「解肌發表散風寒行氣寛中消痰利肺和血温中止痛定喘安胎解魚蟹毒治蛇犬傷」. The seafood-antidote use the DB mentions is well attested: 食蟹中毒 — 「紫蘇煑汁飲二升」【金匱要略】.

results.pre1900_finding: काञ्चनारो हिमो ग्राही तुवरः — Kanchanara is HIMA (cold), grahi (checking/absorbent), tuvara (astringent). The classical word is हिम (hima), a synonym of शीत (sita) rather than sita itself. The cold potency is confirmed by the 16th-century Sanskrit verse and by two independent pre-1900 printed lexicons that quote it with attribution.
results.source_year: 16th century (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, Sanskrit original); attested in print 1819-1858 (Shabdakalpadruma) and 1873-1884 (Vachaspatyam); species fixed 1877 (Dutt)
results.evidence: Bhavamishra, भावप्रकाशनिघण्टुः (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu), 16th century, गुडूच्यादिवर्गः verses 101-104, Sanskrit original: 「काञ्चनारः काञ्चनको गण्डारिः शोणपुष्पकः ॥१०१॥ कोविदारश्च मरिकः कुद्दालो युगपत्रकः । कुण्डली ताम्रपुष्पश्चाश्मन्तकः स्वल्पकेशरी ॥१०२॥ काञ्चनारो हिमो ग्राही तुवरः श्लेष्मपित्तनुत् । कृमिकुष्ठगुदभ्रंशगण्डमालाव्रणापहः ॥१०३॥ कोविदारोऽपि तद्वत्स्यात्तयोः पुष्पं लघु स्मृतम् । रूक्षं संग्राहि पित्तास्रप्रदरक्षयकासनुत् ॥१०४॥」 URL: https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/भावप्रकाशः/पूर्वखण्डे_भावप्रकाशनिघण्टुः — PRE-1900 PRINTED ATTESTATION 1: Radhakanta Deb, शब्दकल्पद्रुमः (Shabdakalpadruma), 1819-1858, s.v. कोविदारः, quoting and naming its source: 「काञ्चनालो हिमो ग्राही तुवरः श्लेष्मपित्तनुत् । कृमिकुष्ठगुदभ्रंशगण्डमालाव्रणापहः ॥ कोविदारोऽपि तद्वत्स्यात् तयोः पुष्पं लघु स्मृतम् । रूक्षं संग्राहि पित्तास्रप्रदरक्षयकासनुत्” ॥ इति भावप्रकाशः ।」 URL: https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/शब्दकल्पद्रुमः/केरली — PRE-1900 PRINTED ATTESTATION 2: Taranatha Tarkavachaspati, वाचस्पत्यम् (Vachaspatyam), 1873-1884, s.v. काञ्चन: 「काञ्चनारो हिमग्राही तुवरः श्लेष्मपित्तनुत् । कृमिकुष्ठगुदभ्रंशगण्डमालाव्रणापहः ...” भावप्र० तत्पर्य्यायभेदगुणाद्युक्तम् ।」 URL: https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/वाचस्पत्यम्/काग — SPECIES ANCHOR: Uday Chand Dutt, The Materia Medica of the Hindus, 1877, p.156: "BAUHINIA VARIEGATA, Linn. Sans. Kanchanara, Kovidara. Vern. Kachnar, Hind. Rakta Kanchan, Beng."
additions: PART DISCIPLINE — the DB attributes GUNA to the wrong part. It records 'Guna: Laghu, Ruksa (light, dry)' for the STEM BARK, citing the modern Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia. In the 16th-century verse those two gunas belong to the FLOWER: 「तयोः पुष्पं लघु स्मृतम् । रूक्षं संग्राहि...」 — the FLOWER of the two is remembered as LAGHU (light) and RUKSHA (dry). The verse assigns the bark itself no guna at all. Same structural error the project already documented for Gou Qi Zi.

VIPAKA: NOT STATED in any pre-1900 source found. The DB asserts 'vipaka is Pungent (Katu)' and builds its whole 'decongesting, kapha-drying after-action' reading on it, citing the modern government Pharmacopoeia. The Bhavaprakasha verse gives no vipaka, and neither does the Shabdakalpadruma nor the Vachaspatyam quoting it. Unsourced modern attribution.

RASA CONFIRMED: तुवर (tuvara) = kashaya, ASTRINGENT. This is the only rasa the verse gives. The DB adds 'with a Bitter (Tikta) alterative edge' — तिक्त is NOT in the classical verse. The 'alterative' descriptor traces to the colonial English translators (Dutt 1877 p.156: "described as alterative, tonic, astringent"), and alterative is an action word, not a taste.

DOSHA ACTION IS CONTESTED between two classical nighantus and must not be collapsed. Bhavaprakasha (16th c.): श्लेष्मपित्तनुत् — removes KAPHA and PITTA (this is what the DB records). Rajanighantu, quoted in the Shabdakalpadruma 1819-58 immediately after the Bhavaprakasha verse: 「अस्य गुणाः । कषायत्वम् । संग्राहित्वम् । व्रणरोपणत्वम् ॥ दीपनत्वम् । कफवातमूत्रकृच्छ्रनाशित्वञ्च । इति राजनिर्घण्टः ॥」 — astringency, checking, WOUND-HEALING, DIPANA (digestive-kindling), and destroying KAPHA, VATA and dysuria. Kapha-pitta versus kapha-vata is a real divergence. Report both.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom, from the 16th-century verse: कृमि (worms), कुष्ठ (kushtha, the skin-disease class), गुदभ्रंश (guda-bhramsha, RECTAL PROLAPSE), गण्डमाला (ganda-mala, SCROFULA / cervical glandular chains), व्रण (vrana, ulcers). The glandular/lymphatic indication the DB centres its monograph on is directly and verbatim in the 16th-century Sanskrit — it does not need the modern Pharmacopoeia to support it. Note गुदभ्रंश, rectal prolapse, which the DB does not carry at all.

FLOWER as a separate drug: 「पित्तास्रप्रदरक्षयकासनुत्」 — the flower dispels pitta-and-blood disorders, PRADARA (menorrhagia), KSHAYA (wasting) and KASA (cough), and is संग्राहि (checking). Rajavallabha, quoted in Shabdakalpadruma 1819-58: 「तत्पुष्पगुणाः । धारकत्वम् । रुचिकारित्वम् । रक्तपित्तरोगे सुपथ्यत्वञ्च ।」 — retaining, appetising, and highly suitable in raktapitta.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, pre-1900, two named classical formulas. Chakradatta, via Dutt 1877 p.156: the bark of the red variety "to be rubbed into an emulsion with rice water and administered, with the addition of ginger, in scrofulous enlargement of the glands of the neck." Sarangadhara's Kanchanara guggulu, via Dutt 1877 pp.156-157: "Take of the bark of Bauhinia variegata, eighty tolas, the three myrobalans sixty tolas, ginger, black pepper, long pepper and the bark of Crataeva religiosa (varuna), eight tolas each, cardamoms, cinnamon, and tejpatra leaves, each two tolas, powder them all and rub together with guggulu." The DB names this formula but cites it to the modern tradition; it is in Dutt 1877.

SPECIES CAUTION: the Sanskrit tradition treats Kanchanara/Kanchanala and Kovidara as a WHITE/RED pair, and the Bhavaprakasha says outright 「कोविदारोऽपि तद्वत्स्यात्」 — Kovidara is likewise. Shabdakalpadruma 1819-58 glosses कोविदारः as रक्तकाञ्चनवृक्षः, the RED kanchan tree. The equation of Kanchanara with Bauhinia variegata specifically is the colonial botanists' determination (Dutt 1877, Dymock 1890 I.536), not the nighantu's. The cold-potency verse therefore covers B. variegata AND B. acuminata/purpurea equally.
NO CONTRAINDICATION is stated in any pre-1900 source found for this herb. Record the absence.

CITATION HYGIENE: the DB's primary_text_citation is the modern Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India (ayush.gov.in, 'ongoing') — a forbidden modern government standard. Every element of it except vipaka and the bark-guna can now be replaced with a pre-1900 primary.

results.pre1900_finding: 葉莖根子氣味苦寒無毒 — leaf, stem, root and seed: bitter, COLD, non-toxic. Identical in the Han-dynasty layer (味苦，寒) and in 1596 and 1757. No dissenting reading recorded anywhere.
results.source_year: 1596 (BCGM); 1799 recension of a c. 200 CE text (SNBCJ); 1757 (BCCX)
results.evidence: Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (Bencao Gangmu), 1596, 卷15 草之四, entry 青蒿 headed 【本經下品】, 釋名 草蒿: 「葉莖根子氣味苦寒無毒」【時珍曰伏硫黄】. The seed is given separately and differently: 「子氣味甘冷無毒主治明目開胃炒用治勞瘦壯徤人」. URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷15 — CROSS-CHECK, Han layer: Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan & Sun Fengyi recension, 1799, s.v. 草蒿: 「味苦，寒。主疥瘙、痂癢、惡創，殺虫，留熱在骨節間，明目。一名青蒿，一名方潰。生川澤。」 URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) — CROSS-CHECK, Qing layer: Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757, s.v. 青蒿: 「苦寒。得春木少陽之令最早。（二月生苗。）故入少陽、厥陰血分。（肝、胆。）」 URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 下品 (LOWER class) — the single most consequential finding in this batch for a product recommending daily herbs. BCGM 1596 heads the entry 【本經下品】, and in the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension 草蒿 sits in 卷三·下經 among the 草 lower-grade drugs. The 1799 lower-grade preamble states what that means: 「下藥，一百二十五種，為左使。主治病以應地。多毒，不可久服。欲除寒熱邪氣，破積聚，愈疾者，本下經。」 — 125 lower drugs, the assistants; they TREAT DISEASE; MANY ARE TOXIC AND THEY MUST NOT BE TAKEN OVER LONG PERIODS. Classical grade forbids open-ended daily use of this herb. The DB carries no grade field and no duration signal.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), stated as a doctrine with a reason, not a list. Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 發明: 「青蒿得春木少陽之氣最早故所主之證皆少陽厥隂血分之病也」 — it receives the SHAOYANG qi of spring-wood earliest, therefore every pattern it governs is a disease of the SHAOYANG and JUEYIN BLOOD ASPECT. Wu Yiluo 1757 repeats it and names the organs: 「故入少陽、厥陰血分。（肝、胆。）」 — Liver and Gallbladder. The DB adds KIDNEY to that list; no pre-1900 source found supports the Kidney channel.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, and it is severe. Lei Xiao, quoted in BCGM 1596 修治: 「凡使惟中為妙到膝即仰到腰即俛使子勿使葉使根勿使莖四件若同使翻然成痼疾采得葉用七嵗兒七箇溺浸七日七夜漉出晒乾」 — use only the MIDDLE portion; USE THE SEED, NOT THE LEAF; USE THE ROOT, NOT THE STEM; IF ALL FOUR ARE USED TOGETHER IT TURNS INTO A CHRONIC DISEASE. Then steep the gathered leaves seven days and seven nights in the urine of seven seven-year-old boys, strain, sun-dry. Wu Yiluo 1757 preserves the core rule verbatim: 「使子勿使葉。使根勿使茎。熬膏良。」 — and prefers it reduced to a paste.

DO-NOT-BOIL DOCTRINE — the Ge Hong method, verbatim in BCGM 1596 附方 under 瘧疾寒熱: 「肘後方用青蒿一握水二升絞汁服之」 — Zhou Hou Bei Ji Fang: one handful of qinghao, two sheng of water, WRING OUT THE JUICE and drink it. Not decocted. The DB's primary citation names the Zhou Hou Fang but does not carry the method, which is precisely the point on which the herb's activity turns.

ADDITIONAL PREPARATION VEHICLES, repeatedly specified: 童子小便 (boys' urine) for the steaming-bone and exhaustion indications — 「青蒿細剉水三升童子小便五升同煎取一升半」【斗門方】; and 熬膏 (reduction to a paste) as the preferred form in 1757.

CONTRAINDICATIONS, classically stated: Wu Yiluo, 本草從新 1757: 「凡苦寒藥。多與胃家不利。惟青蒿芬芳袭脾。宜於血虚有熱之人。以其不犯冲和之氣爾。寒而泄瀉者。仍當避之。」 — bitter-cold drugs are generally bad for the Stomach; qinghao is the exception because its fragrance reaches the Spleen and it does not offend the harmonising qi; but THOSE WITH COLD AND DIARRHOEA MUST STILL AVOID IT. The DB records no contraindication at all.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS by layer, BCGM 1596: 本經 — 「疥瘙痂痒惡瘡殺蝨治留熱在骨節間明目」; 陳藏器 — 「鬼氣尸疰伏留婦人血氣腹内滿及冷熱久痢秋冬用子春夏用苖」 (note the SEASONAL part rule: seed in autumn and winter, seedling in spring and summer); 大明 — 「補中益氣輕身補勞駐顔色長毛髪令黒不老」; 蘇恭 — 「生擣傅金瘡止血止疼良」; 時珍 — 「治瘧疾寒熱」. Su Song, 發明: 「青蒿治骨蒸勢[熱]勞為最古方單用之」 — for steaming-bone exhaustion fever it is supreme, and the old formulas used it ALONE.
PART DISCIPLINE: the SEED has its own and different reading in BCGM 1596 — 「子氣味甘冷無毒」, SWEET and 冷 (cold), against the leaf/stem/root's 苦寒. Different taste, different character of cold.
CHEMICAL/PROCESSING NOTE from Li Shizhen inside the qi-wei line: 伏硫黄 — it subdues sulphur.

SPECIES CAUTION already visible in the 1596 text: BCGM gives 黄花蒿 (釋名 臭蒿) as a SEPARATE adjacent entry from 青蒿. Shen Kuo, quoted in 集解: 「青蒿一類自有二種一種黄色一種青色本草謂之青蒿亦有所别也」 — the classical tradition already distinguished a yellow-flowered from a green kind. The modern identification of Qing Hao with Artemisia annua sits across that classical split; the DB should not treat the 1596 entry as a clean one-to-one match.

results.pre1900_finding: 葉氣味苦甘寒有小毒 — the leaf is bitter, sweet, COLD (寒 not 涼), and SLIGHTLY TOXIC — with an explicit dissent printed alongside it: 大明曰家桑葉煖無毒 (Da Ming: the CULTIVATED mulberry leaf is WARM and non-toxic). Three separate refinements are needed: the reading is cold not cool; a 有小毒 the DB omits entirely; and a directly contested reading spanning cold to warm. Separately, the Shennong assigns the LEAF no temperature at all — the 甘寒 the DB's citation leans on belongs to the ROOT BARK.
results.source_year: 1596 (BCGM); 1799 recension of a c. 200 CE text (SNBCJ)
results.evidence: Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (Bencao Gangmu), 1596, 卷36 木之三, entry 桑 headed 【本經中品】, leaf sub-entry: 「葉氣味苦甘寒有小毒」【大明曰家桑葉煖無毒】「主治除寒熱出汗」【本經】. URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷36 — THE SHENNONG LAYER, which does NOT support a leaf temperature: Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan & Sun Fengyi recension, 1799, s.v. 桑根白皮: 「味甘，寒。主傷中、五勞六極、羸瘦，崩中脈絕，補虛益氣。葉：主除寒熱出汗。」 — the 甘寒 governs 桑根白皮, the ROOT BARK; the leaf is given an indication and no potency. URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) — Note also BCGM 1596's own root-bark line carries four competing readings: 「氣味甘寒無毒」【權曰平大明曰温元素曰苦酸杲曰甘辛寒可升可降陽中...】
additions: CHANNEL ENTRY (归经) — the DB is CONTRADICTED here. It records 'Sang Ye enters the Lung and Liver channels.' Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 發明, states: 「桑葉乃手足陽明之藥汁煎代茗能止消渴」 — mulberry leaf is a HAND-AND-FOOT YANGMING medicine (Large Intestine and Stomach). No pre-1900 source found assigns the leaf to Lung and Liver.

THE BLOOD-SUGAR CLAIM HAS A PRE-1900 ROOT, and it is in the same sentence: 「汁煎代茗能止消渴」 — decocted and drunk IN PLACE OF TEA it stops 消渴 (xiao ke, wasting-thirst). The DB attributes the post-meal glucose effect to a modern NCCIH/clinical citation; Li Shizhen 1596 states the indication and the vehicle. Meng Shen, quoted in the same entry, gives the preparation: 「炙熟煎飲代茶止渴」 — roast until done, decoct, drink as tea, stops thirst.

SHENNONG GRADE: 中品 (MIDDLE class) — BCGM 1596 heads the tree 【本經中品】, and in the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension 桑根白皮 sits in 卷二·中經. Duration meaning, 1799 preamble: 「中藥一百二十種為臣，主養性以應人。無毒、有毒，斟酌其宜。」 — weigh their suitability, some being toxic. Note this grade attaches to the ROOT BARK entry, under which the leaf is subordinate.

TOXICITY, entirely absent from the DB: 有小毒 (slightly toxic) in the leaf's own qi-wei line, BCGM 1596. Da Ming's dissent restricts it — 家桑葉煖無毒, the CULTIVATED (as opposed to wild) mulberry leaf is warm and non-toxic. If the product uses cultivated Morus alba leaf, Da Ming's reading is the applicable one and it is WARM, not cool. This is a live contradiction requiring a founder decision, not a silent pick.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — harvest timing is doctrine, not detail. Su Song, BCGM 1596 發明: 「以四月桑茂盛時采葉又十月霜後三分二分已落時一分在者名神仙葉即采取與前葉同隂么擣末丸散任服或煎水代茶飲之」 — gather in the fourth month at full leaf; and after the tenth-month FROST, when two of three parts have fallen, the one part still hanging is called 神仙葉, IMMORTALS' LEAF; gather that, shade-dry with the earlier leaf, powder for pills or powders, or decoct and drink in place of tea. Zhu Zhenheng, same section: 「經霜桑葉研末米飲服止盜汗」 — FROST-EXPOSED leaf, powdered, in rice water, stops night sweats. The DB says 'traditionally gathered after the first autumn frost'; the 1596 text specifies two distinct harvests and reserves the frost leaf for particular indications.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS by layer, BCGM 1596: 本經 — 「除寒熱出汗」; 別錄 — 「汁解蜈蚣毒」; 蘇恭 — 「煎濃汁服能除脚氣水腫利大小腸」; 大明 — 「煎飲利五臟通闗節下氣嫩葉煎酒服治一切風蒸熟擣罯風痛出汗并撲損瘀血挼爛塗蛇蟲傷」; 陳藏器 — 「研汁治金瘡及小兒吻瘡煎汁服止霍亂腹痛吐下」; 時珍 — 「治勞熱欬嗽明目長髪」. The DB's wind-heat/exterior-releasing framing is a later systematisation; the 1596 record is dominated by sweating, damp-swelling, trauma and eye indications.

CHARRED FORM: the DB says 'charred (Sang Ye tan) it also cools the blood to stem minor heat-driven bleeding.' The 1596 附方 supports the bleeding use but with a plain roasted, not charred, preparation: 吐血不止 — 「晚桑葉焙研凉茶服三錢只一服止後用補肝肺藥」 (late mulberry leaf, gently roasted and ground, taken in COOL TEA, three qian, one dose only, then follow with Liver- and Lung-supplementing medicines). The 'only one dose' instruction is doctrine and is not in the DB.

PART DISCIPLINE across the whole tree, BCGM 1596: 桑根白皮 甘寒無毒 (with 甄權 平, 大明 温, 李杲 甘辛寒 dissents); 葉 苦甘寒有小毒 (大明 煖); 枝 苦平 — and of the twig Su Song says 「桑枝不冷不熱可以常服」, NEITHER COLD NOR HOT, MAY BE TAKEN CONSTANTLY. Four parts, four readings. A monograph that inherits 甘寒 from the root bark for the leaf is doing what the project already flagged on Gou Qi Zi.

CITATION HYGIENE: the DB's secondary_citation for this herb names Grieve, A Modern Herbal, 1931 and Bensky 2004 — both post-1900 and unusable. Its primary names the Shennong for the leaf, which as shown assigns the leaf no temperature.

results.pre1900_finding: 仁氣味辛温濇無毒 — the KERNEL is acrid, WARM, ASTRINGENT (濇), non-toxic. Confirmed independently in 1596 and 1757. The 1596 text also prints four competing readings, one of them 平 (neutral), which the DB does not carry. Note the astringent quality 濇 is in the head reading and is absent from the DB's taste field.
results.evidence: Li Shizhen, 本草綱目 (Bencao Gangmu), 1596, 卷14 草之三, entry 縮砂蔤 headed 【宋開寳】: 「仁氣味辛温濇無毒」【權曰辛苦藏器曰酸珣曰辛鹹平…好古曰辛温陽也浮也入手足太隂陽明太陽足少隂七經得白檀香豆蔲為使入肺得人參益智為使入脾得黄蘗茯苓為使入腎得赤白石脂為使入大小膓也】. URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷14 — CROSS-CHECK: Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757, s.v. 砂仁 (即縮砂密): 「辛溫香窜。和胃醒脾。快氣調中。通行结滞。」 URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: GRADE / PROVENANCE: NOT in the Shennong Bencao Jing and therefore carries NO 上/中/下品 grade. BCGM 1596 heads it 【宋開寳】 — first recorded in the Kaibao Bencao, Song dynasty (973-974 CE). Any product copy implying ancient canonical standing for this herb is unsupported; it is a Song-era addition to the materia medica.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), the fullest in this batch. Wang Haogu, quoted in BCGM 1596: 「入手足太隂陽明太陽足少隂七經」 — enters the hand and foot TAIYIN, YANGMING and TAIYANG and the foot SHAOYIN, SEVEN CHANNELS in all. Wu Yiluo 1757 adds an eighth in passing: 「砂仁亦入大小腸經」 (also enters the Large and Small Intestine channels). The DB records no channels.

ENVOY DOCTRINE (使藥) — how the herb is STEERED to a chosen organ, verbatim from Wang Haogu in BCGM 1596 and repeated in 1757: 「得白檀香豆蔲為使入肺得人參益智為使入脾得黄蘗茯苓為使入腎得赤白石脂為使入大小膓也」 — with sandalwood and cardamom as envoys it enters the LUNG; with ginseng and yizhi, the SPLEEN; with phellodendron and poria, the KIDNEY; with red and white shizhi, the LARGE AND SMALL INTESTINE. This is formulation doctrine the DB has no field for and is directly actionable for blend design.

CONTRAINDICATIONS — and one of them cuts against a claim the DB makes without caveat. Wu Yiluo, 本草從新 1757: 「辛窜性燥。血虚火炎者勿用。胎妇多服耗氣。必致難產。」 — acrid and penetrating, DRYING by nature; DO NOT USE where blood is deficient and fire flares; PREGNANT WOMEN WHO TAKE MUCH OF IT DRAIN QI AND WILL CERTAINLY HAVE A DIFFICULT LABOUR. The DB states flatly that it 'traditionally calms a restless fetus and eases morning sickness'. Both are in the classical record — BCGM 1596 carries 妊娠胎動 and 子癎昬冐 formulas — but 1757 attaches a hard dose limit to exactly that use. Do not carry the fetus-calming claim without this.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE: Wu Yiluo 1757: 「炒去衣研」 — dry-fry, remove the husk, grind. BCGM 1596 附方 give indication-specific processing: for eclamptic clouding, 「縮砂和皮炒黑熱酒調下二錢」 (fried BLACK WITH THE HUSK ON, two qian in hot wine); for threatened miscarriage, 「縮砂熨斗内炒熟去皮用仁擣碎每服二錢熱酒調下」 (fried done in a flat-iron, husk removed, kernel crushed); for post-partum bleeding, 「新縮砂仁新瓦焙研末米飲服三錢」 (fresh kernel baked on a NEW TILE). Processing is indication-specific, not generic.

CLASSICAL THEORY, worth quoting in copy: Han Mao's 醫通, cited by Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 發明: 「腎惡燥以辛潤之縮砂仁之辛以潤腎燥」 — the Kidney abhors dryness and is moistened by the acrid; the acridity of Sha Ren moistens Kidney dryness. And: 「縮砂屬土主醒脾調胃引諸藥歸宿丹田香而能竄和合五臟冲和之氣」 — it belongs to EARTH, wakes the Spleen, regulates the Stomach, and LEADS THE OTHER MEDICINES HOME TO THE DANTIAN; fragrant and able to bore through, it harmonises the moderating qi of the five zang.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS by layer, BCGM 1596: 開寶 — 「虚勞冷瀉宿食不消赤白洩痢腹中虚痛下氣」; 甄權 — 「主冷氣痛止休息氣痢勞損消化水穀温暖肝腎」; 陳藏器 — 「上氣欬逆奔豚鬼疰驚癎邪氣」; 大明 — 「一切氣霍亂轉筋能起酒香味」; 楊士瀛 — 「和中行氣止痛安胎」; 張元素 — 「治脾胃氣結滯不散」; 時珍 — 「補肺醒脾養胃益腎理元氣通滯氣散寒飲脹痞噎膈嘔吐止女子崩中除咽喉口齒浮熱化銅鐵骨哽」.

COMPETING PRE-1900 READINGS printed inside the 1596 qi-wei line, which the DB flattens to a single 'Pungent / Warm': 甄權 — 辛苦 (acrid and bitter); 陳藏器 — 酸 (sour); 李珣 — 辛鹹平 (acrid, salty, NEUTRAL); 王好古 — 辛温陽也浮也 (acrid warm, yang, floating). Li Xun's 平 is a genuine pre-1900 dissent from 'warm'.

CITATION HYGIENE — DIRECT RULE VIOLATION IN THE STORED ROW. The DB's primary_text_citation for this herb names 'Stuart, Chinese Materia Medica: Vegetable Kingdom (1911)', with an author field of 'King's American Dispensatory' and a year field of 1898 and a henriettes-herb.com URL. Stuart 1911 is on the forbidden list (it is the post-1900 revision of Porter Smith 1871); the author, year and URL fields do not match the work named; and Porter Smith 1871, the allowed predecessor, transmits no temperature at all. This citation cannot support any part of the stored row and should be replaced with BCGM 1596.

additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 本經中品 — MIDDLE grade, stated in the BCGM entry header. The DB does not record this. Middle grade in the Shennong scheme means the herb governs disease and is NOT intended for unlimited daily use, unlike upper-grade herbs. Directly relevant to a product recommending daily herbs.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), BCGM 1596, quoting Zhang Yuansu 張元素: 「腎經本藥入足陽明手太隂經氣分」 — an essential Kidney-channel medicine that enters the foot-yangming (Stomach) and hand-taiyin (Lung) channels, qi aspect. This matches the DB's Lung/Stomach/Kidney claim and now has a pre-1900 anchor.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS (本經, quoted in BCGM): 「消渇熱中除邪氣肢體浮腫下水補不足益氣」 — wasting-thirst and heat in the centre, dispelling evil qi, swelling of the limbs, draining water, supplementing insufficiency, boosting qi.
名醫別錄 layer (quoted in BCGM): 「療傷寒乆瘧煩熱脇下邪氣膈中惡及風汗内疽多服令人洩」 — cold damage, chronic malaria, vexing heat, evil qi below the ribs.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, BCGM quoting Lei Xiao 雷斆: 「凡使先於槐砧上剉細燒乾木臼杵擣勿犯鐡器」 — chop on a locust-wood block, pound in a wooden mortar, NEVER let it touch iron. Li Shizhen adds a directional rule: 「引經上行則用酒浸焙乾下行則用鹽水潤焙」 — wine-soak and bake to send it upward, salt-water to send it downward.

CONTRAINDICATION, stated classically in the 別錄 line quoted above: 「多服令人洩」 — taken in quantity it causes diarrhoea. Confirmed and sharpened by Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757: 「傷胃滑腸。令人作瀉」 (injures the stomach, makes the bowels slippery, causes purging). The DB carries no contraindication of this kind.

COMPATIBILITY, BCGM: 「得黄蘗及酒良能伏鹽及蓬砂」 — good with Phellodendron and wine. Li Shizhen states the pairing doctrine outright: 「二藥必相須而行」 — Zhi Mu and Huang Bo must be used together, one working the qi aspect and the other the blood aspect.

results.herb: Capillaris Wormwood (Yin Chen Hao) — Artemisia capillaris, young aerial parts
results.pre1900_finding: 莖葉氣味苦平微寒無毒 — stem and leaf: bitter, NEUTRAL, slightly cold, non-toxic. The 1596 text prints the two layers side by side and does not resolve them. The Han-layer reading is flatly 平 (neutral): 味苦，平. 'Cool' rests entirely on the junior 別錄/大明 layer (大明曰石茵蔯苦凉無毒), not on the 本經.

additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 本經上品 — UPPER grade, stated in the BCGM header and confirmed by the 草上品七十三種 table of contents in the Sun Xingyan recension. Upper grade plus the 本經 line 「久服，輕身、益氣、耐老」 (prolonged taking lightens the body, boosts qi, resists ageing) means this was classically sanctioned for sustained daily use. The DB records neither the grade nor the久服 claim.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), BCGM 1596 quoting Zhang Yuansu: 「苦甘隂中微陽入足太陽經」 — enters the foot-taiyang (BLADDER) channel. Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757, repeats it: 「入足太陽經。（膀胱。）發汗利水。以泄太陰、陽明之溼熱」. NOTE: this CONTRADICTS the DB's channel claim. The DB says Yin Chen Hao 'drains damp-heat from the Liver and Gallbladder'; the pre-1900 texts assign it to the Bladder channel, working through sweat and urine, draining damp-heat out of the Spleen and Stomach. Liver/Gallbladder attribution is not a pre-1900 reading.
CLASSICAL INDICATIONS (本經, quoted verbatim in BCGM): 「風濕寒熱邪氣熱結黄疸久服輕身益氣耐老靣白悦長年白兎食之仙」. 別錄 layer: 「治通身發黄小便不利除頭熱去伏瘕」 — whole-body yellowing, inhibited urination, head heat, hidden conglomerations.
TOXICITY DISSENT worth surfacing: 權曰苦辛有小毒 — Zhen Quan records it as SLIGHTLY TOXIC, against the head line's 無毒. The DB records no toxicity note at all.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, BCGM quoting Lei Xiao: 「凡使須用葉有八角者隂乾去根細剉勿令犯火」 — use leaves with eight angles, shade-dry, discard the root, chop fine, DO NOT let it near fire. This is a stronger and more specific rule than the DB's 'young shoots only'.

CONTRAINDICATION, Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757: 「按黃胆須分陰黃、陽黃。陽黃宜茵陳。陰黃宜溫補。若用茵陳。多致不救」 — jaundice must be split into yin and yang types; yang jaundice takes Yin Chen, yin jaundice needs warming supplementation, and giving Yin Chen in yin jaundice often puts the case beyond rescue. The DB gestures at this but does not carry it as a stated contraindication. (Quoted from the Chinese Wikisource transcription of 本草從新, whose orthography is mixed simplified/traditional; the reading is reliable, a traditional scan should be used before this is printed as the 1757 text.)

SPECIES CAUTION from the source itself: BCGM 集解 records that 山茵蔯, 家茵蔯 and 石茵蔯 were already three different plants in trade by 1596, with Su Song writing 「茵蔯蒿當别是一物主療自異不得為山茵蔯也」 — the true Yin Chen Hao is a different plant from Shan Yin Chen and their indications differ. The DB's 'co-official Artemisia scoparia' note is downstream of a confusion that is 900 years old.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经) — AND A DIRECT CONTRADICTION OF THE DB. Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596: 「時珍曰逺志入足少隂腎經非心經藥也其功専於強志益精治善忘益精與志皆腎經之所藏也」 — Yuan Zhi enters the foot-shaoyin KIDNEY channel and is NOT a Heart-channel medicine; its power is specifically to strengthen will and boost essence, and forgetfulness is treated because essence and will are both stored by the Kidney. Wang Haogu is quoted to the same effect: 「逺志腎經氣分藥也」. The DB states it 'enters Heart, Kidney, and Lung' — Li Shizhen explicitly denies the Heart. Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757, takes the opposite side: 「主手少陰。（心、）能通腎氣」. This is a genuine, live pre-1900 disagreement and should be surfaced, not collapsed.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE (mandatory), BCGM quoting Lei Xiao: 「凡使須去心否則令人煩悶仍用甘草湯浸一宿暴乾或焙乾用」 — the core MUST be removed or it causes vexation and oppression; then soak overnight in licorice decoction and sun- or fire-dry. The DB mentions coring and honey-frying; the classical vehicle is LICORICE decoction, not honey, and the reason given for coring is an adverse effect, not harshness on the stomach.

CONTRAINDICATIONS / INCOMPATIBILITIES, BCGM quoting Xu Zhicai 徐之才: 「得茯苓冬葵子龍骨良畏珍珠藜蘆蜚蠊齊蛤」 — good with Fu Ling, Dong Kui Zi and Long Gu; fears (畏) pearl, Li Lu (Veratrum), cockroach and clam. Wu Yiluo, 1757, adds a use-limit: 「不可多用獨用。純虚無滞者忌」 — must not be used in large dose or alone; contraindicated in pure deficiency without stagnation.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom (本經): 「咳逆傷中補不足除邪氣利九竅益智慧耳目聰明不忘強志倍力」. 別錄: 「利丈夫定心氣止驚悸益精去心下膈氣皮膚中熱面目黄」. Note the 之才 line: 「殺天雄附子烏頭毒」 — it kills the toxicity of Tian Xiong, Fu Zi and Wu Tou, a classical antidotal use the DB does not carry.
PART DISCIPLINE: BCGM gives the LEAF a separate entry with its own indications — 「葉主治益精補隂氣止虚損夢洩」 (別錄). The leaf is named 小草 in the 本經 and was a distinct drug.

The Han-layer reading is WARM, not neutral: 味甘，溫, and the Wu Pu variants show the disagreement was already ancient — 神農：甘，小溫；桐君、雷公：甘. BCGM's note adds a third: 桐君雷公甘凉 (COOL). Stored 'Neutral' takes one half of a printed double reading and drops the older half.

additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 本經上品 — UPPER grade, stated in the BCGM header and confirmed by the Sun Xingyan 草上品 contents. With 「久服，耳目聰明，輕身、不飢、延年」 this is the strongest classical warrant in this batch for open-ended daily use. The DB's citation claims upper grade but gives no text; this is the text.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), BCGM 1596: 「李杲曰山藥入手太隂」 and 「按吳綬云山藥入手足太隂二經補其不足清其虛熱」 — hand-taiyin (Lung) and foot-taiyin (Spleen). NOTE: the pre-1900 channel assignment is Lung and Spleen ONLY. The Kidney appears in BCGM as an ACTION (「益腎氣」, 時珍) and via the Ba Wei Wan rationale (「肺爲腎之源」), not as a channel entry. The DB's 'Spleen, Lung, and Kidney' triple is half channel and half action.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — this is substantial and the DB has none of it. Kou Zongshi 寇宗奭 in BCGM: 「入藥貴生乾之故古方皆用乾山藥盖生則性滑不可入藥熟則滯氣只堪啖耳」 — for medicine it must be RAW-dried; ancient formulas all used raw-dried Shan Yao, because raw-and-fresh is too slippery to be medicine and cooked stagnates the qi and is fit only for eating. Lei Xiao: 「采得以銅刀刮去赤皮洗去涎蒸過暴乾用」 — scrape with a COPPER knife (not iron), wash off the slime, steam, sun-dry. Su Song: alum water overnight to strip the slime. A formula in the same entry adds 「忌鐵器生冷」. This directly qualifies the DB's 'dry-fried chao Shan Yao vs raw' note, which is a later distinction.

CONTRAINDICATION, BCGM quoting Meng Shen 孟詵: 「惟和麫作䬪飥則動氣爲不能制麫毒也」 — taken with wheat-flour noodles it stirs the qi, because it cannot subdue the toxin of wheat. Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757, states it as a bare rule: 「勿同麵食」. The DB records no contraindication.
INCOMPATIBILITY: 「之才曰紫芝爲之使惡甘遂」 — Zi Zhi is its envoy; antagonised by Gan Sui.
CLASSICAL INDICATIONS (本經): 「傷中補虚羸除寒熱邪氣補中益氣力長肌肉强隂久服耳目聰明輕身不饑延年」. 別錄 adds a head-and-eye range the DB omits entirely: 「主頭面遊風頭風眼眩下氣止腰痛治虚勞羸痩充五臟除煩熱」.

TAXONOMIC NOTE from the source: Li Shizhen moved this entry OUT of the herb section INTO the vegetable section (校正「自草部移入此」) and states 「薯蕷入藥野生者爲勝若供饌則家種者爲良」 — wild-collected is superior for medicine, cultivated for the table. Relevant to sourcing claims.

additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 中品 — MIDDLE grade. The Sun Xingyan 1799 recension lists 山茱萸 in 「上木，中品一十七種」. (The BCGM 卷36 entry header is a lacuna in the Siku transcription, so the grade is taken from the Shennong contents list, not from BCGM.) Middle grade: governs disease, not an open-ended daily herb. The DB does not record this.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), BCGM 1596 quoting Wang Haogu 王好古: 「陽中之隂入足厥隂少隂經氣分」 — yin within yang; enters the foot-jueyin (Liver) and foot-shaoyin (Kidney) channels, qi aspect. Zhang Yuansu adds the one-word action 「温肝」 (warms the Liver). This anchors the DB's Liver/Kidney claim in a pre-1900 text for the first time.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — the DB's pit rule, with its actual classical source and rationale. BCGM 實脩治, quoting Lei Xiao: 「凡使以酒潤去核取皮一斤只取四兩已來緩火熬乾方用能壯元氣秘精其核能滑精不可服」 — moisten with wine, discard the pit, take the flesh; from one jin only about four liang are obtained; dry over a slow fire. It invigorates original qi and secures essence, and THE PIT CAUSES LEAKAGE OF ESSENCE AND MUST NOT BE TAKEN. Wu Yiluo, 1757, states it in four characters: 「去核。（核能滑精。）」 The DB's part_used note is correct and this is its pre-1900 warrant.
INCOMPATIBILITIES, BCGM: 「蓼實為之使惡桔梗防風防己」 — Liao Shi is its envoy; antagonised by Jie Geng, Fang Feng, Fang Ji. Wu Yiluo 1757 gives 「惡防己、防風、桔梗」.

CONTRAINDICATION, Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757: 「强陽不痿。小便不利者。不宜用」 — unsuitable where yang is already strong and will not subside, or where urination is inhibited. The DB records no contraindication for an astringent given to people with urinary complaints.

MECHANISM IN THE SOURCE'S OWN IDIOM, BCGM 發明 quoting Wang Haogu: 「滑則氣脱濇劑所以收之山茱茰止小便利秘精氣取其味酸濇以收滑也仲景八味丸用之為君其性味可知矣」 — where there is slipperiness the qi deserts, so astringent agents gather it back; Zhongjing used it as sovereign in the Ba Wei Wan.

SPECIES CAUTION from the source itself: BCGM devotes the adjacent entry to 胡頽子 (Elaeagnus, 雀兒酥) precisely because it was being confused with Shan Zhu Yu — 「結實小長儼如山茱茰…核亦如山茱茰但有八稜」. The eight-ridged pit is the 1596 discriminator. Also note the DB's stated indication 'qi and yang collapse with profuse sweating' is NOT in these texts; BCGM records the opposite direction, 「下氣出汗」 (別錄), and the desertion-rescue use is Zhang Xichun's, early 20th century.

results.herb: Corydalis (Yan Hu Suo) — Corydalis yanhusuo, rhizome
results.pre1900_finding: 根氣味辛温無毒 — root: acrid, WARM, non-toxic. Every reading printed in the entry agrees on 温: Li Gao 甘辛温, Wang Haogu 苦辛温純陽, Li Shizhen 味苦㣲辛氣温. Wu Yiluo 1757 concurs: 辛苦而溫.
results.evidence: Li Shizhen 李時珍, 本草綱目 (四庫全書本) 卷13, 延胡索 entry, 1596: header 「{{SK anchor|延胡索}}{{SK notes|宋開寳}}」; qi-wei line 「根氣味辛温無毒」; attached note 「珣曰苦甘杲曰甘辛温可升可降隂中陽也好古曰苦辛温純陽浮也入手足太隂經」; 發明 「時珍曰𤣥胡索味苦㣲辛氣温入手足太隂厥隂四經能行血中氣滯氣中血滯故專治一身上下諸痛用之中的妙不可言」. URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷13&action=raw
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: NONE — and this is a correction the DB needs. The BCGM entry header reads 「宋開寳」, i.e. the drug's canonical first entry is the Song Kaibao Bencao (973 CE). Yan Hu Suo is ABSENT from the Shennong Bencao Jing entirely (zero occurrences of 延胡索 across the whole 242 KB Sun Xingyan 1799 recension). It therefore carries no 上品/中品/下品 grade and no classical warrant for prolonged daily use. Chen Cangqi is cited only inside the 集解 (「藏器曰延胡索生奚國從安東來根如半夏色黄」), which is a habitat note, not a grade.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), BCGM 1596: Wang Haogu 「入手足太隂經」; Li Shizhen expands it to four channels, 「入手足太隂厥隂四經」 — hand- and foot-taiyin (Lung, Spleen) and hand- and foot-jueyin (Pericardium, Liver). The DB records no channel entry.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — the DB says 'most often stir-processed with rice vinegar' but gives no doctrine. Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757, supplies the actual rule: 「生用破血。炒用調血。（酒炒行血、醋炒止血。）」 — raw it BREAKS blood, fried it REGULATES blood; wine-fried moves the blood, VINEGAR-fried STOPS it. Vinegar processing therefore reverses the herb's direction; it is not a neutral default. BCGM formulas show the same split: 醋炒 for menstrual pain, 塩炒 for shan qi, plain 炒研 postpartum. (本草從新 quoted from the Chinese Wikisource transcription, whose orthography is mixed; the reading is reliable, a traditional scan is needed before printing it as the 1757 text.)

CONTRAINDICATIONS, Wu Yiluo 1757 — and these are serious omissions from the DB: 「通經堕胎」 (it opens the menses and CAUSES MISCARRIAGE) and 「經事先期。虚而崩漏。產後虚晕。均忌之」 (contraindicated in early menses, deficiency-type flooding and leaking, and postpartum deficiency dizziness). Also 「然辛溫走而不守。獨用力迅、宜兼補氣血藥用」 — acrid and warm, it runs and does not guard, so used alone its force is precipitous and it should be combined with qi- and blood-supplementing herbs. The DB calls it 'the supreme analgesic for pain of any location' with no counterweight.
CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's idiom (開寶, quoted in BCGM): 「破血婦人月經不調腹中結塊崩中淋露産後諸血病血運暴血衝上因損下血」. Da Ming: 「除風治氣暖腰膝止暴腰痛破癥癖撲損瘀血落胎」 — note 落胎, drops the foetus, stated as an effect.
Li Shizhen's own case reports are in the entry and are worth quoting in a monograph as classical evidence rather than modern pharmacology: 「按方勺泊宅編云…用𤣥胡索當歸桂心等分爲末温酒服三四錢隨量頻進以止爲度遂痛止葢𤣥胡索能活血化氣第一品藥也」.

results.herb: Eucommia Bark (Du Zhong) — Eucommia ulmoides, stem bark
results.pre1900_finding: 氣味辛平無毒 — acrid, NEUTRAL, non-toxic. The Han-layer reading agrees: 味辛，平。 'Warm' comes from the junior layer only — 別錄曰甘温, 權曰苦煖, 元素曰性温. Li Shizhen splits the difference in his own words: 「其氣温平甘微辛」, warm-neutral.
results.source_year: 1596 (Bencao Gangmu); Han-layer reading from the Sun Xingyan recension, 1799
results.evidence: Li Shizhen 李時珍, 本草綱目 (四庫全書本) 卷35上, 杜仲 entry, 1596: header 「{{SK anchor|杜仲}}{{SK notes|本經上品}}」; qi-wei line 「氣味辛平無毒」; attached note 「别錄曰甘温權曰苦煖元素曰性温味辛甘氣味俱薄沈而降陰也杲曰陽也降也好古曰肝經氣分藥也　之才曰惡𤣥參蛇蛻皮」. URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷35上&action=raw  ||  神農本草經, Sun Xingyan recension, 1799 (text c. 200 CE), ==杜仲==: 「味辛，平。主腰脊痛，補中，益精氣，堅筋骨，強志，除陰下癢濕，小便余瀝。久服，輕身、耐老。一名思仙。」 URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=神農本草經_(孫星衍)&action=raw
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 本經上品 — UPPER grade, stated in the BCGM header, confirmed by the Sun Xingyan 木上品二十種 contents list, with 「久服，輕身、耐老」. The DB asserts upper-grade status in its citation string; this is the locatable text behind it.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经) — AND A CORRECTION THE DB NEEDS. BCGM 1596 quoting Wang Haogu: 「肝經氣分藥也」, LIVER channel, qi aspect. Li Shizhen makes the point explicitly in the 發明 and says it was new: 「杜仲古方只知滋腎惟王好古言是肝經氣分藥潤肝燥補肝虚發昔人所未發也蓋肝主筋腎主骨腎充則骨强肝充則筋健…杜仲色紫而潤味甘微辛其氣温平甘温能補微辛能潤故能入肝而補腎子能令母實也」 — ancient formulas knew it only as a Kidney-enricher; the Liver reading is Wang Haogu's, and the Kidney effect follows indirectly ('the child makes the mother replete'). The DB presents Liver and Kidney as co-equal; classically the Kidney effect is derivative.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — the DB's claim needs qualifying. BCGM 1596 gives one classical method only, quoting Lei Xiao: 「凡使削去粗皮每一斤用酥一兩蜜三兩和塗火炙以盡為度細剉用」 — shave off the coarse outer bark, coat each jin with one liang of clarified butter and three liang of honey, roast over fire until absorbed, then chop fine. There is NO salt processing in BCGM. Salt appears only later: Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757, lists 「或酥炙、蜜炙、盐酒炒、薑汁炒、斷絲用」 as alternatives. So 'salt-processed yan du zhong is the classic clinical form' is a post-1596 development, not the classical form. The constant across all methods is 斷絲 — the rubber threads must be broken by heat.

CONTRAINDICATION / INCOMPATIBILITY: BCGM 「之才曰惡𤣥參蛇蛻皮」 — antagonised by Xuan Shen and snake slough. Wu Yiluo 1757 adds the clinical exclusion the DB lacks: 「腎虽虚而火炽者勿用」 — do not use where the Kidney is deficient but fire is blazing. This matters directly for the DB's hypertension indication.
CLASSICAL INDICATIONS (本經, quoted verbatim in BCGM): 「腰膝痛補中益精氣堅筋骨强志除陰下癢濕小便餘瀝久服輕身耐老」. 別錄: 「脚中酸疼不欲踐地」 — aching in the feet with unwillingness to tread the ground. Zhen Quan: 「腎冷䐴腰痛人虚而身强直風也腰不利加而用之」.

FETUS-SECURING USE, with its classical formula, BCGM 附方: 「頻慣墮胎…於兩月前以杜仲八兩糯米煎湯浸透炒去絲續斷二兩酒浸焙乾為末以山藥五六兩為末作糊丸梧子大毎服五十丸空心米飲下」 — habitual miscarriage; note the glutinous-rice-decoction soak and the Shan Yao paste binder. This substantiates the DB's fetus claim from a 1596 text.
IDENTITY TEST from the source, useful for sourcing: 「折之多白絲者為佳」 — bark that shows many white threads when snapped is the good grade (別錄/Tao Hongjing). 「其皮中有銀絲如綿故曰木綿」.

results.herb: Uncaria (Gou Teng) — Uncaria rhynchophylla, hooked stems
results.pre1900_finding: 氣味甘微寒無毒 — sweet, SLIGHTLY COLD, non-toxic; 微寒 is the standard classical equivalent of 'cool'. But Li Shizhen's own reading in the same line is NEUTRAL: 「時珍曰初微甘後微苦平」, and Zhen Quan gives 甘平. So the head line supports the stored value while the compiler himself dissents. Wu Yiluo, 1757, restores cold: 甘微苦寒.
results.evidence: Li Shizhen 李時珍, 本草綱目 (四庫全書本) 卷18下, 釣藤 entry, 1596: header 「{{SK anchor|釣藤}}{{SK notes|别錄下品}}」 with 校正「自木部移入此」; qi-wei line 「氣味甘微寒無毒」; attached note 「保昇曰苦權曰甘平時珍曰初微甘後微苦平」. URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷18下&action=raw
additions: GRADE — THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING FOR THIS HERB. The BCGM header reads 「别錄下品」: Gou Teng is NOT in the Shennong Bencao Jing at all (zero occurrences of 釣藤 or 鉤藤 in the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension) and enters the canon through the Mingyi Bielu as a LOWER-grade drug. Lower grade encodes short, targeted, symptom-driven use, the opposite of the upper-grade daily-tonic warrant. Nothing in the DB row signals this. For a product recommending daily herbs this is a hard flag.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), BCGM 1596: 「時珍曰釣藤手足厥隂藥也足厥隂主風手厥隂主火驚癎眩運皆肝風相火之病釣藤通心包于肝木風靜火息則諸證自除」 — a hand- and foot-jueyin (Pericardium and Liver) medicine; foot-jueyin governs wind, hand-jueyin governs fire; fright epilepsy and dizziness are all diseases of Liver wind and ministerial fire; Gou Teng links the Pericardium to Liver-wood, and when wind is stilled and fire quenched the symptoms resolve of themselves. The DB has the clinical picture but no channel entry and no pre-1900 anchor.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS, in the source's own idiom, all quoted in BCGM: 別錄 「小兒寒熱十二驚癎」; 甄權 「小兒驚啼瘛瘲熱壅客忤胎風」; 時珍 「大人頭旋目眩平肝風除心熱小兒内釣腹痛發斑疹」. Note the centre of gravity is PAEDIATRIC. The adult hypertensive picture in the DB is a modern reading of 頭旋目眩.

PART DOCTRINE, BCGM 集解: 「時珍曰狀如葡萄藤而有鈎紫色古方多用皮后世多用鈎取其力鋭爾」 — ancient formulas mostly used the BARK; later generations use the HOOKS because their force is sharper. The DB's 'stem with hooks' is the late convention, not the classical one, and the source says so.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — decisive and absent from the DB. Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757, under 钩藤钩: 「藤細多钩者良。（去梗、純用嫩钩、其功十倍。）久煎則無力。（俟他藥煎就、方入钩藤、一二沸即起、頗得力也。）」 — discard the stem and use only the tender hooks, whose power is tenfold; PROLONGED DECOCTION DESTROYS ITS POWER, so add it only after the other herbs are cooked, bring it to one or two boils and take it off. Any Eden preparation instruction that boils Gou Teng with the rest of a decoction is contrary to classical doctrine. (Located in the Chinese Wikisource 本草從新 transcription, whose orthography is mixed simplified/traditional; the reading is reliable but a traditional scan is required before printing this as the 1757 text.)

CONTRAINDICATION, Wu Yiluo 1757: 「祛肝風而不燥。庶幾中和。故小兒科珍之。但性稍寒。無火者勿服」 — it dispels Liver wind without drying, hence its value in paediatrics; but its nature is somewhat cold and those WITHOUT fire should not take it. This is the classical form of the DB's 'pair with warming herbs in cold or depleted Vata' hedge.

SPECIES / NAMING HAZARD, flagged for product safety: the DB's common_name field reads 'Cat's Claw Vine / Uncaria (Gou Teng)'. 'Cat's claw' in Western commerce means Uncaria tomentosa, an Amazonian species with a completely different profile, absent from every Chinese source. Gou Teng is Uncaria rhynchophylla, described in BCGM as 「藤長八九尺或一二丈大如苺指其中空」 with hooks 「其刺曲如釣鈎故名」. The two should never share a display name.

results.pre1900_finding: The classical record splits BY PLANT PART, and the stored value is right for the part the DB actually uses. 赤箭 (the stalk, the 本經 entry) = 辛溫 acrid/WARM. 天麻 (the root-tuber, entered as its own drug in 開寶本草 973 and carried by Zhenglei 1108) = 辛平 acrid/NEUTRAL. Since part_used is the rhizome/tuber, 'Neutral' is correct — but it does NOT descend from the 本經 head-reading, which is warm.
results.evidence: Zhenglei Bencao 證類本草 (Tang Shenwei, 1108), 卷09, Siku recension: 「天麻味辛平無毒。主諸風濕痺，四肢拘攣，小兒風癎驚氣，利腰膝，強筋力，久服益氣輕身長年。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/證類本草_(四庫全書本)/卷09 — Bencao Gangmu 本草綱目 (Li Shizhen, 1596), 卷12下, Siku recension: 「赤箭氣味辛温無毒」 with the dissent register attached: 「志曰天麻辛平無毒。大明曰甘暖。權曰赤箭芝一名天麻，味甘平無毒。好古曰苦平，隂中之陽也。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷12下 — Shennong Bencao Jing 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan & Sun Fengyi recension (1799), 上經: 「==赤箭== 味辛，溫。主殺鬼精物、蠱毒惡氣。久服，益氣力，長陰、肥健，輕身、增年。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) — Ben Cao Cong Xin 本草從新 (Wu Yiluo, 1757): 天麻 「辛溫。入肝經氣分。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 上品 (upper/superior). Confirmed twice independently — BCGM 1596 卷12下 heads the entry 「{{SK anchor|赤箭}}{{SK notes|本經上品}}」, and Sun Xingyan 1799 places 赤箭 at offset 16912, inside 卷一·上經 (4515–37256). Upper grade = intended for prolonged, non-toxic, daily use. Directly relevant to a daily-herb product.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), which the DB has no column for: Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 發明: 「天麻乃肝經氣分之藥。素問云諸風掉眩皆屬于木，故天麻入厥隂之經而治諸病。」 = a medicine of the QI ASPECT of the Liver channel; enters the Jueyin channel. Wu Yiluo 1757 states it flatly: 「入肝經氣分」.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, entirely absent from the DB. Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 修治: 「若治肝經風虛，惟洗净，以濕紙包，於糠火中煨熟，取出切片，酒浸一宿，焙乾用。」 — for Liver-channel wind-deficiency: wash clean, wrap in WET PAPER, roast in a chaff fire until done, slice, steep in wine overnight, then bake dry. Lei Xiao's alternative (for wind-painful-obstruction use) is a seven-round roast over 蒺藜子 (Tribulus), 「此乃治風痺藥故如此修事也」 — i.e. the processing method is chosen by the INDICATION, not by the herb.

CONTRAINDICATION, classically stated: Lei Xiao in BCGM 1596: 「凡使天麻，勿用御風草，二物相似，只是葉莖不同…使御風草即勿使天麻，若同用令人有腸結之患。」 — a named adulterant/lookalike, and co-use causes intestinal binding. Wu Yiluo 1757 adds the deficiency caution: 「血液衰少，及非真中風者，忌用（風藥能燥血故也）」 — withhold where blood/fluids are depleted or where the wind-stroke is not genuine, because wind-medicines dry the blood.
CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom. 本經 (via Sun Xingyan 1799, for 赤箭): 殺鬼精物、蠱毒惡氣；久服益氣力，長陰肥健. 名醫別錄: 輕身增年，消癰腫，下支滿，寒疝下血. 開寶 (for 天麻, the root): 主諸風濕痺，四肢拘攣，小兒風癎驚氣，利腰膝，強筋力.

QUALITY GRADING, pre-1900: Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 集解 — good material is 「其根暴乾，肉色堅白如羊角色，呼羊角天麻；蒸過黄皺如乾瓜者，俗呼醤瓜天麻，皆可用者。一種形尖而空薄如玄參状者，不堪用。」 The DB's part_used note 'typically steamed then dried' is confirmed pre-1900 by 「蒸過」 here.

TASTE NOTE: the DB stores 'Sweet'. That matches 甄權 (甘平) and 大明 (甘暖) as quoted in BCGM 1596, but NOT the 本經/BCGM head-reading, which is 辛 (acrid). The stored taste and the stored temperature therefore come from two different classical authorities.

results.pre1900_finding: FOUR pre-1900 sources spanning 1108–1694 all read 平 (NEUTRAL), and Li Shizhen 1596 appends a dissent of 溫 (WARM). Not one source before 1757 calls this herb cool. The only pre-1900 support for 'Cool' is Wu Yiluo 1757 (甘苦涼), the latest witness of the five. The stored value inverts the classical consensus.
results.evidence: Shennong Bencao Jing 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan recension (1799), 上經: 「==女貞實== 味苦，平。主補中，安五臟，養精神，除百疾。久服，肥健、輕身、不老。生山谷。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) — Zhenglei Bencao 證類本草 (1108), 卷12: 「女貞實味苦甘平無毒。主補中安五藏，飬精神，除百疾，乆服肥徤輕身不老。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/證類本草_(四庫全書本)/卷12 — Bencao Gangmu 本草綱目 (Li Shizhen, 1596), 卷36: 「氣味苦平無毒」 followed immediately by 「時珍曰温」 — Li Shizhen's own dissent is WARM, the opposite pole from the stored value. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷36 — CONTRARY WITNESS, reported in full: Ben Cao Cong Xin 本草從新 (Wu Yiluo, 1757), 女貞子: 「甘苦涼。少陰之精，隆冬不凋。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新 (see notes — this transcription is mixed-orthography and the 涼 reading should be re-confirmed against a traditional scan before it is relied on, precisely because it is the sole support for the stored value).
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 上品 (upper/superior). Confirmed twice — BCGM 1596 卷36 heads it 「{{SK anchor|女貞}}{{SK notes|本經上品}}」, and Sun Xingyan 1799 places 女貞實 at offset 29807 inside 卷一·上經. Li Shizhen makes the grade an explicit argument: BCGM 1596 發明 「女貞實乃上品無毒妙藥，而古方罕知用者何哉」 — an upper-grade, non-toxic, superb medicine that old formulas strangely underused. For a product recommending daily herbs this is the strongest possible classical licence for prolonged use.

CHANNEL / ORGAN ENTRY (归经): Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 發明: 「典術云女貞木乃少隂之精，故冬不落葉。觀此則其益腎之功尤可推矣。」 — the tree is the essence of SHAOYIN, hence it keeps its leaves through winter; hence its Kidney-augmenting power. Wu Yiluo 1757 repeats 「少陰之精」. This gives the DB the Shaoyin (Kidney) entry it currently lacks.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE: harvest timing AND processing are both classically fixed. 名醫別錄 via BCGM 1596 集解: 「女貞實生武陵川谷，立冬采」 — gathered at LI DONG (start of winter). Wang Ang 1694 and Wu Yiluo 1757 both specify 冬至採佳，酒蒸 — best gathered at the winter solstice, then WINE-STEAMED. The DB's 'traditionally wine-steamed' is therefore confirmed pre-1900, though the two authorities disagree on whether the harvest point is 立冬 or 冬至.

CONTRAINDICATION, classically stated and currently missing from the DB: Wu Yiluo 1757: 「純陰至静之品，唯陰虚有火者宜之，否則腹痛作瀉。」 — a purely yin, utterly still substance; suitable ONLY for yin deficiency with fire, otherwise it causes abdominal pain and diarrhoea. That is a real restriction on a herb the DB currently frames as a gentle daily tonic.

ER ZHI WAN PAIRING CONFIRMED PRE-1900: the DB asserts the Han Lian Cao (Eclipta) pairing. BCGM 1596 發明 carries it as 女貞丹方: 「女貞實即冬青樹子，去梗葉，酒浸一日夜，布袋擦去皮，晒乾為末，待旱蓮草出，多取數石搗汁」 — privet fruit combined with 旱蓮草 (Eclipta). Wu Yiluo 1757 gives the three-herb version with 桑葚 added and weights (20 兩 / 10 兩 / 10 兩, honey-pilled).

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS: 本經 (Sun Xingyan 1799): 補中，安五臟，養精神，除百疾；久服肥健、輕身、不老. Li Shizhen's own additions, BCGM 1596: 「强隂，健腰膝，變白髮，明目」 — the eye-brightening and hair-darkening claims the DB summarises are Li Shizhen's, not the 本經's.

SPECIES CONFIRMED FROM A PRE-1900 SOURCE, which is unusual and worth banking: BCGM 1596 釋名 identifies 女貞 as 蠟樹 and explains 「近時以放蠟蟲故俗呼為蠟樹」 — the tree on which wax-insects are farmed. That is Ligustrum lucidum, matching the stored latin_name. Wu Yiluo 1757 repeats 「近人放蠟蟲於此樹」. Li Shizhen also resolves the 女貞/冬青 split: 「今方書所用冬青皆此女貞也」.

results.pre1900_finding: 溫 (WARM) in every pre-1900 witness, unbroken from the Han layer to 1757. BCGM 1596 assigns 蒼朮 specifically 氣味苦溫無毒, and Li Shizhen states the dryness explicitly — 「性溫而燥」 — so the stored moisture value 'Dry' is confirmed by the same sentence, not merely inferred.
results.evidence: Bencao Gangmu 本草綱目 (Li Shizhen, 1596), 卷12下, the 蒼朮 sub-entry (which opens 「蒼术釋名赤术」): 「氣味苦温無毒」, and in the attached register: 「時珍曰白木甘而微苦，性温而和；赤术甘而辛烈，性温而燥，隂中陽也，可升可降，入足太隂、陽明、手太隂、陽明、太陽之經。忌同白术。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷12下 — Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan recension (1799), 上經: 「==術== 味苦，溫。主風寒濕痹、死肌、痙、疸。止汗，除熱，消食，作煎餌。久服，輕身、延年、不飢。一名山薊。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) — Zhenglei Bencao 證類本草 (1108), 卷06: 「术味苦甘温無毒。主風寒濕痺死肌痙痘，止汗除熱消食…久服輕身延年不饑。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/證類本草_(四庫全書本)/卷06 — Ben Cao Cong Xin (Wu Yiluo, 1757), 蒼朮: 「苦溫辛烈。燥胃强脾，發汗除溼。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 上品 (upper/superior). BCGM 1596 卷12下 heads the entry 「{{SK anchor|术}}{{SK notes|直律切，本經上品}}」; Sun Xingyan 1799 places 術 in 卷一·上經. Note the grade attaches to the UNDIFFERENTIATED 術 — see the differentiation caveat below.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), five channels, from Li Shizhen himself, BCGM 1596: 「入足太隂、陽明、手太隂、陽明、太陽之經」 = Foot Taiyin (Spleen), Foot Yangming (Stomach), Hand Taiyin (Lung), Hand Yangming (Large Intestine), Taiyang. Zhu Zhenheng, quoted in the same 發明: 「蒼术為足陽明經藥，氣味辛烈，强胃强脾，發穀之氣，能徑入諸經，疎洩陽明之濕。」 Wu Yiluo 1757 anchors the atrophy indication on it: 「陽明虚則宗筋縱弛…蒼朮陽明經藥，經曰治痿獨取陽明」.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — the DB says 'commonly bran or dry stir-fried', but the classical rule is different and is aimed at curbing the herb's dryness. Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 修治: 「蒼术性燥，故以糯米泔浸去其油，切片焙乾用；亦有用脂麻同炒，以制其燥者。」 — soak in GLUTINOUS-RICE washing water to draw off its oil, slice, bake dry; or dry-fry with SESAME to restrain its dryness. Kou Zongshi in the same section: 「蒼木辛烈，須米泔浸洗，再换泔浸二日，去上粗皮用」 — two full days, water changed. Wu Yiluo 1757 concurs: 「糯米泔浸，焙乾，同芝麻炒，以制其燥」.

CONTRAINDICATIONS + SYNERGIES: BCGM 1596 「忌同白术」, i.e. it inherits the Bai Zhu list given earlier in the same entry — 「之才曰防風、地榆為之使；權曰忌桃李、菘菜、雀肉、青魚」 (Fang Feng and Di Yu are its envoys; avoid peach, plum, Chinese cabbage, sparrow meat, mackerel). Wu Yiluo 1757 adds the pattern-level restriction the DB most needs: 「燥结多汗者忌用」 — withhold in dryness-constipation or profuse sweating. Wu also confirms the envoy rule: 「二朮皆防風、地榆爲使」.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom, 本經 (Sun Xingyan 1799): 風寒濕痹、死肌、痙、疸；止汗，除熱，消食，作煎餌. 名醫別錄 via BCGM 1596: 「主頭痛，消痰水，逐皮間風水結腫，除心下急滿及霍亂吐下不止，暖胃消穀嗜食。」 Li Gao: 「除濕發汗，健胃安脾，治痿要藥。」 Zhu Zhenheng: 「散風益氣，總解諸鬱」 — the six-stagnation (氣血痰火濕食) doctrine, stated pre-1900.

A DIFFERENTIATION CAVEAT WORTH STORING: Li Shizhen states plainly that the classics did NOT distinguish grey from white atractylodes — BCGM 1596 釋名: 「术有赤白二種，主治雖近而性味止發不同，本草不分蒼白，亦未可據。」 The DB's primary_text_citation already notes this correctly. The practical consequence: the 本經 苦溫 reading and the 上品 grade were written for an undifferentiated drug, and the split into 蒼/白 is post-Tao Hongjing. Wu Yiluo 1757 dates it: 「古本草不分苍白，陶隐居分两種，始各施用。」

MINOR DIVERGENCE ON TASTE, not temperature: Wang Ang 1694 reads 蒼朮 as 甘溫辛烈 (sweet) where Wu Yiluo 1757 reads 苦溫辛烈 (bitter) and BCGM 1596 reads 苦溫. The stored taste 'Pungent, Bitter' matches BCGM and BCCX. Temperature is unaffected — all three say 溫.

results.pre1900_finding: FIVE independent pre-1900 witnesses (c. 200 CE via 1799, 1108, 1596, 1694, 1757) all read 甘平 — sweet, NEUTRAL. Not one of them assigns 涼 or 寒. There is NO pre-1900 support for the stored 'Cool' at all. This is the cleanest contradiction in the batch: the classical reading is unanimous and the DB departs from it.
results.evidence: Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan recension (1799), 中經: 「==百合== 味甘，平。主邪氣腹張，心痛，利大小便，補中益氣。生川谷。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) — Zhenglei Bencao 證類本草 (1108), 卷08: 「百合味甘平無毒。主邪氣腹脹心痛，利大小便，補中益氣，除浮腫膨脹痞滿寒熱，通身疼痛及乳難喉痺，止涕淚。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/證類本草_(四庫全書本)/卷08 — Bencao Gangmu 本草綱目 (Li Shizhen, 1596), 卷27: 「氣味甘平無毒」, with the single dissent 「權曰有小毒」 (Zhen Quan: slightly toxic) — note the dissent is about TOXICITY, not temperature; no authority in the register moves it off 平. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷27 — Ben Cao Cong Xin (Wu Yiluo, 1757), 百合: 「甘平。潤肺宁心，清熱止嗽。」 — note that even the source which credits it with CLEARING HEAT (清熱) still records the qi as 平, which is exactly the action-word-is-not-a-temperature trap. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 中品 (middle). Confirmed twice — BCGM 1596 卷27 heads it 「{{SK anchor|百合}}{{SK notes|本經中品}}」 with the note 「校正：自草部移入此」 (reclassified out of the herb section into the vegetable section), and Sun Xingyan 1799 places 百合 at offset 42714, inside 卷二·中經 (37256–58834). MIDDLE grade encodes conditional rather than indefinite use — materially different from the 上品 herbs in this batch, and relevant to any daily-use recommendation.

A TOXICITY FLAG THE DB DOES NOT CARRY: BCGM 1596 records 「權曰有小毒」 — Zhen Quan holds Bai He to be SLIGHTLY TOXIC. The 本經, 別錄, Zhenglei 1108 and both Qing sources all say 無毒, so this is a minority reading, but it is a named pre-1900 dissent and should be visible rather than silently dropped.

CONTRAINDICATION, classically stated, absent from the DB: Wu Yiluo 1757: 「善通二便。中寒下陷者忌之。」 — it freely opens both forms of elimination, therefore withhold it where there is interior COLD with sinking/prolapse. This is the practical counterweight to the herb's moistening reputation.

PREPARATION / SELECTION DOCTRINE: Wu Yiluo 1757: 「花白者入藥」 — only the WHITE-FLOWERED kind enters medicine (repeated by Wang Ang 1694). Meng Shen, quoted in BCGM 1596: 「心急黄，宜蜜蒸食之」 — for that presentation, steam it with honey and eat it. Wu Yiluo also gives the fresh-juice route: 「肺病吐血，鲜百合搗汁，和水飲之，亦可煮食」.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom. 本經 (Sun Xingyan 1799): 邪氣腹脹，心痛，利大小便，補中益氣. 名醫別錄 via BCGM 1596: 「除浮腫臚脹痞滿寒熱，通身疼痛及乳難喉痺，止涕淚。」 甄權: 「百邪鬼魅，涕泣不止，除心下急滿痛，治脚氣熱欬。」 大明: 「安心定膽益志，養五臟，治顛邪狂呌驚悸，産後血狂運。」 The DB's shen-settling / grief framing has genuine pre-1900 warrant here — but in the idiom of 鬼魅, 顛邪狂呌 and 驚悸, not of 'grief'.

BAI HE BING (百合病) IS CLASSICALLY ATTESTED AND THE NAME-PUZZLE IS TOO: BCGM 1596 credits 宗奭 with 「治百合病」. Wu Yiluo 1757 records both the picture and the standing objection: 「傷寒百合病（行住坐卧不定，如有鬼神状。蘇頌曰：病名百合，而用百合治之，不識其義；士材曰：亦清心宁神之效。）」 — Su Song openly says he cannot see why the herb named for the disease should treat it; Li Shicai answers that the effect is heart-clearing and spirit-settling. Worth carrying as a documented classical dispute rather than a settled fact.
ETYMOLOGY, from Li Shizhen, BCGM 1596 釋名: 「百合之根以衆瓣合成也」 — the root is a hundred scales joined into one; 「或云專治百合病故名，亦通」. Also 蒜腦藷 「其根如大蒜，其味如山藷」.

SPECIES CAUTION: the pre-1900 Chinese texts do not resolve 百合 to a Linnaean species, so the stored Lilium lancifolium cannot be confirmed OR refuted from them. Note that BCGM 卷27 carries 山丹 as a SEPARATE adjacent entry, so the classical authors did distinguish at least two lilies. Treat the botanical determination as coming from a modern source, not from these citations.

results.pre1900_finding: 溫 (WARM) unbroken across every pre-1900 witness, and if anything the classical range runs HOTTER than the stored value, not cooler: the 本經 reads 苦溫, the 名醫別錄 reads 大溫 (greatly warm), and Zhen Quan reads 大熱 (greatly hot). Zhenglei 1108 prints the 本經 and 別錄 readings side by side in one string. 'Warm' is the conservative floor of a 溫–大熱 spread.
results.evidence: Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan recension (1799), 中經: 「==厚朴== 味苦，溫。主中風、傷寒、頭痛、寒熱，驚悸氣，血痹死肌，去三虫。」 with the 吳普 variant register: 「厚朴，神農、岐伯、雷公：苦，無毒；李氏：小溫」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/神農本草經_(孫星衍) — Zhenglei Bencao 證類本草 (1108), 卷13, the merged 本經+別錄 double reading in a single string: 「厚朴味苦温大温無毒。主中風傷寒頭痛寒熱，驚悸氣血痺死肌，去三蟲，温中益氣，消痰下氣…」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/證類本草_(四庫全書本)/卷13 — Bencao Gangmu 本草綱目 (Li Shizhen, 1596), 卷35上: 「氣味苦温無毒」 with the register 「别錄曰大温。吳普曰神農、岐伯、雷公苦無毒。李當之小温。權曰苦辛大熱。元素曰氣温味苦辛，氣味俱厚，體重濁而微降，陰中陽也。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草綱目_(四庫全書本)/卷35上 — Ben Cao Cong Xin (Wu Yiluo, 1757): 「苦降能瀉實满，辛溫能散溼满…入足太陰、陽明（脾、胃）。」 https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/本草從新
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 中品 (middle). Confirmed twice — BCGM 1596 卷35上 heads it 「{{SK anchor|厚朴}}{{SK notes|本經中品}}　校正：併入有名未用逐折」, and Sun Xingyan 1799 places 厚朴 at offset 50221 inside 卷二·中經. Middle grade = conditional use, NOT a daily-tonic herb. Wu Yiluo 1757 makes the same point in clinical terms (see contraindication below).

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经): Wu Yiluo 1757: 「入足太陰、陽明（脾、胃）」 = Foot Taiyin Spleen and Foot Yangming Stomach. Zhang Yuansu via BCGM 1596 adds the directional character the DB's 'moves stagnant qi downward' is reaching for: 「氣味俱厚，體重濁而微降，陰中陽也」 — both qi and flavour are thick, the substance heavy and turbid and slightly DESCENDING, yang within yin. Li Gao qualifies it: 「可升可降」.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE — this is the strongest single harvest in the batch, and the DB has no column for it. Lei Xiao, BCGM 1596 修治: 「凡使要紫色味辛者為好，刮去粗皮。入丸散，毎一斤用酥四兩炙熟用；若入湯飲，用自然薑汁八兩灸盡為度。」 — the processing DIFFERS BY DOSAGE FORM: for pills and powders, roast with 4 兩 butter per catty; for decoctions, roast with 8 兩 of neat GINGER JUICE until fully absorbed. And Kou Zongshi gives the reason, which is a hard rule: 「味苦，不以薑制則棘人喉舌」 — unprocessed by ginger, it PRICKS the throat and tongue. Wu Yiluo 1757: 「刮去粗皮，切片，薑汁炒」. Da Ming: 「凡入藥去粗皮，用薑汁灸，或浸炒用」.

CONTRAINDICATIONS, including a pregnancy warning stated classically: Wu Yiluo 1757: 「但可施於元氣未虚、邪氣方盛…若脾胃虚者，切勿沾唇，虽一時未見其害，而清純冲和之氣，潜傷默耗矣。孕妇服之，大損胎元。」 — only where original qi is not yet depleted and pathogenic qi is still strong; where the Spleen and Stomach are weak, do not let it touch the lips, because the damage is silent and cumulative; taken in PREGNANCY it gravely injures the foetal base. Incompatibilities, BCGM 1596 and Zhenglei 1108 agreeing: 「乾薑為之使，惡澤瀉、硝石、寒水石，忌豆，食之動氣」 — dried ginger is its envoy; antagonises Ze Xie, Xiao Shi and Han Shui Shi; avoid BEANS, which stir the qi.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom. 本經 (Sun Xingyan 1799): 中風、傷寒、頭痛、寒熱，驚悸氣，血痹死肌，去三蟲. 名醫別錄 via Zhenglei 1108 and BCGM 1596: 「温中益氣，消痰下氣，療霍亂及腹痛脹滿，胃中冷逆，胸中嘔不止，洩痢淋露，除驚，去留熱心煩滿，厚腸胃。」 甄權: 「治積年冷氣，腹内雷鳴虚吼，宿食不消，去結水，破宿血…大温胃氣，治冷痛。」 王好古: 「主肺氣脹満膨而喘欬」 — the DB's Lung/rebellious-qi pattern is Wang Haogu's, and can be cited as such.

FORMULA DOCTRINE, pre-1900: Wu Yiluo 1757 gives the Ping Wei San rationale in the herb's own entry — 「佐蒼朮爲平胃散，平溼土之太過，以致於中和」 — paired with Cang Zhu it levels an excess of damp earth back to the mean. Note this pairs directly with H276 in the same batch.

SELECTION CRITERION, pre-1900: 「肉濃紫潤、味辛者良」 (Wu Yiluo 1757) and Lei Xiao's 「要紫色味辛者為好」 — thick-fleshed, purple, moist, acrid-tasting bark. The name itself encodes it: BCGM 1596 釋名 「其木質朴而皮厚，味辛烈而色紫赤，故有厚朴、烈、赤諸名」.

results.pre1900_finding: The 本經 head-reading is 辛微溫 (acrid, SLIGHTLY WARM) with 有小毒, and it stayed that way through Zhenglei 1108. Li Shizhen 1596 then explicitly OVERRULES it in the qi-wei register: 「時珍曰當以苦辛平為是」 — it should properly be taken as bitter, acrid, NEUTRAL. Both Qing sources follow Li Shizhen (苦辛平). So the stored 'Neutral' is correct and has a named pre-1900 author, but it is Li Shizhen's 1596 correction, not the classical head-reading — and the DB should not present it as the 本經 value.

additions: *** QC CATCH ON THE STORED CITATION, NOT THE TEMPERATURE ***. The DB's primary_text_citation for H280 states Jie Geng is 'recorded as a MIDDLE-GRADE herb'. That is wrong on two independent pre-1900 witnesses. BCGM 1596 卷12上 heads the entry 「{{SK anchor|桔梗}}{{SK notes|本經下品}}」 — LOWER grade. Sun Xingyan 1799 places 桔梗 at offset 62554, inside 卷三·下經 (58834–80219) — LOWER grade. 下品 encodes short-course, symptom-directed use and explicitly NOT prolonged daily use, so this error runs in the most consequential possible direction for a product that recommends daily herbs. Recommend correcting the citation text.

A TOXICITY FLAG THE DB DOES NOT CARRY: 有小毒 (slightly toxic) appears in BOTH Zhenglei 1108 and the BCGM 1596 head-line. It is not a stray reading — it is the 本經 assignment carried forward for five centuries, and Li Shizhen's correction addresses the flavour and qi without removing it from the head-line. Combined with the 下品 grade this materially changes how the herb should be presented.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), three channels: Wu Yiluo 1757 (and Wang Ang 1694 identically): 「色白屬金，入肺（氣分）瀉熱，兼入手少陰心、足陽明胃經」 = white in colour therefore belonging to METAL, entering the LUNG at the qi aspect to drain heat, and additionally Hand Shaoyin (Heart) and Foot Yangming (Stomach).

THE 'BOAT AND OARS' DOCTRINE, confirmed pre-1900 — the DB's 'floats other herbs upward' is a genuine classical claim and can be cited: Wu Yiluo 1757: 「爲諸藥舟楫，載之上浮，能引苦泄峻下之劑，至於至高之分成功。」 — it is the boat and oars of the other medicines, carrying them upward, able to lead even bitter-draining, drastically downward agents to the highest reaches. Wu also answers the obvious objection: 「既上行而又能下氣，何也？肺主氣，肺金清肃，氣自下行耳」.
PREPARATION DOCTRINE: Wu Yiluo 1757: 「去浮皮，泔浸，微炒」 — strip the loose outer skin, steep in rice-washing water, lightly dry-fry.

CONTRAINDICATIONS AND PAIRINGS, from BCGM 1596: 「之才曰節皮為之使，畏白及、龍膽草，忌豬肉。得牡礪、逺志療恚怒；得消石、石膏療傷寒；白粥解其毒。」 — fears Bai Ji and Long Dan Cao; avoid PORK; white rice congee is the antidote to its toxicity. Zhenglei 1108 gives the same set with a variant: 「畏白及、龍眼、龍膽」. Li Shizhen adds 「伏砒」 (it subdues arsenic).

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom. 本經 (Sun Xingyan 1799): 胸脅痛如刀刺，腹滿，腸鳴幽幽，驚恐悸氣 — note the 本經 indication set is about CHEST-AND-FLANK PAIN and fright-palpitation, not cough. 名醫別錄 supplies the throat and Lung material: 「利五臓腸胃，補血氣，除寒熱風痺，温中消穀，療喉咽痛，下蠱毒。」 Wu Yiluo 1757 organises the modern-looking picture with the mechanism attached to each: 痰壅喘促、鼻塞（肺氣不利）、目赤、喉痹咽痛（两少陰火）、齒痛（陽明風熱）、口瘡、肺痈乾咳（火郁在肺）、胸膈刺痛（火郁上焦）、腹痛腸鸣（肺火郁於大腸）.

SPECIES TRAP, flagged by Li Shizhen himself and worth recording: BCGM 1596 釋名 warns that the 本經 entry for 桔梗 carried 薺苨 (Adenophora, a DIFFERENT genus) as an alias — 「本經桔梗一名薺苨，而今俗呼薺苨為甜桔梗也。至别録始出薺苨條，分為二物，然其性味功用皆不同，當以别録為是。」 So the 本經 head-reading (the 辛微溫 the DB would otherwise inherit) was written against a name that covered two plants, and Li Shizhen says the 別錄's separation is the correct one. This is independent grounds for not treating the 本經 value as binding on Platycodon grandiflorus.

results.pre1900_finding: 溫 (WARM) in every pre-1900 witness without exception — 苦溫 in the Sun Xingyan recension of the 本經, 甘辛溫 in Zhenglei 1108, 甘溫 in BCGM 1596, 辛苦性溫 in 1694, 辛甘微溫 in 1757. *** PREPARATION DOCTRINE, absent from the DB and unusually specific ***. Lei Xiao, BCGM 1596, under the heading 根皮修治: 「凡采得根，日乾，以銅刀劈破去骨，剉如大豆許，用酒細拌蒸，從巳至未，日乾用。」 — sun-dry the root; split it with a COPPER knife (not iron); discard the woody core ('bone'); chop to soybean size; mix thoroughly with WINE and steam from the si hour to the wei hour (roughly 9am to 3pm); sun-dry. Wu Yiluo 1757: 「肉濃者佳。酒拌蒸用。」 The DB's part_used correctly says root bark; the classical instruction to remove the 骨 is the operative step that produces it.

SELECTION DOCTRINE, with a stated functional split: Wu Yiluo 1757: 「单瓣花红者入藥。（時珍曰：花白者補，赤者利，須分别之。）」 — only the SINGLE-PETALLED RED-flowered plant enters medicine; and per Li Shizhen the white-flowered supplements while the red drains, so the two must be kept distinct. This is a cultivar-level distinction the DB has no field for.

Wu Yiluo 1757 adds the pattern-level and obstetric restrictions: 「胃氣虚寒、經行過期不净者勿服。胎前亦宜酌用。」 — do not give where Stomach qi is deficient and cold, or where menses run past term without clearing; and use judiciously in pregnancy. The 吳普 register in Sun Xingyan 1799 also preserves a minority TOXICITY reading: 「黃帝：苦，有毒」.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom. 本經 (Sun Xingyan 1799): 寒熱，中風瘛瘲、痙，驚癇邪氣；除癥堅瘀血留舍腸胃；安五臟；療癰瘡. 名醫別錄 via BCGM 1596: 「除時氣頭痛，客熱五勞，勞氣頭腰痛，風噤癩疾。」 吳普: 「久服輕身益壽。」 甄權: 「治冷氣，散諸痛，女子經脈不通，血瀝腰痛。」 大明: 「通關腠血脉，排膿，消撲損瘀血，續筋骨，除風痺。」

THE DAN PI / DI GU PI STEAMING-BONE DISTINCTION, pre-1900: Zhang Yuansu via Wu Yiluo 1757: 「丹皮治無汗之骨蒸，地骨皮治有汗之骨蒸」 — Mu Dan Pi for steaming-bone WITHOUT sweating, Di Gu Pi for steaming-bone WITH sweating. The DB's 'night fever without sweating' is Zhang Yuansu's distinction and can now be cited to a pre-1900 source.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经): not stated for 栝樓 in the BCGM entry. Wu Yiluo, 本草從新, 1757, 栝蔞仁: 「甘補肺。苦寒潤下。能清上焦之火。使痰氣下降。爲治嗽要藥。」 — function is placed in Lung and upper burner. CAUTION: this Wikisource transcription of BCCX is mixed simplified/traditional, so treat it as locate-only, not quotable as the 1757 text.

CONTRAINDICATIONS / INCOMPATIBILITIES (classical, root): 之才曰枸杞為之使　惡乾薑　畏牛膝乾漆　反烏頭 (BCGM 1596) — Xu Zhicai: gouqi is its envoy; it hates dried ginger; it fears niuxi and dried lacquer; it OPPOSES aconite (烏頭). That last is one of the Eighteen Antagonisms (十八反), a hard classical incompatibility that belongs on any monograph and is absent from the stored row.

CONTRAINDICATIONS (seed, 1757): 「寒胃滑腸。胃虚食少。脾虚泄瀉。勿投。」 — it chills the stomach and makes the bowel slippery; do not give where the stomach is deficient with poor appetite, or in spleen-deficient diarrhoea. Tian Hua Fen: 「脾胃虚寒者。均宜戒用。」 (Wu Yiluo 1757, locate-only transcription).

PREPARATION DOCTRINE (BCGM 1596, 實修治): 「斆曰凡使皮子莖根其效各别其栝圓黄皮厚蒂小樓則形長赤皮蒂粗隂人服樓陽人服栝並去殻皮革膜及油用」 — Lei Xiao: peel, seed, stem and root each have DIFFERENT effects; the round yellow thick-skinned 'gua' and the long red 'lou' are distinguished, yin-type persons take 'lou' and yang-type persons take 'gua'; in all cases remove the shell, skin, membrane and OIL before use. Li Shizhen adds 「栝樓古方全用後世乃分子瓤各用」 — ancient formulas used the whole fruit; later ages separated seed and pulp. Root: 「秋冬采根去皮寸切水浸逐日換水四五日取出搗泥以絹衣濾汁澄粉晒乾用」 — a four-to-five-day repeated water maceration and starch settling, not a simple decoction.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom (BCGM 1596): fruit — 胸痺 (chest painful obstruction), 悦澤人面 (別錄), 潤肺燥降火, 滌痰結, 利咽喉, 止消渴, 利大腸, 消癰腫瘡毒 (時珍); seed 炒用 — 補虚勞口乾, 潤心肺, 治吐血, 腸風瀉血, 赤白痢 (大明). Root — 消渴身熱煩滿大熱, 補虛安中, 續絕傷 (本經); 除腸胃中痼熱, 八疸, 身面黄, 唇乾口燥, 短氣, 通月水 (別錄).

SPECIES NOTE: pre-1900 texts use no Linnaean name. BCGM's botanical description 「其實圓長青時如瓜黄時如熟柿…内有扁子大如絲瓜子殻色褐仁色綠多脂」 is consistent with the drug now called T. kirilowii, but the identification is a modern overlay on the classical name 栝樓, not something the 1596 text asserts.

URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E6%9C%AC%E8%8D%89%E7%B6%B1%E7%9B%AE_(%E5%9B%9B%E5%BA%AB%E5%85%A8%E6%9B%B8%E6%9C%AC)/%E5%8D%B719 . Shennong Bencao Jing 神農本草經, Sun Xingyan 孫星衍 & Sun Fengyi recension, 1799: 「==澤瀉== 味甘，寒。主風寒濕痹，乳難。消水，養五臟，益氣力，肥健。久服，耳目聰明，不飢、延[年]、輕身，面生光，能行水上。一名水瀉，一名芒芋，一名鵠瀉。生池澤。」 URL: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E7%A5%9E%E8%BE%B2%E6%9C%AC%E8%8D%89%E7%B6%93_(%E5%AD%AB%E6%98%9F%E8%A1%8D)
additions: SHENNONG GRADE: 上品 — UPPER grade. Stated twice: the BCGM head note reads 「澤瀉{{SK notes|本經上品}}」 (1596), and Ze Xie appears in the 草木上品 roster of the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension (…薏苡仁　澤瀉　遠志…). Upper grade encodes intended long-term/daily use — and the 1799 text explicitly says 久服 ("with long use") 耳目聰明，不飢，延年，輕身. But see the contraindication below, which cuts directly against that.

CHANNEL ENTRY (归经), verbatim from BCGM 1596: 「好古曰隂中微陽入足太陽少隂經」 — Wang Haogu: within yin there is slight yang; it enters the foot Taiyang (Bladder) and foot Shaoyin (Kidney) channels. This is a genuine pre-1900 channel assignment and the database has no column for it.

CONTRAINDICATION, and it is a strong one: 「扁鵲曰多服病人眼」 (BCGM 1596) — Bian Que: taking much of it sickens the person's EYES. This sits in direct tension with the upper-grade / 久服 framing and must be surfaced on any product that recommends the herb daily. INCOMPATIBILITY: 「之才曰畏海蛤文蛤」 — Xu Zhicai: it fears haige and wenge (clam shells).

CONTESTED TEMPERATURE, do not collapse it: 本經/BCGM head reading 甘寒 (sweet, cold); 名醫別錄 gives the taste as 鹹 (salty); 甄權 gives 苦 (bitter); 張元素 gives 甘平 (sweet, NEUTRAL) — a genuine named 12th-century dissent from 'cold'; 李杲 gives 甘鹹寒. Four readings, two temperatures.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE (BCGM 1596, 根修治): 「斆曰不計多少細剉酒浸一宿取出暴乾任用」 — Lei Xiao: however much you use, cut it fine, steep in WINE overnight, then take it out and sun-dry before use. Wine-processing is doctrine here, not optional.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the source's own idiom: 本經 (via 1799 recension) — 風寒濕痺, 乳難 (difficult lactation), 消水, 養五臟, 益氣力, 肥健, and with long use 耳目聰明, 能行水上. 別錄 — 補虚損五臟痞滿, 起隂氣, 止洩精, 消渴, 淋瀝, 逐膀胱三焦停水. 甄權 — 主腎虛精自出, 治五淋, 宣通水道. 大明 — 主頭旋耳虛鳴, 通小腸, 止尿血, 主難産, 補女人血海令人有子. 李杲 — 入腎經, 去舊水養新水, 利小便, 消腫脹, 滲洩止渴.

MOISTURE COLUMN WARNING: the stored moisture 'Dry' is not supported by any thermal-or-quality statement in these texts. What the sources give is an ACTION — 消水, 逐膀胱三焦停水, 行水 (drains standing water). Under this project's own rule that an action word is not an energetic assignment, 'Dry' here is an inference from function, not a classical attribute.

SPECIES NOTE: the classical name 澤瀉 is not resolvable to Alisma orientale vs A. plantago-aquatica from any pre-1900 text; the 1596 集解 describes 「叢生淺水中葉狹而長…葉似牛舌獨莖而長秋時開白花」 without a species distinction.

results.pre1900_finding: The classical Sanskrit assignment is USHNA — HOT, not cool. Raja Nighantu 5.202: 「तिक्ता दारुहरिद्रा तु कटूष्णा व्रणमेहनुत्」 — Daruharidra is bitter, PUNGENT-AND-HOT (katu-ushna). Bhavaprakasha Nighantu 2.202 assigns it by reference: 「दार्वी निशागुणा किन्तु नेत्रकर्णास्यरोगनुत्」 (Darvi has the qualities of nisha/turmeric, but additionally cures eye, ear and mouth disease), and nisha/haridra is defined two verses earlier at 2.197 as 「हरिद्रा कटुका तिक्ता रूक्षोष्णा कफपित्तनुत्」 — dry and HOT. The extract Rasanjana is likewise 「उष्णं रसायनं तिक्तं छेदनं व्रणदोषहृत्」 (BPN 2.205) — hot. The stored 'Cool' does have a pre-1900 witness, but it is the Unani/bazaar reckoning, not the Ayurvedic one.
results.source_year: c. 1300 (Raja Nighantu) and 16th century (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu), both read in Devanagari original; opposing reading from Dymock, Pharmacographia Indica Vol. I, 1890
results.evidence: Narahari नरहरि, राजनिघण्टुः, पिप्पल्यादिवर्गः 5.202 (c. 13th century; Devanagari original, sa.wikisource): 「तिक्ता दारुहरिद्रा तु कटूष्णा व्रणमेहनुत् । कण्डूविसर्पत्वग्दोषविषकर्णाक्षिदोषहा ॥ ५.२०२」 URL: https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%98%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9F%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%83/%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A6%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83 . Bhavamishra भावमिश्र, भावप्रकाशनिघण्टुः, हरीतक्यादिवर्ग 2.197 and 2.202-205 (16th century; Devanagari original, sa.wikisource): 「हरिद्रा कटुका तिक्ता रूक्षोष्णा कफपित्तनुत् ॥१९७」 … 「दार्वी निशागुणा किन्तु नेत्रकर्णास्यरोगनुत् ॥२०२」 … 「दार्वीक्वाथसमं क्षीरं पादं पक्त्वा यदा घनम् । तदा रसाञ्जनाख्यं तन्नेत्रयोः परमं हितम् ॥२०३」 … 「रसाञ्जनं कटु श्लेष्मविषनेत्रविकारनुत् ॥२०४ उष्णं रसायनं तिक्तं छेदनं व्रणदोषहृत् ॥२०५」 URL: https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A4%83/%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%82%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%96%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%87_%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B6%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%98%E0%A4%A3%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9F%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%83 . THE OPPOSING PRE-1900 WITNESS, quoted so it is not buried — William Dymock, C. J. H. Warden and David Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica, Vol. I, entry BERBERIS ARISTATA, DC., 1890, p. 66: "In the bazaars the stem, extract and fruit are always obtainable; the two first are considered cold and dry, and are prescribed in combination with other bitters and aromatics, as tonics and antiperiodics" and "The fruit is cooling and acid." URL: https://archive.org/download/b21960343_0001/b21960343_0001_djvu.txt . English glosses of the Sanskrit are my own working renderings; I did not rely on any modern published translation.
additions: THE TWO TRADITIONS DISAGREE HEAD-ON AND MUST BOTH BE CARRIED. Ayurvedic (Raja Nighantu c.1300, Bhavaprakasha 16th c.): USHNA, hot. Unani/bazaar as recorded by Dymock 1890: "cold and dry". The stored 'Cool, Dry' matches Dymock and contradicts both Sanskrit nighantus. This needs a founder decision on which stream the database represents, exactly like the 枸杞子 case already flagged in project memory.
VIPAKA: not stated for Darvi in either nighantu. Do not fill this in. What IS stated for the parent drug haridra (BPN 2.197) is rasa katu + tikta and guna ruksha-ushna.
GUNA: रूक्ष (ruksha, DRY) — inherited from haridra via BPN 2.202's 'nisha-guna' formula. This is the one point where the stored row and the Sanskrit sources agree: dry is correct, cool is not.

PREPARATION DOCTRINE, stated as a recipe in the original (BPN 2.203): 「दार्वीक्वाथसमं क्षीरं पादं पक्त्वा यदा घनम् । तदा रसाञ्जनाख्यं तन्नेत्रयोः परमं हितम्」 — equal parts Darvi decoction and MILK, boiled down to one quarter until thick, is what is called Rasanjana, and it is supremely beneficial for the eyes. Independently corroborated in English by Dymock 1890: "Hakim Abd-el-Hamid describes its manufacture from the powdered wood by exhaustion with water, filtration, and admixture with an equal bulk of cow's milk, the mixture being finally evaporated to the consistence of an extract" — and Dymock adds "this method of preparation is the same as that described in Sanskrit works." U. C. Dutt, The Materia Medica of the Hindus, 1877, p. 107, gives the same: the extract "is directed to be prepared by boiling together equal parts of a decoction of Indian barberry and milk, till reduced to the consistence of an extract." So the milk decoction is not optional flourish; it is the defining preparation, and the database's part_used field is right to name it.

GRADE-EQUIVALENT: the extract Rasanjana is classed रसायनम् (rasayana) at BPN 2.205 — the Ayurvedic analogue of upper-grade, i.e. suitable for sustained rejuvenative use, in contrast to the root's sharper action.

CLASSICAL INDICATIONS in the sources' own idiom: RN 5.202 — व्रण (wounds), मेह (prameha/urinary-diabetic disorders), कण्डू (itch), विसर्प (erysipelas), त्वग्दोष (skin disorders), विष (poison), कर्ण-अक्षि-दोष (ear and eye disorders). BPN 2.202 — नेत्र-कर्ण-आस्य-रोग (eye, ear and MOUTH disease), the specific addition that distinguishes Darvi from turmeric. Rasanjana, BPN 2.204-205 — श्लेष्म, विष, नेत्रविकार, छेदन (scraping/cutting action), व्रणदोष. Dutt 1877 adds the Indian clinical uses: skin disease, menorrhagia, diarrhoea, jaundice, "and above all, in affections of the eyes", and names the compound formulas Rasanjanadi churna and Darvyadi kvatha.

SPECIES NOTE: Dymock's 1890 entry is headed BERBERIS ARISTATA, DC. but treats B. lycium and B. asiatica under the same article; Dutt 1877 heads his entry "BERBERIS ASIATICA AND OTHER SPECIES". No pre-1900 source isolates B. aristata. Also relevant to this project's Chinese work: F. Porter Smith 1871 called the 枸杞/地骨皮 drug 'Berberis Lycium' — do not let that stray determination cross-contaminate this monograph.
